jobs.excerpt: As a T&T| CBRE Construction Project Manager you will be responsible for providing consulting services to an assigned market or client account to help achieve the company's strategic business objectives.
jobs.description:
As a T&T| CBRE Construction Project Manager you will be responsible for providing consulting services to an assigned market or client account to help achieve the company's strategic business objectives.

This is a remote role for someone in the Pacific Time Zone. We are looking for a construction project manager to support our financial retail banking client on their projects. This person will support a large volume on projects consisting of HVAC, roofing, and parking lot upgrades, etc. There is no travel required for this role.

What You’ll Do:

  • Manage all areas of project management for singular real estate projects. This includes planning, design, construction, occupancy, and closeout.
  • Work directly with clients to prepare all elements of the project. This includes the scope of work, project delivery resource requirements, cost estimates & budget, work plan schedule & milestones, quality control, and risk identification.
  • Define the project delivery resources from pre-qualified lists or through the project qualification process. Conduct a standard request for proposals, complete bid evaluations, and recommend resources to clients.
  • Implement project documentation governance that is aligned with company and client requirements.
  • Ensure project data integrity and documentation is accurate, timely, and coordinated.
  • Direct the project delivery team by providing guidance and direction to achieve goals.
  • Create action plans to meet objectives, budget, and schedule. Track the progress of each project and report status and variances.
  • Demonstrate ability to identify project threats and develop risk mitigation and contingency plans. Implement action plans to reduce or eliminate project risks.
  • Apply in-depth knowledge of standard principles and techniques/procedures to accomplish complex assignments and provide innovative solutions.
  • Coach others and share in-depth knowledge of own job discipline and broad knowledge of several job disciplines within the function.
  • Impact a range of customer, operational, project, or service activities within own team and other related teams
  • Work within broad guidelines and policies.

Explain difficult or sensitive information

  • Bachelor's Degree preferred with 5-8 years of relevant experience. In lieu of a degree, a combination of experience and education will be considered. LEED AP, PMP, and/or CCM designation(s) preferred.
  • Ability to exercise judgment based on the analysis of multiple sources of information.
  • Willingness to take a new perspective on existing solutions.
  • In-depth knowledge of Microsoft Office products. Examples include Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.
  • Organizational skills with an advanced inquisitive mindset.
  • Sophisticated math skills. Ability to calculate mildly complex figures such as percentages, fractions, and other financial-related calculations.

*SOX control responsibilities may be part of this role, which are to be adhered to where applicable.

*On-site presence and requirements may change depending on our client's needs*

jobs.title: Controller - Business Unit
jobs.excerpt: Covetrus is a global animal-health technology and services leader dedicated to empowering veterinary practice partners to drive improved health and financial outcomes.
jobs.description:
Covetrus is a global animal-health technology and services leader dedicated to empowering veterinary practice partners to drive improved health and financial outcomes. We bring together products, services, and technology into a single platform that connects our customers to the solutions and insights they need to work best. Our passion for the well-being of animals and those who care for them drives us to advance the world of veterinary medicine.



The Business Unit Controller is responsible for the oversight of the accounting, financial reporting, and control environment of Covetrus North America’s largest business unit. The MWI Controller will leverage their accounting expertise in revenue recognition, inventory management and other complex areas such as software development, property accounting, internal controls, process implementation and operational oversight.


The Controller will have an in-depth knowledge of US GAAP and will have the ability to apply standard principles, theories, concepts and techniques as well as make complex decisions. As a core leader of the Controllership team, this role is responsible for inspiring the team, peers, and leadership, and building an effective and engaged team while supporting their development.

This position reports to the North America Controller and manages a team of accounting professionals.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

  • Direct the functional areas within revenue recognition, inventory control, general accounting, and compliance through partnership with various areas of operations, FP&A and shared services.
  • Ensure compliance with GAAP and other regulatory and/or internally developed accounting policies and procedures.
  • Oversee monthly accounting close process including analytical review of the monthly results to ensure accurate accounting records are maintained.
  • Serve as the point of contact and owner of key controls that include, but not limited to: record to report, procure to pay, order to cash, leasing, inventory, and fixed assets.
  • Be attuned to early warnings of financial control gaps and be able to proactively implement action plans to swiftly remedy.
  • Understand and manage multiple different income streams including product, manufacturing, fees, subscription, software, royalty, consulting, bundling, rebates and margin reimbursements.
  • Provide thought leadership to the business on revenue building initiatives while ensuring compliance with revenue recognition (ASC 606)
  • Comfortable creating or re-evaluating current policies and memos around reserves and impairment analyses that can vary across subsidiaries.
  • Oversight of all intercompany transactions and allocation methodologies.
  • Oversight of all physical inventories and material cycle count adjustments and ensure compliance based on established controls.
  • Implement, document and maintain adequate and effective processes to improve and shorten the monthly accounting close.
  • Issue timely and complete month-end reports and analytics to the consolidation team.
  • Serve as the point of contact for all internal and external audits.
  • Provide counsel and advice to management in developing objectives, strategies and tactics from a financial and accounting perspective.
  • Encourage ideas and creative approaches for continuous improvement.
  • Establish a clear understanding of other functional areas of company and provide guidance to executives of Business Development, Operations, Quality, HR, Program Management, Product, and Development in relation to financial goals and strategies.
  • Keep up to date on the animal health market and applicable accounting rules and regulations.
  • Provide training and guidance to finance staff and non-financial colleagues across the business.
  • Mentor/develop direct reports and retain/promote top performers.

QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLSETS

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance
  • CPA Required, MBA a plus
  • 8+ years of diverse financial experience in various finance / accounting roles
  • 3+ years in a hands-on management position
  • Strength of character, with the ability to take clear, decisive action in steering the company's worth and safeguard values
  • A history of active involvement and success beyond the traditional responsibilities of financial reporting
  • Experience integrating an accounting function as part of a business combination
  • Works effectively in a fast-paced environment with multiple competing deadlines
  • Possess agility and can adapt quickly to changing priorities
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
  • Strong work ethic with willingness and ability to dig into details to accomplish tasks and complete projects


We offer the following benefits for you to take advantage of while you are here provided you meet the eligibility requirements under each governing program:

  • 401k savings & company match

  • Paid time off

  • Health, dental, and vision benefits

jobs.description:
Discover Vanderbilt Health: With eight hospitals and over 180 clinics, we are the region’s largest comprehensive academic health system. .

Monday - Friday

Days

jobs.title: Analytics Engineer, Finance and Modeling
jobs.excerpt: At In Tandem, we build technology that helps families manage everyday routines and navigate life’s biggest transitions.
jobs.description:
At In Tandem, we build technology that helps families manage everyday routines and navigate life’s biggest transitions. Through our four brands—OurFamilyWizard, Cozi, FamilyWall, and Custody Navigator—we help families stay organized, communicate well, and foster healthy childhoods.
We believe technology should strengthen relationships and make daily coordination less complicated. Everything we create is designed to lighten the mental load, reduce conflict, and support families through big and small moments.
If you want your work to make a real difference in the daily lives of parents and kids, In Tandem is the place where your impact will truly matter.

As an Analytics Engineer (Finance & Modeling), you'll own the metrics, reporting and reconciliation our financial decisions rest on, turning subscription and transaction data across OurFamilyWizard, Cozi, FamilyWall and Custody Navigator into numbers the business can defend. As that foundation becomes automatic, the work shifts toward forecasting and modeling.

You won't start from scratch. Our dbt project is live on Databricks with a star-schema finance mart in production and documented in Unity Catalog. What's missing is the layer on top, and that layer is yours. We also run an internal AI agent that answers business questions in Slack off the semantic layer, so every metric you define and test becomes a question Finance can ask directly rather than queue.

What you'll accomplish:

  • Governed metrics. Add the definitions the finance mart doesn't have yet (ARR, renewal rate, churn, CAC), versioned in dbt and documented in Unity Catalog, with the tests that make each one defensible, and wired into the agent so Finance can ask them directly.
  • Reporting Finance can run without you. Move the recurring finance pack into marimo, retire the Tableau views behind it, and turn a monthly hand-build into something that runs on a schedule.
  • Numbers that reconcile. Reconcile transactions across the app stores, payment processors, subscription systems and the ledger, with automated checks that alert rather than surface at close. Route discrepancies upstream with the evidence attached and turn each one into a test. You build the checks and escalate. Accounting owns the treatment.
  • Forecasting for Finance. Cohort subscriber and revenue projection, and aggregate renewal and retention forecasting, feeding the CFO's forecast and board reporting. LTV by acquisition source, feeding paid spend allocation with Growth. Pricing and promo impact, modeled before we ship rather than measured after. Individual churn propensity and uplift follow once there's a retention motion ready to act on the scores.
  • Models ship as scored tables in dbt and Unity Catalog, with tests, lineage and a definition the agent can answer from. Not as notebooks.

Who you are:

  • Statistically rigorous. You know why a cohort curve is the wrong shape, what a model is leaking, and when a result is noise.
  • Fluent in finance, and unwilling to let a number you can't explain go out the door. When two systems disagree, you find out why and tell the people upstream.
  • An engineer who owns the number end to end, from a CFO's question through the model, the test, the report and the conversation that follows. A spreadsheet nobody can reproduce reads to you as a liability.
  • AI-proficient in practice, not in theory. Claude Code, coding agents and agent SDKs are part of our daily loop, and we expect you to already work this way. A lot of what used to be a week of modeling work is now an afternoon, and we're hiring for people who have internalized that.
  • Willing to wear several hats. This is a small team supporting four brands. Some weeks you're deep in a retention model, some weeks you're chasing an app store discrepancy or unblocking someone else's dashboard. The scope above is the center of the role, not a fence around it.
  • Motivated by work that matters. Families rely on these products during real moments in their lives.

What you bring:

  • 3+ years in analytics engineering, data science, BI engineering or advanced analytics.
  • Statistical modeling shipped into a business process: forecasting, survival or cohort analysis, or propensity.
  • Measuring the lift from a price change or a growth experiment. You don't need to have designed the test, but you need to be able to read the result honestly and say what it's worth.
  • Subscription metrics you've built and defended to a finance stakeholder: ARR/MRR, renewal, churn, LTV/CAC, or cohort revenue.
  • Strong SQL and real dimensional modeling. You've designed marts, not just queried them.
  • Python and Git as daily habits.
Nice to have, not a dealbreaker:
  • dbt, Databricks and Unity Catalog, or a comparable lakehouse.
  • Reconciling transactional data to a financial system of record.
  • Code-first notebook reporting (marimo, Hex, Streamlit, Quarto).

jobs.excerpt: OverviewThe Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc.
jobs.description:
Overview

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.

CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic, with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.

At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work:

CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.

Global Markets Team Overview

The CHAI Global Markets Team (GMT) strives to build healthier marketplaces to ensure the sustainable supply of vital medical commodities. In particular, the GMT is responsible for designing, negotiating, and supporting the effective implementation of market-shaping interventions that can increase access to critical health commodities in LMICs. Example market-shaping interventions range from traditional policy-led and grant-financed initiatives such as pooled procurement, coordinated ordering, and strategic demand forecasting to more innovative mechanisms such as volume guarantees (VGs), advance market commitments (AMCs), and working capital facilities. Example market shaping efforts that CHAI has been involved with include the following:

  • Kenya is granted special Caffeine Citrate pricing after Clinton Health Access Initiative led negotiations with Ethypharm – Health Business
  • CHAI and The Hepatitis Fund announce pricing breakthrough to reduce cost of viral hepatitis treatment by over 90 percent
  • New agreement secures historic US$1 price for HIV self-test
  • Global partnership to make available 120M affordable, quality COVID-19 rapid tests for low- and middle-income countries
  • Price reduction agreement for contraceptive implants increased distribution by >50% and will save more than US$300M

The GMT collaborates with internal and external stakeholders on both the supply- and demand-sides of the market to assess the potential public-health impact of proposed market-shaping interventions. The GMT also plays a leading role within CHAI in terms of managing relationships with branded and generic pharmaceutical and diagnostics companies.

Within the GMT, the Women’s and New Born Health (WNH) team is composed of individuals who are passionate about increasing access to quality and affordable WNH products in LMICs and ensuring there is a secure and sustainable supply. The GMT WNH team emphasizes professional development and growth for its staff and strives to foster a dynamic and meritocratic team environment. GMT managers will proactively work with the new Associate to ensure they feel both continually supported and challenged at work.

Position Overview

This Associate will support GMT’s WNH market shaping activities by driving forward the analytical work required to thoughtfully design and implement strategies to secure sufficient supply of critical commodities for LMICs. They will also collect and analyse data from various sources such as government tenders, shipment data from procurers and manufacturers, demographic data from household surveys, and usage data reported by countries.

The Associate will be responsible for developing rigorous market analyses (e.g., demand forecasts) to support investment decisions by suppliers, country programs, donors, and other key stakeholders. The Associate's work will be critical to inform the GMT’s strategic decisions, such as how to secure appropriate production capacity of affordable, quality-assured WNH commodities to meet forecasted demand or how to support the scale-up of new or underutilized products by addressing key market barriers. Through this role, the Associate will develop collaborative relationships with multiple teams within CHAI as well as with pharmaceutical suppliers and other key leaders within the WNH space.

For this Associate position, we are seeking a highly motivated, entrepreneurial individual with outstanding analytical capabilities, problem-solving skills, and communication abilities. The individual must be comfortable synthesizing large amounts of quantitative and qualitative data into thoughtful recommendations. They must also be able to function independently, balance multiple priorities simultaneously, and work effectively across a range of stakeholders.

This role can also be offered at a Senior Associate level, commensurate with the qualifications and experience of the candidate. Preference is for this role to be based in a CHAI Program Country. This role will require up to 25% travel.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and manage databases, analyses, and frameworks to identify and prioritize market-shaping interventions
  • Conduct landscape assessments and profile manufacturers to identify opportunities to strengthen quality-assured supply for WNH commodities
  • Collaborate with internal and external partners to assess market outlook, supplier landscape, production economics, and procurement trends across a range of products
  • Evaluate cost drivers and inform access pricing strategies and supplier negotiations
  • Track product availability, registration status, and supplier performance across priority markets, coordinating with regulatory and country teams to support product introduction and scale-up
  • Support the design and execution of supply-side interventions (e.g., pooled procurement, regional manufacturing, risk mitigation strategies) to enhance affordability, availability, and sustainability of key commodities
  • Work with CHAI country and global teams to assess feasibility and impact of market-shaping approaches using standardized frameworks and methodologies
  • Synthesize qualitative and quantitative data to develop strategies and generate clear communications materials for internal and external stakeholders
  • Present findings to various audiences, including donors, governments, suppliers, and global partners
  • Maintain effective relationships with senior-level stakeholders across CHAI and partner organizations
  • Execute other responsibilities as needed by the team

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree and 5+ years of analytical or business experience
  • Demonstrated ability to think strategically, handle ambiguity, and work in a fast-paced, multicultural environment
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare compelling presentations and written reports and present effectively to stakeholders, including donors and more senior-level individuals
  • Ability to drive forward assigned workstreams effectively (e.g., through thoughtful work planning, priority setting, stakeholder engagement, etc.)
  • Ability to build collaborative relationship with internal and external stakeholders, including more senior-level individuals
  • High level of proficiency in Microsoft Office (particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word) and R; proficiency in Tableau and Power BI preferred
  • Experience with ownership of workstreams and/or openness to working remotely with a decentralized team
  • Available for 25% travel
  • English language fluency, both written and verbal

At Agiboo we are making lives easier for our customers. Our flagship product, Agiblocks CTRM, is the first Commodity Trade and Risk Management software solution that really simplifies the daily practices of commodity trade professionals. Designed by traders, Agiblocks enables its users to focus on the essence of their trading.

We are a truly diverse and multicultural organisation – with colleagues and customers based across the globe from Europe to Singapore to Brazil and more. Our employees are experts in their field, passionate about what they do and always looking for new and better ways to solve our industry's problems. 

Part of Cultura Technologies and Constellation Software Inc, we have an entrepreneurial spirit with the personal feel of a smaller company, backed by the strength of a larger, global parent company.  Day to day you will be the expert in your field, owning and driving the sales strategy and closing deal. As a small business, life at Agiboo is dynamic, fast-paced and exciting. You will utilise your network, build on existing relationships and attend conferences to build up your sales pipeline. Supporting you will be expertise, knowledge and resources from Cultura and CSI, that can help you be the best that you can be. We are passionate about developing our people, and there are plenty of opportunities to develop your skills, build your knowledge and further your career whether within Agiboo or elsewhere within the Group.

Agiboo is a team bursting with talent, helping make our customers lives easier, it’s a big challenge, are you up for it? 

Job Description:

About the role


Agiblocks is the cloud-based CTRM platform that international agricultural and soft-commodity traders use to run trades, risk, logistics, billing, financial integrations and compliance. Our customers’ operations cannot fail, so high availability, performance and resilience are not features, they are the baseline.

We are looking for a hands-on Software Development Team Lead to run the day-to-day R&D process, provide technical leadership and coordinate the DevOps effort. Working closely with the Product Owner and Business Unit Leader, you will keep the team’s development rhythm effective, participate in technical discussions and help the team make pragmatic delivery and design decisions.

A defining part of this role is changing how we build and test. We are moving to AI-supported, largely automated testing and adopting AI-assisted software development across the team, and we want a leader who will drive that change rather than wait for it.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will remain close enough to the code to review work, troubleshoot issues and contribute directly when this helps the team, while spending most of your time coordinating delivery, facilitating technical decisions and improving how the team works.


What you will own


Modernising how we build and test, a priority for this role


Lead the transition towards substantially more automated testing: expand automated coverage, reduce manual regression effort and use AI-assisted test generation and maintenance where it adds value, so releases can be validated faster and more consistently.

Introduce AI-assisted software development across the team - coding assistants, AI-supported code review, documentation and legacy migration and make it a standing working practice rather than a pilot.

Set the guardrails that keep AI-generated code safe in a mission-critical product: human accountability for every merge, security review, licence and IP hygiene and no erosion of readability or maintainability.

Define and report the measures that prove it is working, delivery cycle time, escaped defects, automated coverage and regression run time.


Team leadership

Lead, mentor and motivate the team across development, QA and DevOps, onshore and offshore.

Drive recruiting, onboarding and performance feedback.

Grow engineers technically through code review, pair programming and design discussion.

Build a collaborative, accountable, results-driven team culture.


Delivery and process

Work with the Product Owner to clarify requirements, estimate work and plan sprints.

Run the team’s day-to-day R&D process: facilitate daily stand-ups, prepare and lead twice-weekly user-story grooming sessions and run biweekly sprint closing and planning meetings.

Coordinate development and DevOps contributions to customer-funded, consulting and implementation projects and report progress against their milestones.

Track and report sprint outcomes and delivery metrics.

Coordinate the software release process and provide cost estimates, or facilitate reliable team estimates, for new work, customer requests and quotations.


Technical ownership

Stay hands-on: write code, review pull requests and debug production issues.

Lead and moderate technical discussions, help the team evaluate options and make or approve day-to-day technical decisions within the agreed product and architecture direction.

Coordinate the DevOps effort for Agiboo-built and deployed applications, align priorities with the DevOps engineers and ensure that hosting, deployment and release needs are addressed. The role sets day-to-day direction and facilitates decisions but is not expected to administer the platform independently.

Troubleshoot product and infrastructure issues and enforce secure, sound engineering practice.

Evaluate and lead modernisation of tools, platforms and integrations (market data, ERP and financial systems).


What you bring — essential

Degree or diploma in Computer Science, Engineering or a comparable technical discipline.

5+ years in professional software development, with solid experience building and maintaining commercial web-based business software.

Experience as a technical lead, senior developer with team coordination responsibilities, or development manager. This may be a first formal people-leadership role for a candidate who has already led technical discussions and delivery activities.

Strong working knowledge of web-based C# and .NET, including traditional .NET and modern .NET; SQL Server and Entity Framework; containerized software hosting and SaaS delivery; and integration with external systems.

A modern UI framework in production: React, Blazor or ASP.NET MVC.

Microsoft Azure and microservices architecture, with enough working knowledge of containerised, cloud-based deployment (Kubernetes) to direct and challenge a DevOps team.

Layered / 3-tier application design, with clean separation of business logic from UI.

Relational and document databases: MS SQL / Azure SQL and MongoDB.

Hands-on Agile/Scrum, CI/CD and test automation practice, with automated tests integrated into the pipeline.

Demonstrated use of AI-assisted development in a working team - coding assistants, AI-supported review or AI-generated tests with a clear view of where it helps and where it does not.


What you bring — preferred

Optimizing cloud applications for high throughput and high availability.

Commodity trading and risk management, or domain knowledge in agriculture, energy or metals.

Delivering in a support-intensive, customer-facing product environment.

Rolling out AI tooling across an engineering team: adoption, standards and guardrails.

Agentic coding tools or AI-assisted test generation platforms in a compliance-sensitive product.

Breadth across a wide array of technologies and integration patterns.


How you work

Hands-on by preference. You would rather unblock a defect than chair a status meeting.

Strong ownership: accountable for what the team ships, not just for the tasks assigned.

Structured and calm under competing priorities and live customer escalations.

Clear communicator with engineers, product, and customers alike.

Pragmatic about AI: you treat it as leverage applied under engineering judgement, not as a substitute for it.

Quality-first and customer-focused


Scope and authority

Manages the development, QA and DevOps team, onshore and offshore.

Owns sprint planning, task allocation and performance feedback.

Makes day-to-day delivery and technical decisions within agreed priorities and architecture guardrails, escalating material product, investment, people or platform decisions to the Business Unit Leader and Product Owner.


Reports to the Business Unit Leader and works closely with the Product Owner.

Job Description

A bit about this role:

Within Member Experience Operations, the Guide Training function prepares Guides to serve our members and keeps them growing throughout their careers at Devoted. That spans new hire onboarding, upskilling into more complex work, role-based training for specialized teams, readiness for each new plan year, and the development that helps Guides move into their next role.

As the Director, you will own this function end to end: its strategy, its operating plan, its budget, its team, and its results. You will build it into three capabilities with clear owners, Learning Design, Training Delivery, and Measurement and Readiness, and lead it through managers. You will be accountable not only for what a Guide can do the day they leave training, but for whether they reach proficiency in their first 90 days.


The population we train grows with the company and concentrates heavily from September through December, and new products and market segments will require capability we do not have yet. This role builds Guide Training into a function that can meet that, and that can prove its effect on member experience with evidence.


Your Responsibilities and Impact will include:

  • Function strategy and operating plan: Own a published operating plan for Guide Training with dated commitments and a defensible point of view on how Guides learn this work: ramp design, modality mix, delivery standards, mentorship, the role of AI-assisted practice, and what the function deliberately does not do. Evolve it as the Guide organization grows and diversifies.
  • Readiness and the first 90 days: Own what a Guide can do when they leave training and through day 90. Set the readiness standard that every population clears before taking member interactions, covering provisioning, systems access, competency verification, defined success measures, and a rollback plan. Hold go/no-go authority on readiness for any population, internal or vendor. Diagnose whether early performance gaps are training gaps, intervene with targeted remediation and practice, and partner with Guide Supervisors on a structured handoff at graduation, equipping Guide leaders to reinforce training on the floor. Set the training and readiness standard that vendor populations must meet.
  • Measurement and continuous improvement: Commit to outcome targets and answer for them: quality and accuracy at 30, 60, and 90 days, speed to proficiency, workflow adherence, escalation rates, learner experience, and early attrition by cohort. Partner with Quality and Workforce Management to build a single measurement approach, review cohort results on a regular cadence, and turn what they show into design changes. Apply the same discipline to the function itself, with a retrospective review of every cohort.
  • Prioritization and intake: Run intake across the Guide organization and cross-functional partners. Translate broad needs into scoped work with owners, effort estimates, dates, and success measures. jobs.description:
About Mainspring

Mainspring Energy manufactures and delivers fuel-flexible, low-emissions local power solutions that rapidly add new capacity and deliver reliable, affordable, and sustainable electric power. The company began commercial shipments of its Mainspring Linear Generators in 2020 and today has hundreds of megawatts in advanced development and field operations for leading Fortune 500 companies, data centers, and utilities. Mainspring also partners with global energy leaders including AEP, NextEra Energy Resources, Schneider Electric, and more.

The core values that ground our work, guide our decisions, and connect us together:

  • Pragmatic Optimism
  • Excellence without Ego
  • Proactive Collaboration

Job Overview

    Project Engineers report to the Project Engineering Manager within the Project Delivery department. A key enabler of Mainspring’s mission is the ability of its team to deliver solutions based on our linear generator technology that solve customer problems in the cross-section of resiliency and clean power supply.

    The project engineering team provides the technical expertise, guidance, and support to deploy linear generators into the field efficiently—building customer confidence and enabling future scalability. This role focuses on our largest deployments: sites of 10MW and above that either connect directly to the grid or serve large load sites such as data centers.

Responsibilities

    This role will be responsible for:

  • Leading the overall technical definition and direction of assigned projects, including site layouts, single-line diagrams, equipment selection, sequences of operation, plant controls, communication, and network security schemes, protection and metering schemes, grounding, code and grid code compliance, fuel systems, and safety systems

  • Serving as the technical integrator across electrical, mechanical, civil, controls, fuel, and utility scopes: providing design coordination, value engineering, and interface reviews so all disciplines come together into one buildable, compliant project, and collaborating with project managers, development, procurement, and other stakeholders within timelines and budgets

  • Providing technical support to the interconnection team: supplying plant data, single-lines, and equipment models for applications, reviewing Feasibility, System Impact, and Facility Studies, and advising on technical terms in interconnection agreements

  • For large-load and data center sites, defining how the plant serves and protects the load, including islanding, load-following, and transfer schemes

  • Guiding selection and specification of medium-voltage and plant interconnection equipment such as switchgear, breakers, transformers, protective relays, revenue meters, reclosers, and PPC/SCADA hardware, plus fuel equipment such as gas regulators and valves; developing specifications, sequences of operation, EPC scopes of work, design standards, and testing procedures; and supporting procurement and proposal requests

  • Working directly with clients & engineering partners to translate project requirements into official plan sets using best practices, QA/QC standards, and due diligence; answering RFIs, approving submittals, and reviewing documents and designs to close gaps in function, performance, scope, and responsibility from initial design through commissioning

  • Approving design variances, independently resolving engineering modifications to maintain design intent and schedules

  • Conducting engineering reviews of site assessments, inspections, and power system studies (load flow, short circuit, coordination, arc flash), and ensuring plant controls and protection settings meet utility, ISO/RTO, IEEE 1547/2800, and applicable NERC/FERC requirements, including ride-through, reactive power, and telemetry

  • Monitoring changes to regional grid codes, utility interconnection handbooks, and IEEE/NERC standards, proactively compiling compliance risks and necessary product adaptations

  • Supporting permitting for large facilities in coordination with development, environmental, and AHJ stakeholders

  • Leading final grid code compliance demonstrations, including NERC/IEEE (1547/2800) model validation and protection relay checkout, and supporting commissioning and energization activities such as witness testing, metering checkout, and utility acceptance testing to secure final Permission to Operate (PTO)

  • Participating in and developing improvement initiatives, using Lean or similar methods, that increase operational efficiency within a rapidly growing project delivery department

  • Documenting execution challenges and creating training materials and instructional documents to better define engineering requirements for future deployments

  • Travelling to project sites at varying stages based on availability

Job Qualifications and Experience

  • B.S. degree in Electrical Engineering or related discipline (power systems emphasis preferred; Mechanical, Systems, Controls, or Mechatronics considered). Technical degree and equivalent experience may be substituted

  • Proven working experience as a project engineer or power systems engineer with 8+ years of relevant experience, including at least 2–5 years in a direct contributing role on grid-scale generation or storage projects utilizing at least some of the following:

  • Solar PV, Central Inverters, Battery Energy Storage Systems (AC- and DC-coupled), Modular Generation Packages, Microturbines, Reciprocating Engines/Gensets, Large Fuel Cells, Cogen/CHP, Plant Controllers/DERMS, Virtual Power Plants

  • Experience with most of the following is essential: project management, medium-voltage (5 kV+) distribution and protection system design, data acquisition and control systems (SCADA/PPC/EMS), understanding of technical drawings & construction plan sets, and electrical system troubleshooting

  • Familiar with construction processes, sequencing, and contractor management for large generation sites

  • Strong grasp of balance-of-plant interfaces, including equipment foundations, structural layouts, fuel/gas delivery systems, and hazardous area requirements, with proven ability to review, cross-reference, and approve multi-disciplinary EPC design packages (single-lines, P&IDs, civil site plans)

  • Familiar with rules, regulations, best practices, and standards for the power generation industry, including NEC, NESC, IEEE (1547, 2800, C37 series), UL 1741, utility interconnection handbooks, regional grid codes, and the proper sizing/installation/use of power system equipment

  • Working knowledge of FERC interconnection requirements and NERC reliability standards as they apply to generation facilities

  • Comprehension of medium-voltage protection functions, utility-grade protective relays (e.g., SEL), revenue metering, and their use in power plant design and at the point of interconnection

  • Ability to interpret and act on power system study results (load flow, short circuit, coordination, arc flash, power quality, dynamic/ride-through), including outputs from ETAP, SKM, CYME, or PSS/E

  • Familiarity with SCADA systems and power plant controllers for voltage regulation and dynamic power control, plus industrial network protocols and devices (e.g., DNP3, Modbus, IEC 61850)

  • Excellent decision making, communication, time management, documentation, and organizational skills. Self-directed, with an ownership mindset and enthusiasm for building processes within a growing team

jobs.description:
Position:Chief Financial Officer (CFO)

About the Role

We are seeking an accomplished and commercially strategic Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead the financial strategy, financial performance, capital management, investment finance, treasury, reporting, and financial governance of a diversified Insurance & Investment organization.

The CFO will serve as a key member of the executive leadership team and strategic advisor to the CEO/President and Board, providing leadership across financial planning, insurance accounting, capital and solvency management, investment portfolio performance, asset-liability management, treasury, risk, regulatory reporting, and corporate development.

The successful candidate will combine deep financial expertise with strong commercial and investment acumen and will be capable of operating in a highly regulated financial-services environment.

Key Responsibilities

1. Financial Strategy & Executive Leadership

Develop and execute the organization's overall financial strategy.

Advise the CEO, President, and Board on financial performance, capital allocation, investment strategy, and enterprise value creation.

Translate corporate strategy into financial plans, budgets, forecasts, and measurable objectives.

Lead financial decision-making across insurance, investment, and corporate operations.

Establish strong financial governance and accountability across the organization.

2. Financial Planning, Budgeting & Performance

Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, and long-term financial planning.

Develop financial models and scenario analyses to support strategic decisions.

Monitor revenue, profitability, expenses, capital efficiency, and operating performance.

Establish financial KPIs and executive dashboards.

Identify opportunities to improve profitability, efficiency, and shareholder returns.

3. Insurance Finance & Performance

Oversee financial management of insurance operations, including premiums, claims, reserves, expenses, and underwriting performance.

Monitor key insurance financial metrics including loss ratios, combined ratios, expense ratios, and underwriting profitability.

Partner with actuarial, underwriting, claims, and risk teams to assess financial performance and emerging exposures.

Ensure appropriate financial treatment and reporting of insurance liabilities and reserves.

Support pricing, product profitability, reinsurance, and portfolio decisions from a financial perspective.

4. Investment Finance & Portfolio Management

Provide financial oversight of the organization's investment portfolio and investment activities.

Partner with the CIO/Chief Investment Officer and Investment Committee on portfolio strategy and performance.

Monitor investment income, realized/unrealized gains, asset allocation, liquidity, and risk-adjusted returns.

Evaluate investment opportunities and strategic asset-allocation decisions.

Ensure investment activities are aligned with the organization's liabilities, liquidity requirements, risk appetite, and regulatory requirements.

5. Capital, Solvency & Balance Sheet Management

Lead capital planning and balance-sheet optimization.

Monitor solvency, capital adequacy, liquidity, leverage, and financial resilience.

Develop strategies to optimize the organization's capital structure and return on capital.

Assess the financial impact of major business, investment, and insurance decisions on capital requirements.

Work closely with Risk and Actuarial functions on capital and solvency assessments.

6. Asset-Liability Management (ALM)

Provide executive financial oversight of asset-liability management.

Ensure investment portfolios are appropriately aligned with insurance liabilities and liquidity requirements.

Monitor duration, interest-rate sensitivity, liquidity gaps, and market exposures.

Support development of ALM strategies and balance-sheet optimization initiatives.

Ensure appropriate financial stress testing and scenario analysis.

7. Treasury & Liquidity

Oversee treasury, cash management, liquidity planning, and banking relationships.

Maintain adequate liquidity to meet claims, operating obligations, investment commitments, and strategic requirements.

Optimize cash deployment and short-term investment strategies.

Monitor interest-rate, foreign-exchange, credit, and liquidity exposures.

Establish robust treasury policies and controls.

8. Regulatory & Financial Reporting

Ensure accurate, timely, and transparent financial reporting to the Board, shareholders, regulators, and other stakeholders.

Oversee statutory accounts, management reporting, regulatory returns, and consolidated financial statements.

Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and insurance regulations.

Lead relationships with external auditors, regulators, actuarial advisers, tax advisers, and other professional stakeholders.

Maintain strong financial controls and governance frameworks.

9. Risk Management & Financial Controls

Establish effective financial risk-management frameworks.

Monitor exposure to market, credit, liquidity, underwriting, operational, interest-rate, and foreign-exchange risks.

Strengthen internal controls, financial policies, and governance processes.

Work closely with the CRO, Chief Actuary, CIO, and other executives to manage enterprise-wide financial risks.

Ensure appropriate stress testing and contingency planning.

10. Reinsurance & Capital Optimization

Provide financial oversight of reinsurance strategy and economics.

Evaluate the financial and capital implications of reinsurance arrangements.

Monitor reinsurance recoverables, counterparty exposure, and profitability.

Support optimization of risk transfer, capital efficiency, and balance-sheet resilience.

11. Corporate Development & Strategic Investments

Lead financial evaluation of acquisitions, strategic investments, joint ventures, and business expansion opportunities.

Oversee financial due diligence, valuation, transaction modeling, and investment cases.

Assess potential M&A opportunities and their impact on capital, solvency, earnings, and shareholder value.

Support negotiations with investors, financial institutions, and strategic partners.

12. Investor & Stakeholder Relations

Develop strong relationships with shareholders, institutional investors, banks, rating agencies, regulators, and other financial stakeholders.

Communicate financial performance, capital strategy, investment results, and business outlook to key stakeholders.

Support investor presentations, Board materials, and strategic financial communications.

13. Finance Transformation & Technology

Modernize finance systems, reporting infrastructure, ERP platforms, and financial analytics.

Improve automation, data quality, forecasting, and management reporting.

Establish real-time visibility into financial, insurance, investment, and risk performance.

Drive continuous improvement within the finance function.

14. Leadership & Talent Development

Lead Finance, FP&A, Treasury, Accounting, Financial Reporting, Tax, and related functions.

Build a high-performing and commercially focused finance organization.

Develop finance leadership talent and succession plans.

Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, financial discipline, and business partnership.

Key Performance Indicators

The CFO will be accountable for:

Revenue and earnings growth

Operating and net profitability

Return on equity (ROE)

Return on capital

Capital adequacy and solvency

Investment portfolio performance

Investment income and risk-adjusted returns

Combined ratio / underwriting profitability

Expense efficiency

Liquidity and cash-flow management

Balance-sheet optimization

Budget and forecast accuracy

Regulatory and financial reporting quality

Cost of capital

Financial risk management

Shareholder value creation

Candidate Profile

Essential Experience

15+ years of progressive finance experience, including significant executive leadership.

Previous experience as CFO, Group CFO, Finance Director, VP Finance, Deputy CFO, or equivalent.

Significant experience within insurance, asset management, investment management, banking, pensions, financial services, or a related regulated financial institution.

Strong understanding of insurance financial statements, investment portfolios, capital management, and regulatory requirements.

Proven experience managing complex balance sheets, liquidity, capital, and financial performance.

Strong experience working with Boards, regulators, auditors, investors, rating agencies, and senior executives.

Demonstrated experience in financial strategy, investment analysis, and capital allocation.

Preferred Experience

Experience as Group CFO within a diversified insurance or financial-services group.

Experience across both insurance and investment/asset-management businesses.

Experience with life insurance, general insurance, health insurance, pensions, or reinsurance.

Exposure to institutional investment portfolios and alternative investments.

Experience with M&A, strategic investments, capital raising, restructuring, or corporate transformation.

Experience operating across multiple jurisdictions or regulated markets.

Experience interacting with insurance regulators and rating agencies.

Education & Professional Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

Professional qualification such as CA, ACCA, CPA, CMA, CFA, or equivalent strongly preferred.

MBA or Master's degree in Finance/Business is an advantage.

Relevant insurance, actuarial, investment, or risk-management qualifications are advantageous.

Core Competencies

Insurance Finance

Corporate Finance

Investment Finance

Capital & Solvency Management

Asset-Liability Management

Treasury & Liquidity

Financial Planning & Analysis

Investment Analysis

Financial Modeling

Risk Management

Regulatory Reporting

Insurance Accounting

M&A & Corporate Development

Capital Allocation

Investor Relations

Corporate Governance

Financial Transformation

Leadership Characteristics

The successful CFO will be:

Strategic, commercially minded, and financially rigorous

Highly analytical and investment-oriented

Experienced in highly regulated environments

Strong in capital and balance-sheet management

Comfortable engaging with Boards, regulators, investors, and rating agencies

Able to balance growth, profitability, liquidity, capital, and risk

An effective strategic partner to the CEO, CIO, CRO, and Chief Actuary

Strong in complex financial decision-making

A transformational finance leader capable of building high-performing teams

Compensation

A competitive executive compensation package comprising base salary, performance-based incentives, executive benefits, and other benefits commensurate with experience and market benchmarks.

Club Caddie is a fast-growing golf course management software (GMS) company and a member of the Jonas Software family, a division of Constellation Software Inc. (TSX: CSU). Our platform is the operating system for golf, unifying point of sale, tee sheet, member management, food and beverage, and payments into a single connected system for public, semi-private, and multi-course operators.

We are built by operators, for operators, and our brand is anchored in four commitments: Unified Operations, Intelligent Action, Revenue Momentum, and Hospitality Memory. Our mission is to expand Jonas' reputation and market share with public, semi-private, and single-course operators (SCOs), and we're investing in field sales talent that knows these courses inside and out.


THE ROLE

The Sales Manager owns and grows a defined regional territory by winning new single-course operator (SCO) customers. This is a hunting and consultative selling role for a seasoned golf industry professional who knows course operations, understands GMS technology, and can guide owners and general managers from first conversation to signed agreement.

You will report directly to the Vice President of Sales (SCO) and work in close partnership with Marketing, Product, Implementation, and Customer Success to build a healthy territory pipeline, tailor your strategy to regional market dynamics, and deliver a clean handoff to onboarding for every new customer.

The Salary range for this role is between $70,000 - $75,000 USD


WHAT YOU'LL DO


Own and Grow Your Regional Territory

  • Build and execute a territory plan that targets high-value SCO opportunities, tailored to the market dynamics of your region.
  • Maintain a strong, consistent pipeline from lead generation through close, with steady activity at every stage.
  • Use deep industry expertise to tailor Club Caddie's value proposition to each course's operation and goals.

Lead the Full Sales Cycle

  • Own the end-to-end process: prospecting, discovery, presentations, demos, negotiation, and contract execution.
  • Present Club Caddie's platform with a high level of technical and operational credibility.
  • Meet or exceed territory quotas and revenue targets.

Build Industry Relationships

  • Develop long-term, trust-based relationships with course owners, general managers, and industry influencers.
  • Represent Club Caddie at industry events, trade shows, and regional gatherings to build pipeline and brand presence.
  • Act as a trusted advisor and ambassador, positioning Club Caddie as the premier GMS for single-course operators.

Win Against the Competition

  • Negotiate and close deals with a clear, defensible value narrative, maximizing revenue per customer.
  • Compete effectively against incumbent point-of-sale and tee sheet providers.

Drive Cross-Functional Alignment

  • Partner with Marketing on territory-specific campaigns and lead-generation efforts.
  • Share market feedback with Sales Leadership, Product, and Marketing to refine go-to-market strategy and competitive positioning.
  • Ensure a clean, well-documented handoff from sales to implementation, protecting the customer experience from contract to go-live.

Forecasting & Performance

  • Keep activities, pipeline stages, and deal progression accurate and current in HubSpot.
  • Deliver regular territory performance reports and forecasts to the VP of Sales (SCO).
  • Continuously analyze territory results and refine your approach to improve conversion and revenue growth.

WHAT YOU BRING

  • Proven SaaS or enterprise software sales experience, with a strong track record of meeting and exceeding targets; golf industry experience strongly preferred.
  • Extensive knowledge of golf course operations, with experience working in or selling to single-course operators.
  • Familiarity with GMS platforms, POS systems, and the technology that runs a golf operation.
  • Excellent consultative selling skills, with the ability to build trust and credibility with owners, GMs, and front-line operators.
  • Strong negotiation and closing skills, including a history of winning deals against established competitors.
  • Highly organized and data-driven; disciplined about CRM hygiene, pipeline accuracy, and forecasting (HubSpot experience a plus).
  • Self-directed and results-driven, thriving as an individual contributor and able to balance priorities across a large territory.
  • A genuine passion for the golf industry and for helping operators run better businesses.

WHY JOIN CLUB CADDIE

  • Own a regional territory and be directly responsible for driving its revenue growth.
  • Sell a genuinely differentiated, unified platform into an industry you love, with the autonomy to build your own pipeline and strategy.
  • Competitive base plus uncapped commission, benefits, and career growth, backed by the scale and stability of Jonas Software and Constellation Software.
  • Help shape how Club Caddie wins with single-course operators, not just execute an existing playbook.

Club Caddie is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

To thrive in ArborBridge’s Online AP Calculus Tutor position, it’s helpful if you are…

An AP Calculus Expert.

You have formal experience tutoring the AP Calculus exam(s) and have extensive knowledge of both the AP content and AP testing strategies. You know the test inside and out and can confidently answer any student or parent question. You have a proven track record of helping students achieve outstanding score improvements, and families who work with you sing your praises. You are truly on the forefront of test preparation and enjoy keeping yourself up to date on changes to the exams and the test-taking process.

Education is your passion, and private, one-on-one online tutoring is your ideal method for providing a top-notch experience for your students and their families. You’re not interested in on-demand homework help. Instead, you are an expert at creating a personalized tutoring program: You map out customized lesson plans, solidify practice test timelines, identify the right amount of homework, and propose the ideal meeting schedule to help your students reach their goals. Department:

WDTech - R&D

We are Walker & Dunlop. We are one of the largest providers of capital to the commercial real estate industry, enabling real estate owners and operators to bring their visions of communities — where people live, work, shop, and play — to life. We are committed to creating meaningful social, environmental, and economic change in our communities.

Department Overview

WDTech is Walker & Dunlop’s technology organization, bringing together product, design, engineering, data, infrastructure, information security, and operations to build, operate, and protect the technology that powers our business.

You will have the opportunity to apply modern technology and AI within one of the nation’s leading commercial real estate finance and advisory services firms. W&D’s market position, deep industry expertise, client relationships, and proprietary data provide a strong foundation for solving meaningful business problems, improving how we work and serve our clients, and creating new sources of competitive advantage.

Across WDTech, we combine business context with disciplined technology practices and a high standard for security, resilience, and quality. Teams have ownership of meaningful problems and collaborate across disciplines, make thoughtful decisions, and continuously improve the products, platforms, and capabilities that move W&D forward.

The Impact You Will Have

The Program Manager, AI Enablement is responsible for supporting the planning, coordination, and execution of strategic AI initiatives across Walker & Dunlop. Working closely with the SVP, AI Enablement, this role translates strategic priorities into actionable plans, establishes clear processes and accountability, and ensures alignment across multiple concurrent programs.

This position serves as a key liaison between AI engineering teams, product partners, and business stakeholders to support the development, implementation, and adoption of AI capabilities across the organization. The ideal candidate brings strong program management expertise, a practical understanding of AI technologies, and exceptional organizational and communication skills to manage competing priorities, address challenges, and drive successful program outcomes.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Partner with the SVP, AI Enablement to establish priorities, develop execution plans, and coordinate a portfolio of strategic AI initiatives across engineering, product, and business functions.
  • Collaborate with AI engineering teams, product partners, and business stakeholders to align program objectives, scope, timelines, dependencies, deliverables, and success measures.
  • Coordinate the development and implementation of the AI Platform, including the Agent Layer, Agent Control Plane, Knowledge Gateway, and Context Layer, ensuring alignment on technical dependencies, development priorities, and release schedules.
  • Partner with Legal, Risk, Compliance, and Information Security teams to coordinate the development, approval, implementation, and ongoing maintenance of AI-related policies and governance standards.
  • Oversee the coordination of AI workflow and agent deployment initiatives, including intake, discovery, development, evaluation, approval, launch, and adoption.
  • Collaborate with Human Resources and department leadership to support the development and delivery of enterprise-wide AI training programs, including foundational learning and role- or department-specific training.
  • Establish and maintain program management processes, including planning cycles, project tracking, status reporting, risk registers, decision logs, and recurring stakeholder meetings.
  • Develop and maintain program governance frameworks, executive reporting, and stakeholder communications to provide visibility into progress, priorities, risks, and key decisions.
  • Proactively identify, assess, and address program risks, dependencies, and obstacles, escalating issues with recommended solutions when appropriate.
  • Support the SVP, AI Enablement in preparing executive communications, stakeholder updates, leadership presentations, and cross-functional meetings, ensuring timely follow-through on commitments and action items.
  • Identify opportunities to improve program management tools, processes, documentation, and operating practices to support the continued growth and effectiveness of AI Enablement initiatives.
  • Perform other duties as assigned

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • 7+ years of experience in program management, project management, technology delivery, or related roles, including at least 3 years managing multiple concurrent initiatives.
  • Proven experience managing complex, cross-functional programs involving engineering, product, and business stakeholders, including program planning, risk management, and executive reporting.
  • Demonstrated experience partnering with senior leadership to support strategic initiatives, organizational priorities, and decision-making.
  • Experience in technology-driven environments, preferably involving artificial intelligence, machine learning, or digital transformation initiatives.
  • PMP, PgMP, or equivalent certification and experience in commercial real estate, financial services, or capital markets preferred.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Strong knowledge of program management methodologies, governance practices, and project management tools, including Jira, Linear, Confluence, or Notion.
  • Understanding of AI platform architecture, agentic systems, and key components such as the Agent Layer, Agent Control Plane, Knowledge Gateway, and Context Layer.
  • Familiarity with AI applications, including document intelligence, knowledge retrieval, workflow automation, decision support, and agent development and monitoring.
  • Knowledge of AI governance, security, and risk management principles, including data protection, access controls, prompt injection, and agent permissions.
  • Ability to leverage AI technologies and development tools to support workflow improvements, data analysis, and operational efficiency.
  • Knowledge of emerging AI technologies and industry trends, with a commitment to continuous learning and professional development.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex technical information into clear, actionable updates for executive and business audiences.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities, navigate ambiguity, and adapt to changing business needs.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment, maintain confidentiality, work independently, and collaborate effectively across teams and leadership levels.
  • Ability to show ownership of your work, take on challenges and acknowledge growth opportunities, and demonstrate patience when learning new processes
  • Courtesy, respect, and thoughtfulness in teaming with colleagues and other stakeholders

This position has an estimated base salary of $190,000 - $210,000 plus a discretionary bonus. An employment offer is based on the applicant’s relevant work experience, applicable knowledge, skills, abilities, internal equity, and alignment with market data.

What We Offer 

  • The opportunity to join one of Fortune Magazine’s Great Places to Work winners

  • Comprehensive benefit options* that have earned Walker & Dunlop the gold level of the 2025 Cigna Healthy Workforce Designation™, some of which include:
    - Up to 83% subsidized medical payroll deductions
    - Competitive dental and vision benefits

    - 401(k) + match

    promote health, engagement, and balance

    - Company-paid life, short and long-term disability insurance

  • Career development opportunities

*Eligibility may vary based on average number of hours worked

jobs.description:
Gartner is the world's leading research and advisory company, helping enterprise leaders make faster, smarter decisions and achieve their most critical priorities. Our analysts are industry thought leaders who provide actionable, objective insight to senior executives around the world.


We are seeking a Senior Director Analyst to join Gartner's Procurement Technology research team. This role is ideal for an experienced procurement technology expert with deep knowledge of Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM), Source-to-Pay (S2P) technologies, and the evolving role of Artificial Intelligence in procurement.


As a Gartner analyst, you will shape the market's understanding of procurement technology, advise senior executives on critical decisions, and drive thought leadership that influences organizations worldwide.


What You'll Do

  • Lead Industry Research
  • Develop and deliver compelling, evidence-based research for procurement and technology leaders.
  • Establish Gartner's point of view on the evolution of:
  • Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) technology
  • Source-to-Pay (S2P) technology
  • Procurement orchestration technology
  • AI-enabled procurement
  • Contract intelligence and supplier intelligence
  • Identify emerging trends, market disruptions, and innovative technologies impacting procurement organizations.

Advise Senior Executives

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to Chief Procurement Officers, Heads of Procurement Technology, Digital Transformation Leaders and CIOs.
  • Conduct high-value client inquiries and strategic advisory discussions.
  • Help clients:
  • Develop digital transformation vision & strategy for procurement
  • Prioritize and sequence procurement tech investments including AI
  • Evaluate, select, and navigate complex vendor decisions
  • Follow best practices for technology implementation and adoption
  • Deploy effective change management for procurement technology
  • Understand the evolution and future of the procurement technology landscape

Deliver World-Class Thought Leadership

  • Publish innovative research that addresses clients' most pressing challenges.
  • Contribute to Gartner's market-leading methodologies, frameworks, and assessment models.
  • Present at Gartner conferences and executive events globally.
  • Facilitate executive roundtables, webinars, and peer discussions.

Assess the Procurement Technology Market

  • Engage with leading technology providers, startups, investors, and industry practitioners.
  • Evaluate emerging and established vendors across the procurement technology ecosystem.
  • Contribute to Gartner market research including, but not limited to:
  • Market Overviews
  • Magic Quadrants
  • Market Quadrants
  • Hype Cycles

Shape the Future of AI in Procurement

  • Lead research into the capabilities of various types of AI in procurement (i.e. generative AI, agentic AI)
  • Help clients separate AI hype from practical business outcomes
  • Lead research into the impact of AI on procurement over time
  • Establish best practices for governance, adoption, risk management, and value realization.

What You'll Need

Required Experience

  • Significant experience within procurement technology (source-to-pay), sourcing technology, and CLM technology.
  • Deep expertise in Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM), including vendor landscape of standalone CLM providers.
  • Deep understanding of Source-to-Pay (S2P) suites and procurement technology ecosystems, including vendor landscape.
  • Experience advising executives, leading transformation initiatives, and assessing procurement technology vendors.
  • Demonstrated expertise in Artificial Intelligence applications within procurement, sourcing, contracting, or supplier management.
  • Exceptional written, analytical, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to synthesize complex information into clear, actionable insight.
  • Strong executive presence and credibility with senior business leaders.

Preferred Background

We welcome candidates from a variety of backgrounds, including:

  • Procurement technology leadership
  • Procurement consulting
  • Enterprise software strategy
  • Digital procurement transformation
  • CLM solution leadership
  • Procurement operations and innovation
  • Industry analyst research
  • Experience with platforms such as SAP Ariba, Coupa, Ivalua, Oracle, JAGGAER, GEP, Icertis, Sirion, Ironclad, Agiloft, Conga, and other leading procurement and CLM vendors is highly valued.

What Makes a Successful Gartner Analyst

  • Successful analysts are naturally curious, commercially minded, and passionate about helping executives solve complex challenges.
  • They:
  • Bring a distinctive point of view with strong positions on procurement technology.
  • Challenge conventional thinking.
  • Thrive in ambiguous and rapidly changing markets.
  • Transform complex topics into actionable guidance.
  • Influence thousands of organizations through their research and advisory work.
  • Enjoy continuous learning and intellectual exploration.

Why Gartner

At Gartner, your expertise can influence the decisions of the world's leading organizations. You will collaborate with some of the brightest minds in research and advisory while helping senior leaders navigate one of the fastest-evolving areas of enterprise technology.

If you are passionate about procurement technology, excited by the transformative potential of AI, and motivated to shape the future of the market through thought leadership and client impact, we encourage you to apply.


Who are we?

At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world.

Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission-critical priorities.

Since our founding in 1979, we’ve grown to 20,000 associates globally who support over 13,000 client enterprises in ~90 countries and territories. We do important, interesting and substantive work that matters. That’s why we hire associates with the intellectual curiosity, energy and drive to want to make a difference. The bar is unapologetically high. So is the impact you can have here.

What makes Gartner a great place to work?

Our vast, virtually untapped market potential offers limitless opportunities – opportunities that may not even exist right now – for you to grow professionally and flourish personally. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance.

We hire remarkable people who collaborate and win as a team. Together, our singular, unifying goal is to deliver results for our clients.

Our teams are inclusive and composed of individuals from different geographies, cultures, religions, ethnicities, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities and generations.

We invest in great leaders who bring out the best in you and the company, enabling us to multiply our impact and results. This is why, year after year, we are recognized worldwide as a great place to work.

Gartner is the world authority on AI

At Gartner, you’ll join a company at the very center of the AI revolution. Gartner has proactive, objective guidance throughout clients’ AI journeys. We set the standard for how organizations leverage artificial intelligence to drive meaningful impact. jobs.description:
A Day in Your Life at MKS

As a Global HS Classification Specialist within the Harmonized System Center of Excellence (HSCOE), you will research, assign, document, and maintain product classifications across multiple national tariff schedules. You will work with technical documentation and partner with Engineering, Product Management, Supply Chain, regional trade teams, and other subject-matter experts to understand product function, composition, operating principles, and end use. You will apply formal HS classification methodology, prepare clear and auditable rationale, and help build the standards and knowledge base that support a sustainable global classification capability.

This is an experienced individual-contributor role for someone who can independently complete routine and moderate-risk classifications, recognize when an issue requires escalation, and explain complex conclusions clearly to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

You Will Make an Impact By

  • Researching and assigning 6-digit HS classifications and applicable country-specific tariff extensions across multiple national tariff schedules.
  • Applying the General Rules of Interpretation, Section and Chapter Notes, Explanatory Notes, customs rulings, and country-specific tariff guidance in a disciplined and sequential manner.
  • Analyzing product drawings, specifications, bills of material, datasheets, product descriptions, images, existing records, and other technical evidence.
  • Engaging Engineering, Product Management, Supply Chain, regional trade teams, and other technical SMEs when available documentation is incomplete, unclear, or conflicting.
  • Documenting the relevant technical facts, alternatives considered, methodology applied, sources reviewed, final code, national tariff extension, assumptions, and approval status.
  • Completing routine and moderate-risk classifications independently and escalating high-risk, ambiguous, precedent-setting, or strategically important cases for review by the designated U.S. licensed customs broker or HSCOE leadership.
  • Supporting risk-based quality assurance through sampled review, correction of identified issues, and participation in classification calibration sessions.
  • Creating reusable product-family rationales, classification decision guides, and research templates that improve consistency and reduce repeated analysis.
  • Helping draft and improve classification SOPs, work instructions, evidence requirements, escalation criteria, and governance controls.
  • Maintaining accurate and traceable classification data in approved repositories and in SAP, Oracle, E2open, or comparable ERP and global trade management environments.
  • Identifying recurring classification patterns, data-quality issues, documentation gaps, and opportunities for standardization or controlled bulk treatment.
  • Working with a flexible global schedule that provides reasonable recurring overlap with stakeholders in the United States, EMEA, and APAC.

What You Bring to the Team

  • Four to seven years of relevant experience in HS or tariff classification, customs brokerage, trade consulting, manufacturing, or a related global trade function.
  • Demonstrated experience classifying products across multiple national tariff schedules rather than relying only on a single country tariff.
  • Strong working knowledge of HS structure and formal classification methodology, including the GRIs, legal notes, Explanatory Notes, rulings, and national tariff guidance.
  • Ability to independently research complex products and convert technical facts into clear, defensible, and auditable classification rationale.
  • Strong written and spoken English, including the ability to explain complex conclusions, assumptions, and risks clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and experience with SAP, Oracle, and E2open or a comparable global trade management platform.
  • Strong analytical judgment, attention to detail, organization, and documentation discipline.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple assignments, identify missing information, and escalate appropriately without sacrificing quality.

Preferred Qualifications

  • A bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, International Trade, International Business, or a related field. Substantial directly relevant classification experience may be accepted in place of a degree.
  • Experience classifying complex industrial, semiconductor, vacuum, instrumentation, electrical, machinery, assemblies, components, or spare-parts products. Strong transferable experience from customs brokerage, consulting, or another manufacturing sector will also be considered.
  • A relevant customs, brokerage, or trade-compliance credential or recognized professional training.
  • Experience creating classification standards, product-family decision guides, SOPs, or knowledge-repository content.
  • Experience participating in peer review, quality sampling, or classification calibration.
