jobs.description:
Department Overview

The Office of Proposal & Award Management (OPAM), a unit within Research Development & Administration (RDA), supports OHSU's missions of healing, teaching and discovery by partnering with the research community to electively navigate the pre-award and post-­award administration on of sponsored projects. We support the OHSU research community with grant and contract proposal submission, contract negotiation, interpretation on and implementation on of sponsor terms and conditions and fiscal management of all sponsored projects.

Function/Duties of Position

The Sr. Industry Research Agreements Administrator is responsible for independently managing, analyzing, drafting, negotiating and executing complex sponsored project agreements funded by industry partners. Sr. Industry Research Agreements Administrator identifies and mitigates legal and business risks in agreements, ensures compliance with institutional policies, laws and regulations. This position must provide creative solutions to balance compliance and the needs of the research project.

Contract Management

  • Independently manage, analyze, draft, negotiate and execute complex sponsored project agreements funded by industry partners including, but not limited to, clinical trial agreements, collaboration agreements, investigator-initiated agreements, sponsored research agreements, master agreements, and business associate agreements.
  • Negotiate contract terms, incorporate appropriate terms, and as necessary, draft terms, working with various contracting parties to ensure that the requirements of the University and the industry sponsor are met while mitigating risk, maintaining the integrity of the research plan and protecting the intellectual property rights of the principal investigator and the University.
  • Consult and collaborate with CRSO, Collaborations and Entrepreneurship, OHSU Legal, Risk Management, ORIO, the funder, the sponsor and its affiliates, the principal investigator and his/her department where appropriate.
  • Ensure that contract payment schedules, budgets, reporting requirements, termination schedules, and deliverable schedules are complete, compatible with OHSU policy, practicable, and in the best interest of the principal investigator and OHSU.
  • Use extensive knowledge of applicable OHSU policy, public laws, regulations, and guidelines to translate program requirements into contract terms.
  • Verify necessary internal prior approvals, compliance requirements and documentation of subcontract institutions.

Customer Service

  • Provide superior customer service to internal and external contacts.
  • Clearly and reliably communicate with sponsors on behalf of OHSU (sponsors both internal and external to OHSU).
  • Provide subject matter expertise to entire Institution (including departments, hospital, foundation, and other contracting groups).
  • Develop and maintain working partnership with IRB, CRSO, and other internal offices as needed.
  • Actively participate as a team member by assisting others and freely sharing information.

Training

  • Provide leadership and training on internal processes and procedures to departmental staff and stakeholders, including training of Contract Administrators and Contract Coordinators.

  • Draft or modify policies, guidance, strategies, and practices to ensure researchers comply with contractual obligations under the contracts, including compliance with applicable state and federal regulation in conjunction with OHSU policies.

  • Develop contractual language, standard terms and clauses, templates and master agreements for training and use by the Industry Agreement team.

  • Participate in and contribute to externally focused departmental initiatives, such as contracts formal and informal training for department staff or faculty, brown-bag training sessions, and Research Administration Information Network (RAIN) meetings.

  • Serve as a resource for department staff, including study teams.

General Responsibilities

  • Stay current with OHSU, RDA, CRSO, ORIO and OPAM policies and procedures.
  • Maintain proficiency with University information systems including, but not limited to: InfoEd, Cognos, eCRIS, OGA, IRB, IACUC, IBC, and Conflict of Interest in Research.
  • Actively participate in training opportunities made available to build skills and increase knowledge.
  • Process Improvement - Assist in the identification, evaluation and development of more efficient and cost-effective processes.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree, plus five years of experience in federal and/or industry contract negotiation; OR

  • Equivalent combination of education and experience.

  • Must possess or attain within 6 months of hire OHSU signature authority for the specified contract type within portfolio.

Skills and Abilities

  • Operate with a high degree of independence and autonomy, with the ability to identify and escalate issues appropriately.

  • Ability to train and mentor others on understanding and negotiating contract language.

  • Ability to use independent professional judgment, take initiative, have a strong work ethic and express a positive attitude.

  • Ability to establish and maintain effective and collaborative working relationships and maintain a high degree of professionalism in dealing with OHSU faculty, staff and external funding agencies.

  • Demonstrated excellent analytical skills with the ability to understand and synthesize complex guidelines and regulatory requirements.

  • Excellent communication skills as demonstrated by the ability to interpret, convey, explain, and uphold regulatory requirements and contract language to administrative and investigator clients in the OHSU research community.

  • Ability to adapt to new or changed electronic systems, processes, and in the absence of processes.

  • Ability to handle multiple priorities in a fast-paced, sometimes stressful environment often with competing deadlines.

  • Demonstrated ability to accurately comprehend and interpret medical and scientific terminology, concepts, and methodology.

  • Ability to negotiate with multiple parties and come to mutually satisfactory results.

    Thorough understanding of budgeting principles and procedures.

Additional Details

Please enter work experience in months and years on resume.

Fully remote position within the United States. If employee chooses to utilize campus flex space, it’s a typical office environment. Possible travel to national meetings.

Regular work hours to be coordinated with manager. Work schedule falls within the normal daytime range of 7:30am–5:00pm Pacific time.

Benefits

  • Healthcare for full-time employees covered 100% and 88% for dependents.
  • $50K of term life insurance provided at no cost to the employee.
  • Two separate above market pension plans to choose from.
  • Vacation - up to 200 hours per year dependent on length of service.
  • Sick Leave - up to 96 hours per year.
  • 9 paid holidays per year.
  • Substantial Tri-Met and C-Tran discounts.
  • Employee Assistance Program.
  • Childcare service discounts.
  • Tuition reimbursement.
  • Employee discounts to local and national businesses.

Why apply to OHSU?

We are Oregon's only public academic health center. In addition to caring for patients, we lead groundbreaking research. We also train the next generation of health care professionals. As Portland's largest employer, we give you opportunities to learn and advance in a system of hospitals and clinics across Oregon and Southwest Washington. All are welcome. jobs.description:
Property Description

Davidson Hospitality Group is a dynamic and innovative hospitality management company that is constantly seeking top talent to join its team. With its headquarters located in the heart of the hospitality industry in Atlanta, Georgia, Davidson Hospitality Group is a leader in hotel and resort management, providing comprehensive and results-driven services to a diverse portfolio of properties across the United States. As a job applicant, you can expect to work in a collaborative and supportive environment that encourages creativity, growth, and professional development. With a strong commitment to excellence in guest service, employee engagement, and financial performance, Davidson Hospitality Group offers a rewarding and fulfilling career path for individuals who are passionate about the hospitality industry. Whether you are seeking a corporate role in operations, sales and marketing, revenue management, finance, human resources, or other areas, Davidson Hospitality Group offers a wide range of career opportunities for motivated and talented individuals. Join the team at Davidson Hospitality Group and be a part of a dynamic and growing organization that is dedicated to delivering exceptional hospitality experiences.

Overview

Are you an accomplished hospitality marketing leader who knows how to inspire teams, build powerful brands, and turn innovative marketing strategies into measurable business results? Do you thrive on influencing others, developing marketing talent, and driving commercial success across a diverse portfolio of hotels and resorts?

Davidson Hospitality Group is seeking a dynamic, results-driven Corporate Director of Integrated Marketing to provide strategic marketing leadership across an assigned portfolio of hotels and resorts. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced hospitality marketing professional who brings a strong track record of leadership, commercial expertise, and the ability to guide and influence marketing teams across multiple properties.

In this highly visible, above-property leadership role, you'll serve as a trusted strategic advisor to property marketing teams, general managers, regional leadership, commercial teams, and ownership. You'll play a critical role in coaching and developing property marketing leaders, elevating marketing performance, and ensuring strategies align with each hotel's unique business objectives, revenue priorities, and brand positioning.

You'll provide strategic direction and oversight across the full spectrum of integrated marketing, including digital marketing, paid media, public relations, social media, brand storytelling, and guest engagement. Rather than managing day-to-day execution, you'll empower property teams with the guidance, resources, accountability, and expertise needed to deliver exceptional results.

Working collaboratively with Davidson's corporate marketing resources, agency partners, and hotel leadership teams, you'll identify growth opportunities, strengthen marketing effectiveness, share best practices, and drive measurable commercial success across the portfolio.

Success in this role requires more than exceptional marketing expertise. We're looking for a confident, collaborative leader with strong commercial acumen, analytical thinking, exceptional relationship-building skills, and a demonstrated ability to influence, mentor, and develop teams while balancing the diverse needs of multiple hotels and ownership groups.

This position is remote; however, candidates must reside in the Southeastern United States to effectively support our regional portfolio of hotels and resorts. Travel to assigned properties will be required.

If you're a strategic thinker, passionate hospitality marketer, and proven leader who's ready to make an impact beyond a single property, we'd love to hear from you!

Responsibilities

Marketing Strategy & Commercial Leadership

  • Lead the strategic direction of integrated, omnichannel marketing plans across an assigned portfolio, guiding property teams in developing, refining, and prioritizing initiatives aligned with each hotel's business objectives, revenue strategy, positioning, and key priorities.

  • Partner closely with property commercial leaders to uncover opportunities that elevate brand awareness, generate demand, increase guest engagement, drive direct bookings, and maximize revenue throughout the traveler journey.

  • Bring a marketing perspective to commercial strategy discussions, delivering insights, innovative ideas, and actionable recommendations that optimize marketing effectiveness.

  • Shape compelling hotel and restaurant positioning, marketable offers, programming, and demand-driving initiatives that differentiate properties and connect with target audiences.

Integrated Marketing & Brand Oversight

  • Provide strategic leadership and oversight across the full marketing mix, including websites, SEO/AEO, paid media, email marketing, public relations, social media, influencer partnerships, and other guest-facing marketing touchpoints.

  • Evaluate channel strategies, messaging, content, and creative execution to ensure a cohesive guest journey and strong, differentiated brand positioning.

  • Inspire property teams to uncover compelling brand stories, memorable guest experiences, community partnerships, and creative property activations that support commercial objectives.

  • Advise on brand-building initiatives, photography, video production, and content quality, collaborating with property teams, agency partners, and Davidson's specialty marketing resources.

Portfolio & Stakeholder Relationships

  • Build strong, trusted partnerships with property marketing leaders, general managers, commercial teams, operations leaders, and ownership representatives to align marketing priorities with business goals.

  • Champion proactive communication, clear expectations, timely follow-through, and collaborative problem-solving to keep marketing initiatives moving forward.

  • Develop a deep understanding of each hotel's unique market, brand identity, ownership expectations, resources, and business challenges, tailoring marketing guidance and support to maximize impact.

  • Navigate competing portfolio priorities, anticipate challenges, and proactively communicate opportunities, risks, and recommendations to appropriate corporate and property stakeholders.

Agency & Partner Management

  • Collaborate with hotel teams to evaluate agency strategies, recommendations, deliverables, and results across public relations, paid media, social media, digital marketing, and specialty marketing disciplines.

  • Connect property marketing teams with Davidson's corporate marketing resources, preferred agency partners, innovative tools, and subject matter experts to strengthen marketing capabilities and results.

Reporting, Analytics & Performance Optimization

  • Turn marketing data into actionable insights by reviewing key performance indicators, channel effectiveness, business trends, and reporting to identify growth opportunities and recommend strategic improvements.

  • Guide property teams in evaluating campaign performance, optimizing marketing investments, and adjusting strategies based on measurable results and evolving commercial priorities.

Property Team Development & Marketing Excellence

  • Inspire, coach, and develop property marketing professionals through strategic guidance, constructive feedback, collaborative problem-solving, and sharing of marketing best practices.

  • Foster a culture of accountability, creativity, and execution excellence while empowering property teams to maintain ownership of their day-to-day marketing activities.

  • Partner with corporate marketing colleagues to elevate portfolio-wide marketing excellence through improved processes, templates, training, technology adoption, and consistent standards.

  • Stay ahead of the curve on hospitality marketing trends, emerging platforms, artificial intelligence capabilities, and evolving consumer behavior, translating innovative ideas into practical, results-driven recommendations.

  • Travel to assigned hotels and participate in meetings as business needs require, strengthening relationships and ensuring alignment across the portfolio.

If you're thrilled about leading transformative marketing efforts and creating impactful brand experiences, apply now and become an essential part of our dynamic team!

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

  • 5+ years of progressive hospitality marketing experience, including at least 2 years in a director-level hospitality marketing role; multi-property or above-property marketing experience preferred.

  • Demonstrated success leading, coaching, and developing hospitality marketing teams, including the ability to influence property-level marketing leaders and drive accountability without direct reporting authority.

  • Proven experience partnering with hotel ownership groups, general managers, and commercial leadership teams to influence marketing strategy and business performance.

  • Strong expertise in integrated marketing strategy, paid media, website optimization, SEO/AEO, social media, public relations, and email marketing.

  • Demonstrated ability to analyze marketing performance, translate data into actionable insights, and connect marketing strategies to measurable commercial outcomes.

  • Exceptional relationship-building, influencing, coaching, and conflict-resolution skills, with the confidence and credibility to lead and inspire teams without direct reporting authority.

  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills, responsiveness, organizational abilities, and commitment to delivering on expectations.

  • Ability to successfully manage priorities across multiple properties, adapt to changing business needs, and consistently meet commitments in a dynamic hospitality environment.

  • Experience working with independent hotels and major hospitality brands, including Marriott, Hilton, and Hyatt.

  • Proficiency with common business productivity tools and familiarity with hospitality marketing systems, analytics tools, and reporting platforms.

  • Must reside in the Southeastern United States and be willing to travel to assigned hotels and resorts and work varied hours as business needs require.

jobs.excerpt: About MenloMenlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it.
jobs.description:
About Menlo

Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role

Industrial design at Menlo is not cosmetic. Asimov is a physical product that will be assembled, operated, serviced, and iterated on, and how it looks, feels, and reads to the people around it is as consequential as how it performs. As our Industrial Designer, you will own the form language and physical identity of Asimov, from enclosures and surface treatments to ergonomics, CMF (color, material, finish), and packaging. You will translate that vision into parts that manufacture, assemble, and survive the real world, working shoulder to shoulder with mechanical and electrical engineers so every design decision holds up in production. This is design that ships to real hardware, not renders.

What You'll Do

  • Own industrial design for Asimov and the Menlo hardware family: form, proportion, ergonomics, and CMF, from concept and form language to production-ready enclosures, covers, and structural aesthetics

  • Turn mechanical and electrical constraints into clean, intentional design that does not hide the engineering

  • Prototype fast in foam, print, and machined parts, then iterate on real robots to test design intent

  • Own the CMF specification process: material selection, surface finish standards, color systems, and supplier engagement, and make sure those choices hold up in the field

  • Own design for manufacturing and assembly alongside mechanical engineering: DFM reviews, tolerance stack-ups, fastening, serviceability, part count, and assembly sequencing, catching issues before tooling

  • Design the human-facing details: grips, handles, access panels, indicators, and anything a person touches or reads

  • Shape the packaging and unboxing experience and user-facing documentation for Asimov kits and development hardware

  • Maintain design consistency across the Menlo hardware product family as the portfolio expands

What We Look For

  • A strong portfolio of shipped physical products, ideally complex electromechanical hardware, showing a consistent design sensibility under real technical constraints

  • 4 or more years shipping physical products: consumer electronics, robotics, medical devices, or similarly complex hardware

  • Deep industrial design fundamentals: form, proportion, ergonomics, and CMF

  • Strong proficiency in 3D modeling and surfacing (Alias, Rhino, SolidWorks, or equivalent) and rendering (KeyShot or similar), plus real DFM and DFA experience

  • Working knowledge of manufacturing processes: injection molding, sheet metal, die casting, and surface finishing

  • Experience working directly with mechanical engineers and contract manufacturers in a fast, iterative environment

  • Comfort moving from sketch to prototype to production without needing a large team around you

  • Experience designing for humanoid or legged robots, cobots, or other electromechanical systems

  • A bias for building, testing on hardware, and iterating quickly, with the judgment to know when to obsess over a detail and when to ship

Nice to Have

  • Experience taking a product from zero to first production run

  • Hands-on shop skills: 3D printing, machining, moldmaking, and finishing

  • Exposure to DFM/DFA review in a high-mix, low-volume manufacturing context

  • Familiarity with simulation-driven or CAD-driven design workflows

  • A feel for how design and brand reinforce each other

  • Interest in open-source hardware communities

Why Join Menlo

You will define what a humanoid robot looks like at the moment the category is being written. That is a rare brief at this stage of a company, and it comes with the autonomy to match. Your work ships to real machines, in the real world, fast, alongside a small team that moves fast and takes the craft seriously. If you want your design to live in hardware people actually use rather than a slide, this is the place.

A Note on AI

You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Menlo Research is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Menlo provides reasonable accommodations during the application process. If you need one, please let your recruiter know.

jobs.excerpt: Job Summary: Job Description: ABOUT MODAXOModaxo is a global collective of technology companies focused on People Transportation.
jobs.description:
Job Summary:

Job Description:

ABOUT MODAXO

Modaxo is a global collective of technology companies focused on People Transportation. Our businesses deliver software and solutions that connect people with the places they need to go. We combine the community and accountability of local businesses with the reach, investment and shared learning of a global organisation.

We operate through a decentralised, multi-brand model. Our businesses retain local ownership and autonomy, while benefiting from relevant knowledge, proven practices and connections across the wider organisation. As Modaxo grows organically and through acquisition, our ability to capture, govern and reuse knowledge becomes increasingly important.


About the role

This is a new, high-visibility role with enterprise scope. It is designed to turn expertise spread across Modaxo businesses, functions and leaders into a trusted, accessible and reusable body of knowledge and learning content. This is a strategic knowledge and capability role, accountable for translating priority knowledge into practical application. You will set the knowledge and content strategy, establish the governance model, build a prioritised roadmap and source and curate content with subject matter experts. You will be accountable for the quality and coherence of the global layer, while business units remain free to create local content within agreed standards.

The role will succeed through judgement, influence and value creation. It must balance enterprise priorities with the realities of independently run businesses and make deliberate choices about what should be captured, standardised, scaled, signposted or managed within the businesses.


The role is remote and can be based in Eastern Canada or UK/Europe.


You will deliver

1. Enterprise Knowledge Strategy and Roadmap

  • Set the strategy. Define the enterprise knowledge and content strategy, aligned to Modaxo priorities and translated into a practical multi-year roadmap.
  • Prioritise for impact. Build a transparent intake and prioritisation approach with leaders and stakeholders, focusing effort on the knowledge that will create the greatest business value.
  • Own the global layer. Clarify which knowledge should be owned globally, which should remain local, and where common standards or signposting are sufficient.
  • Connect the portfolio. Create a coherent view across leadership content, functional playbooks, case studies, templates, AI capability content, acquisition learning and other reusable assets (understanding messaging and different channels and formats).

2. Networks, Stakeholder Engagement and Knowledge Sourcing

  • Build a strong network. Create and support a network of business-unit contributors, content owners and subject matter experts who help surface needs and validate knowledge.
  • Enable communities of practice. Partner with functional and business leaders to connect practitioners around shared challenges, proven approaches and emerging practice.
  • Make expertise visible. Develop simple ways for employees to identify where relevant expertise sits and how to access it.
  • Use live exchange selectively. Combine curated content with peer learning, case discussions, expert sessions and communities where human exchange adds more value than a static asset.

3. Knowledge Capture and Curation

  • Build a repeatable sourcing model. Build effective relationships and effective ways to source and identify potential stories.Create practical ways to extract expertise, lessons learned, playbooks and examples across Modaxo without placing unnecessary burden on business leaders and domain experts.
  • Capture what works. Identify proven practices and relevant stories, validate them with the right experts and turn them into reusable enterprise assets.
  • Protect critical expertise. Identify institutional knowledge at risk through leadership changes, retirement, transformation or acquisition, and establish proportionate methods to capture and transfer it.
  • Curate before creating. Reuse, adapt or signpost strong existing material where possible and commission new content only where a genuine gap exists.
  • Support acquisition learning. Build mechanisms to capture valuable expertise and practices from acquired businesses and make relevant Modaxo knowledge easier for new businesses and leaders to access.

4. Priority Capability and Learning Content

  • Lead the content roadmap. Translate Modaxo global priorities into a sequenced roadmap of flagship knowledge and learning content, with clear audiences, outcomes, owners and delivery routes for both business and functions.
  • Accelerate AI capability in the near term. Own the knowledge and learning content that helps leaders and employees understand the impact of AI, build relevant judgement and adapt their work, partnering with the AI CoE and Transformation team and other experts.
  • Build for application. Shape content around real decisions, tools, examples and behaviour change.
  • Commission specialist expertise. Pull from subject matter experts, other writers, facilitators and internal production teams as required. This role is accountable for the content outcome, not expected to be the technical expert on every topic.
  • Shape pathways and experiences. Connect assets into practical journeys for priority audiences, including leaders, new joiners, acquired businesses and functional communities.

6. Insight, Adoption and Continuous Improvement

  • Measure usefulness. Define measures that show whether people can find, trust, apply and reuse priority knowledge. Quality is more important than volume.
  • Build feedback loops. Use platform data, search patterns, stakeholder feedback and learner evidence to understand demand, gaps and friction.
  • Maintain a living backlog. Regularly review the roadmap based on strategic need, evidence of use, duplication and changing business priorities.
  • Demonstrate value. Report clearly on adoption, quality, reach, application and selected business outcomes.

7. Knowledge Architecture and Governance

  • Design the architecture. Establish a practical taxonomy, metadata and content model so people can find relevant knowledge by topic, role, business need, audience and format.
  • Set the quality bar. Define minimum standards for accuracy, format, accessibility, ownership, approval, source attribution and review.
  • Manage the lifecycle. Put clear review, version control, archive and retirement processes in place so the knowledge base remains current rather than becoming a static repository.
  • Create accountable ownership. Ensure priority assets have named business owners and subject matter validators, with clear responsibilities for maintenance.
  • Enable trusted search and reuse. Work with system and digital workplace specialists so content is structured, tagged and maintained in a way that supports effective discovery and appropriate future AI-assisted retrieval.

The role will work across the organisation and will need to build credibility with senior leaders and practitioners globally.

What success will look like?

First 12 months

  • A clear Modaxo global knowledge and content strategy, operating model and 12 & 24 month knowledge roadmap agreed with the relevant leaders and reviewed on a defined cadence.
  • Two to three flagship priorities delivered with evidence of improved understanding, application or time-to-competency. AI capability is an early priority. Evidence of building strong relationships with key stakeholders and identifying and delivering strong learning pathways and stories.
  • A functioning knowledge-sourcing network across businesses and functions, with a repeatable route for capturing stories, playbooks, tools and lessons learned.
  • A baseline view of current content, duplication, gaps and critical knowledge at risk, with agreed action for the highest-value areas.
  • Useful adoption and quality measures in place, moving beyond course completion to include findability, reuse, freshness, confidence and application.
  • A minimum viable enterprise governance framework in use, including named ownership, review cycles and retirement standards for priority content.
  • Clear working boundaries and productive partnerships with AI Transformation, HR Systems, Communications, IT and business-owned content experts.

Medium to long term

  • Modaxo has a trusted enterprise knowledge content and governance model that scales as the Group grows.
  • Priority expertise can be found and reused across businesses without undermining local autonomy.
  • Critical knowledge is captured and transferred during acquisition, leadership transition and organisational change.
  • Leaders and employees can access practical, current content that strengthens AI capability, leadership depth, succession and business performance.
  • Duplication is reduced and strong local practice is more consistently surfaced, validated and scaled.
  • Knowledge governance is embedded through a federated network of accountable owners and contributors.

About you

Experience and expertise

  • You will have a strong track record of setting enterprise knowledge, content or capability strategy and translating it into a focused, prioritised roadmap aligned with business needs.
  • You will demonstrated success influencing senior stakeholders and engaging business units across a complex, global, multi-entity decentralised organisation, including working effectively without formal authority and have proven ability to identify, source and draw out expertise, insight and effective practice from senior leaders, subject-matter experts and practitioners.
  • You have strong content strategy and editorial experience, with the ability to turn complex or specialist knowledge into clear, engaging and practical content without losing accuracy.
  • Experience selecting and combining different channels and formats to build practical capability. This may include messaging, playbooks, tools, case studies, digital resources, structured learning, live experiences and peer exchange, rather than written content alone.
  • You will be setting priorities, governance and quality standards, and commissioning work through subject-matter experts, writers, learning specialists, creative teams or external partners rather than personally producing every element, your track record of designing or materially improving an enterprise knowledge ecosystem, including practical approaches to sourcing, curation, ownership, findability, reuse and lifecycle management is key.
  • Experience using evidence, stakeholder feedback and analytics to prioritise a portfolio of knowledge and capability needs and to assess findability, adoption, application and value.
  • Good grounding in adult learning and instructional design, with experience shaping learning pathways and designing for retention, application and behaviour change rather than information delivery alone and well as shaping practical digital learning and capability solutions. Familiarity with authoring tools and platforms such as Articulate 360, Docebo, SharePoint or equivalent would be useful, but this is not a systems administration role.
  • Experience in a technology, software, professional services, acquisitive or federated business environment is strongly preferred.
  • Experience supporting AI capability, acquisition integration, leadership development, organisational change or communities of practice would be valuable

Skills and attributes

  • Influential without authority: Builds trust across autonomous businesses and aligns diverse senior stakeholders around shared priorities, common standards, and practical outcomes.
  • Strategic and commercially grounded: Connects knowledge, capability, and content decisions to business priorities, focusing resources on areas of greatest value and impact.
  • Exceptional judgement: Distinguishes reusable organisational knowledge from information that should remain local or temporary, making sound decisions on what to create, curate, scale, adapt, or signpost.
  • Stakeholder management and executive influence: Extensive experience engaging, influencing, and building credibility with senior executives and business leaders in complex, matrixed organisations.
  • Knowledge architecture, storytelling, and content development: Strong ability to identify valuable insights within complex or technical information and transform them into compelling, accurate, and practical content for different audiences and channels.
  • Content governance and quality standards: Able to establish and maintain standards for accuracy, accessibility, consistency, localisation, and usability across a global content ecosystem.
  • Excellent communication and facilitation skills: Clear, concise written and verbal communicator in English, capable of tailoring messages, presentations, and workshops for executive, technical, and business audiences. Additional languages such as German, French, or Brazilian Portuguese are advantageous.
  • Builder mindset: Comfortable creating a new function, operating model, governance mechanisms, relationships, and ways of working in an evolving environment with limited infrastructure.
  • Data-informed decision maker: Uses quantitative and qualitative evidence to prioritise needs, improve adoption and content effectiveness, and measure business impact.
  • Curious but pragmatic about AI: Understands the implications of AI for knowledge management, content strategy, and organisational capability development while recognising where technical ownership resides.

Other

· UK/Europe or Eastern Canada, remote, with flexibility to work across time zones.

· International travel will be required periodically, anticipated at approximately two to four trips per year, subject to business need.

· Compensation will be competitive and aligned to experience and employing country.

Overview

Lumicera Health Services is seeking a Sr. Manager, Industry Relations to join our team!

The Sr. Manager, Industry Relations leads the team responsible for establishing, maintaining, and enhancing effective relationships with pharmaceutical manufacturers that produce specialty pharmaceuticals, and directs the negotiation of distribution and procurement contracts to ensure the specialty pharmacy can obtain specialty pharmaceuticals and pricing that meet the demands of its payers and patients. The primary responsibility of this position is to develop and execute manufacturer and trade engagement strategies, oversee the clinical drug pipeline, and maximize access to products in which the specialty pharmacy has a strategic interest in dispensing, including limited distribution medications. The Sr. Manager will lead and develop the Trade Relations team and Proposal Analysts and support Lumicera and its strategic partners in achieving business objectives and sourcing products competitively. This leader will interface with business leaders, pharmacists, legal, compliance, and external vendors with respect to specialty pharmacy services and trade duties.

Is this you? Find out more below!

Responsibilities

How do I make an impact on my team?

  • Lead, develop, and coach the trade relations team, setting priorities and ensuring consistent execution of manufacturer and trade engagement strategy.
  • Direct the negotiation of distribution and procurement agreements with specialty pharmaceutical manufacturers and ensure successful implementation of agreements to achieve compliance and full realization of agreed-upon fees.
  • Develop manufacturer strategies related to clinical disease states, competing medications, and alignment with the PBM formulary.
  • Oversee the clinical drug pipeline and identify opportunities to perform in RFPs and RFIs for manufacturer programs.
  • Secure access to limited distribution medications and oversee negotiation, implementation, and ongoing management of associated agreements, fees, and discounts.
  • Establish, monitor, and negotiate pricing and service agreements with manufacturers, following company policy regarding contract management, including legal and compliance review and oversight.
  • Maintain relationships with pharmaceutical manufacturers and identify manufacturer program opportunities that support the specialty pharmacy’s strategic objectives.
  • Expand and negotiate manufacturer programs, including data and enhanced services programs.

Sharecare is a digital healthcare company that delivers software and tech-enabled services to stakeholders across the healthcare ecosystem to help improve care quality, drive better outcomes, and lower costs. jobs.description:
Why Deephaven Mortgage?

Deephaven Mortgage has been a pioneer and leader in non-QM since our origin in 2012. Our longevity and strength in the non-QM space has allowed a significant number of borrowers to achieve homeownership who otherwise would not have under traditional requirements. Deephaven champions mortgage borrowers whose independence, entrepreneurial drive and determination are often the very reason they cannot qualify for a traditional loan.

We continuously and responsibly innovate new mortgage products and programs that put homeownership within reach of millions of borrowers and investors that need and deserve financing through lending ingenuity that is supported by common-sense underwriting.

Deephaven is comprised of two lending platforms. Our wholesale channel offers loans through a network of over 1,000 independent mortgage brokers. Our correspondent channel buys loans from over 200 correspondent partners.

Deephaven’s headquarters are in Charlotte, North Carolina. To learn more about our innovative loan solutions please visit www.deephavenmortgage.com or email us at .

Job Overview

In this role, you will be responsible for evaluating complex mortgage loan applications that fall outside traditional Qualified Mortgage (QM) guidelines. You will assess borrower risk based on alternative documentation, ensure compliance with company policies and investor guidelines, and play a key role in decision-making for loan approvals.

What You’ll Do

  • Manually underwrite mortgage loan transactions submitted by our Correspondent and Wholesale lending clients to company and investor credit guidelines

  • Perform quality control audits of our third-party vendor to ensure mortgage loans met all company and investor credit guidelines and requirements

  • Review loan scenarios and communicate purchase/funding eligibility requirements to our Correspondent and Wholesale lending clients

  • Collaborate with internal staff (e.g., Underwriters, Account Managers, Processors, Closers, Operations Management, etc.) of our correspondent lending clients, brokers and third party-vendors throughout the review process to clear purchase/funding eligibility conditions

  • Work closely with processing staff to clear loan conditions throughout the process

  • Assist in handling loan-level credit and compliance questions & issues and in the preparation and dissemination of updated mortgage underwriting and compliance standards and procedures

  • Any and all other duties as requested by management

Job Requirements

  • Recent, hands-on Non-QM underwriting experience is required, including, but not limited to:

    • DSCR

    • Bank Statement (personal & business)

    • P&L–only qualification

    • Asset Depletion

    • Multi-family

  • Experience underwriting HELOCs and 2nd mortgages strongly preferred.

  • 15+ years of experience as an underwriter

  • Ability to manually calculate income across all Non-QM programs, including complex self-employed borrower profiles, layered income sources, and variable cash flow.

  • Demonstrated ability to independently review and clear:

    • Title commitments & supporting documentation

    • Appraisal reports (including complex or unique property types)

    • Full condo project reviews (warrantable, non-warrantable, new construction, and small projects)

  • Proficiency in Encompass, with the ability to navigate workflows, analyze documentation, and manage conditions efficiently.

  • High-volume underwriting background, managing 50+ initial underwrites per month while maintaining quality, accuracy, and fast SLAs.

  • Strong understanding of Non-QM guidelines, investor overlays, compensating factors, and risk layering.

  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to clearly document decisions and collaborate with sales, processors, and closers.

  • Strong critical-thinking, independent-decision-making, and problem-solving skills.

  • Commitment to loan quality, compliance, and responsible lending.

Compensation

The compensation band for this role begins at $52.88 per hour, plus a performance based monthly bonus plan.

Privacy Policy

This organization participates in E-Verify

Our Perks

Flexible Time to Recharge – Personalized Time Off for What Matters (because rest isn't one-size fits all)

Future Finance Focused – Generous employer-matched 401(k) plan

Community Connect– Philanthropy Committee that creates charitable initiatives

Health from Day One – Comprehensive health insurance starting on day one of employment

Family Matters – Competitive maternity and paternity leave

Culture & Celebrations – Culture Committee with team-building events and celebrations

Ideas Welcome – Encouraging thought leadership and innovation

Guidance & Growth – Mentorship opportunities for career development

Perk Up – Exclusive discounts on travel, tech, pets, legal, and more

As both a clinical-centric frontier AI lab and an applied AI platform, Sword is reimagining how care is delivered at scale, removing traditional barriers like appointments, waiting rooms, and stigma so more people can access the care they need—and ultimately get back to lives lived in full.

Since 2020, Sword has expanded across physical therapy, women’s health, cardiometabolic, and mental health, and is now moving beyond the session to a fully AI-native, 24/7 care program that brings physical activity, therapeutic exercise, psychotherapy, nutrition, and behavior change into one connected experience. More than 700,000 members across three continents have completed over 10 million AI sessions, helping 1,000+ enterprise clients avoid more than $1 billion in unnecessary healthcare costs. Job Description:

The Engagement Lead is one of the ED&D’s primary client-facing owners, who is accountable for bridging delivery execution with strategic advisory, and commercial stewardship. This role owns the ED&D end-to-end client engagement— ensuring delivery excellence, leading the client delivery team (Architects, Data Engineers, Developers, Business Analysts, and Quality Assurance) that supports the solution, deepening relationships (internal and external), identifying (and or leading growth pursuits) growth opportunities, and connecting clients to the broader capabilities of the dentsu organization.


Depending on assignment, this role may have one or more ongoing client engagements, lead project-based work, or do both concurrently. In all engagements the expectation is the same: show up consultatively, own the outcomes, and bring synergy across teams to create genuine value for clients.


Engagement Leads are conversant across modern data and MarTech stacks and can lead value conversations without relying on a technical translator. Data is their lens for every client interaction: understanding how it flows, how it activates, and how it drives measurable customer experience outcomes and business results.

Engagement Leads should be familiar with general capabilities such as:

  • Data Platforms: Snowflake, Databricks, Google BigQuery, Amazon Redshift, Microsoft Fabric
  • Customer Data Platforms: Adobe Real-Time CDP, Salesforce Data Cloud, Tealium, Segment, Treasure Data, and Hightouch
  • Activation & Orchestration: Adobe Journey Optimizer, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze, Iterable, Oracle Responsys
  • undefined

  • 2+ years of experience in a client-facing role with demonstrated relationship ownership
  • Experience supporting or leading technology delivery teams including Business Consultants, Developers, and/or Quality Assurance

Client Ownership & Relationship Development·

Banking, credit, payments, personal finance, and financial operations—rebuilt from the ground up as a single, intelligent system. Flex is the full financial home for ambitious owners.
Since launching publicly in September 2023, Flex has scaled from zero to nine-figure annualized revenue, with a clear path to profitability by late 2026. We move fast, ship relentlessly, and operate with extreme ownership.
Our customers are affluent business owners ($3–$200M in revenue)—the backbone of the economy and one of the most underserved segments in finance. They’re stuck with outdated banks and fragmented tools. We’re replacing all of it. The opportunity is massive: a ~$1T+ revenue market hiding in plain sight. Our ambition is to build a $100B+ company by delivering a product that is fundamentally better—not incrementally improved.
Flex has raised $100M+ in equity and $300M+ in debt.
- Mission-critical problems: We build software that directly controls how money moves at scale.
- High bar, low ego: Small teams, exceptional people, real ownership.
- Speed over comfort: We prioritize execution, quality, clarity, and results.
- Enduring impact: What we’re building will define how a generation of owners runs their businesses.

Team & Locations

We hire exceptional people who want to build hard things and see their work matter immediately. Roles are available in: San Francisco, Miami, New York, and fully remote.

Flex Fuels Ambition.

About The Role

    Flex is hiring a General Manager to build and run its construction business. You own the sector end to end: the strategy for winning it, the relationships and partnerships that open it, the product priorities it needs, and the P&L it produces. You build on Flex’s platform, balance sheet and teams, and you are responsible for making Flex the primary financial institution for construction.

    The role is modeled on sector coverage at an investment bank. You decide which relationships matter, which partnerships can move hundreds of owners onto Flex at once, and what the product must deliver to win them. Flex’s product, credit, risk and member experience teams execute and service alongside you. The role reports directly to the CEO.

    Construction is one of the largest and most capital-intensive owner-operated sectors in Flex’s range. Contractors, specialty trades, developers and building-products distributors carry long receivable cycles, bonding requirements and heavy equipment and payroll spend, and they decide where to bank on the advice of a small circle of sureties, lenders, associations and software vendors. The General Manager owns that circle.

What You'll Do

    • Own the sector P&L. You are accountable for one number: owners in construction banking with Flex and the revenue they generate. You build the model behind it, report against it weekly, and answer for it.

    • Map the sector and cover it. Within 90 days you have identified the 200 people who move construction and have a coverage plan for each. From then on, that is where your time goes.

    • Originate. Bring owners and firms to Flex directly, through dinners, site visits, conferences, portfolio days and referrals. You represent Flex in your sector and you are expected to be present in it.

    • Structure the partnerships that move the sector. A surety or construction-lender referral program. A trade association. A franchisor or buying group. A construction ERP integration. A sponsor rolling Flex across a portfolio of contractors. You identify them, negotiate them, and own the relationship after signature.

    • Set the product agenda for your sector. You tell product leadership what owners require before they will move their primary banking relationship, in what order, and why.

    • Build the team as the book grows. You begin with Flex’s account executives, account managers and member experience team supporting you. When the pipeline exceeds what one person can cover, you hire and lead your own sector team.

    • Work AI-native. Research, relationship tracking, outreach and modeling run on tools you build or adopt, so your time goes to relationships.

Requirements

    • 7 to 12 years in investment banking, private credit, private equity, venture, or a senior commercial seat inside construction. You have a demonstrable record of originating business, not servicing it.

    • An active network in construction. You can name the 50 people who matter and most of them would take your call this week.

    • Fluent in how contractors are paid and where their capital gets tied up: margins, working capital, pay applications, retainage, bonding, and who lends against each.

    • Comfortable structuring partnerships, negotiating referral economics, and working through a term sheet without support.

    • You build your own models. Banker-level Excel and a working understanding of the unit economics of deposits, cards and credit.

Nice To Haves

    • Experience in fintech, banking or lending, or selling a financial product to business owners.

    • A standing in construction: a podcast, a newsletter, a conference stage, or a board seat at a trade body.

    • Investing, advisory or operating experience in a company in construction.

How To Prepare

    As part of the application, please be prepared to submit a one-pager along with your CV on how you would bring construction to Flex. It should cover:

    • The sector and its owners. Who they are, how many of them fall in Flex’s range, how they make money and where their capital gets tied up.

    • What they need from a bank. The products and terms that would make owners in the sector move their primary relationship, and in what order.

    • The map. The 20 to 30 people and institutions that move the sector, and how many of them you know personally

    • The first three partnerships. The programs that would put hundreds of owners on Flex at once, and why each counterparty would say yes.

    • The investment and the return. A light P&L for the sector: what Flex would need to put in over the first two years (people, product, partnership economics, marketing) and how that investment comes back, in the form of owners banking with Flex and the revenue they produce. We are looking for the shape of the business and the logic behind it.

    • The plan and the team. How you will build this out and you will need to do it.

      • Treat it as a coverage pitch. Bring the map, the partnerships and the economics, and be ready to defend each one.

Why Join Us

Build something generational — Capture the full lifecycle of money for ambitious business owners.
Work on real money, real risk — Payments, credit, and banking at serious scale.
Solve hard problems — AI, underwriting, compliance, and global finance from first principles.
True ownership — Small teams, high trust, real accountability.
Founder-level exposure — Direct access to leadership, customers, and investors.
High bar, high taste — Move fast without cutting corners.
Elite peers — People here are builders, not tourists.
Real upside — Meaningful equity if you help build something big.

jobs.description:
Overview

Geosyntec has an exciting opportunity for a Senior Director level Hydrogeologist to join our contaminated land practice in the UK. This position is suited to a talented, highly motivated individual with extensive experience in contaminated land, groundwater assessment and remediation consulting, who is interested in leading and contributing to our innovative and challenging projects. The successful candidate could be based near one of our offices in Manchester, Bristol or Delph, or fully remote.

Geosyntec is an international engineering and consulting firm serving private and public-sector clients to address their new ventures and complex problems involving our environment, natural resources, and civil infrastructure. Our engineers, scientists, technical and project employees serve our clients from offices across the world. Ranked by ENR as one of the top environmental engineering design firms, Geosyntec is internationally known for its technical leadership, broad experience, and exceptional client service.

We invest in our people. Each employee is unique, and your career at Geosyntec will be too. We offer competitive pay and benefits, and well-being programs to support you and your family.

To Learn More Visit:

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

We expect that you will work on a wide variety of challenging technical projects and will help Geosyntec expand its current practices and capabilities. Collaboration and mentoring are cornerstones of Geosyntec’s culture. You can expect to work closely with experienced professionals across our UK & Ireland business, who will help integrate you into Geosyntec’s culture and advance your career ambitions.

Your responsibilities may include:

  • Growing our site investigation & remediation practice through client relationships, business development efforts and implementing market growth initiatives
  • Project management, including planning and implementing investigation and remediation projects, budgeting and budget management, meeting project schedules, quality requirements and client expectations.
  • Data assessment and development of conceptual site models
  • Design, implement and interpret hydrogeological field test results (e.g. slug testing, pumping tests, packer tests etc.)
  • Design, development and calibration of groundwater models to assess groundwater migration/problems and where needed solute transport, or thermal modelling.
  • Undertaking risk assessments (controlled waters and human health) using both analytical and (where appropriate) numerical packages.
  • Interpretation of modelling results to answer project objects and identify/develop remediation criteria or further works including the design of further works, site investigations, and/or remediation strategies etc.
  • Management of fieldwork tasks including site inspections, multi-media environmental sampling and characterisation, drilling oversight, contractor oversight, and management of remediation system operations and maintenance.
  • Management of remediation treatability and pilot tests with subsequent data evaluation, report writing and work plan development.
  • Management, training and mentoring of early and mid-career professionals.
  • Preparing technical reports, letters, memoranda, plans, specifications, and proposals.
  • Preparing for and participating in meetings with clients, regulatory personnel, and other parties; and
  • Supporting the senior team in client care and development activities.

Geosyntec offers professional development opportunities including attendance and presenting at technical conferences, in-house seminars, webinars, and mentoring, which allow our professionals to build the technical and business skills necessary to become successful consultants. You will be able to engage with our global technical action groups, which promote collaboration across the company as well as individual professional development. jobs.excerpt: About airSlateairSlate is a global SaaS technology company that develops no-code workflow automation, electronic signature, and document management solutions.
jobs.description:
About airSlate

airSlate is a global SaaS technology company that develops no-code workflow automation, electronic signature, and document management solutions. Our award-winning products - SignNow, pdfFiller, DocHub, altaFlow, Instapage, and US Legal Forms - serve over hundreds of millions of users and more than one million customers worldwide, helping organizations of every size digitize processes, improve efficiency, and transform how they work.
We’re in an exciting phase of growth and transformation, with teammates in more than 20 countries across three continents and main hubs in the United States, Poland, Ukraine and Philippines.
At airSlate, we’re building value for customers and a culture where growth and innovation go hand in hand. We’re looking for people eager to shape products, scale a company, and thrive in a fast-moving environment.

Who we are

airSlate built a $1800M+ business serving dozens of millions of users across pdfFiller, SignNow, DocHub, AltaFlow and Instapage, on the back of a proprietary long-tail marketing engine. AI is now disrupting the core of that business and, at the same time, opening up a much bigger opportunity: solving the underlying business outcome end to end — draft, sign, track, invoice, collect — not just the document step.

The opportunity

We're running the company as two deliberately separate efforts. Our legacy portfolio — pdfFiller, DocHub, SignNow, AltaFlow — which we're optimizing for defensible 3-5 year revenue to fund what's next. AI Labs: a structurally separate, AI-native business we're building from scratch, targeting $20-50M of new topline in 2-3 years.
AI Labs is already proving the model works. BizDraft — AI-drafted agreements for SMBs — has shipped and is our learning vehicle for running a ~90% AI-driven product end to end. Ordinum, an AI compliance agent for regulated SMBs, is in development. BizPulse, which reconstructs a small business's financial and operational reality straight from its inbox, is in a controlled experiment. Alongside the products, AI Labs has rebuilt the pdfFiller editor from scratch (5x faster, 10x smaller) and stood up internal AI systems — Discovery Engine, document-based segmentation, Synthetic Users, Zero Reporting — that are starting to change how the rest of the company works.
We need a product leader to take AI Labs from "proving the model" to a real business.

The role

You'll own product for AI Labs: strategy, roadmap, and definition across our AI-native product line (BizDraft, Ordinum, BizPulse, and whatever comes next). You lead a small group of Product Owners, and will work in tight lockstep with AI Labs' engineering leadership, who own the build team.
A small go-to-market team — one product marketer and one marketer — supports AI Labs today, and you'll work closely with them on market analysis, idea generation, triage and prioritization, positioning, and launch.

What you'll do:

  • Own product strategy and roadmap for AI Labs, targeting $20-50M in new AI-native topline over 2-3 years
  • Scale BizDraft post-launch, drive Ordinum and BizPulse through to go/no-go for launch
  • Identify, size and prioritize 2 to 5 more high-potential projects, based on established customer needs and a potential competitive advantage for airSlate
  • Hire and lead a very small team of AI-native, 0-to-1 Product Owners, each owning the build out of a specific product against the prioritized ideas, and developing it based on customer and market feedback
  • Develop a working understanding of our existing products (pdfFiller, SignNow, DocHub, AltaFlow) and their customers, to surface needs and use cases AI Labs can act on — some of which may be better rolled into an existing product as a feature rather than launched as a standalone AI Labs product
  • Define product requirements and priorities with the precision AI-driven execution demands
  • Partner closely with AI Labs' engineering lead on sequencing and trade-offs, without owning the engineering team directly
  • Decide which internal AI systems incubated in Labs (Discovery Engine, segmentation, Synthetic Users, Zero Reporting, etc.) are ready to hand off to a functional owner — Marketing, CIO, Data — once proven, and which stay in Labs
  • Partner with the AI Labs go-to-market team on positioning, GTM planning, and launch execution for each product as it matures
  • Represent AI Labs product progress to the executive team and the board

Who you are:

  • Experienced in building 0-to-1 inside a larger company
  • A builder-operator who has shipped AI-native products end to end — or at the very least, transformative standalone features or modules on top of existing products, with proven adoption success
  • Deeply fluent in AI-assisted build workflows (Claude Code, OpenAI's Codex and the like) and what they change about team shape, ratios, and the product definition bar
  • Comfortable driving product outcomes through precision and influence rather than headcount — you won't have an engineering team reporting to you
  • Commercially minded — comfortable partnering closely with marketing and PMM on positioning and GTM
  • Low ego and collaborative — able to earn credibility with engineering leadership and peers rather than assume it from the org chart
  • SaaS, SMB, and document/workflow space experience a plus

Why this and not somewhere else

Ownership of product for the most ambitious green-field initiative in the company, with real budget and a mandate to help build a $20-50M+ business from scratch — backed by a company with 100M+ users and proven distribution.

What we offer

Flexible working environment - Our teams operate across the globe. We value in‑person collaboration in our hubs, but we also embrace remote and hybrid working. You can work from one of our offices in the United States, Poland, Romania or Ukraine, or remotely from many countries.
Competitive compensation and stock options - We offer salaries that reflect local market conditions and experience, plus a performance-based bonus system and stock options so you share in the company’s growth.
Professional growth and learning - We invest in your development through courses, conferences, and access to learning resources. We encourage career growth and internal mobility, supporting teammates who want to explore new opportunities within airSlate.
Health and well‑being - We provide comprehensive benefits tailored to each country, including health coverage, wellness programmes and access to fitness options. We also dedicate quarterly company-wide Mental Health Days, when everyone takes time off to rest and recharge.
Family‑friendly culture - Family life is part of who we are, and we embrace it in many forms. From flexibility for parents to our airSlate Junior Club for kids, to company-wide family days and our pet-friendly approach, we’re committed to making work and life easier to balance.

jobs.excerpt: OverviewHealthEdge® offers AI-powered operational infrastructure for health insurance companies, guaranteeing an enduring financial edge in an increasingly competitive market.
jobs.description:
Overview

HealthEdge® offers AI-powered operational infrastructure for health insurance companies, guaranteeing an enduring financial edge in an increasingly competitive market. We're experiencing strong market momentum, with a growing number of health plans choosing HealthEdge to modernize their operations and compete more effectively. As we expand, we're investing in the people who power that growth, making this a pivotal moment to join us and shape the future of healthcare technology. Learn more at HealthEdge.com.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Director, IT Operations is accountable for establishing and operating the service-management governance model for Client IT Operations. This leader will create the standards, operating discipline, governance, and management mechanisms required to deliver consistent, predictable, and transparent technology operations across a complex 24x7 BPaaS/EPaaS environment.

The role is designed to be a force multiplier for operational teams: strengthening Incident, Problem/RCA, Change, Release, Knowledge, and Service Governance practices while ensuring that technical ownership remains with the teams responsible for resolution. The Director will drive cross-functional accountability, executive-quality communications, and measurable continuous improvement across onshore and offshore delivery organizations.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Build and lead the Service Management Office, including the governance framework, operating cadence, standards, controls, templates, and performance mechanisms used across Client IT Operations.
  • Own the service-management process framework for Incident Management, Problem Management/RCA, Change Management, Release Management, Knowledge Management, and related service-governance practices.
  • Establish clear roles, decision rights, escalation paths, and accountability across Tech Ops, infrastructure/platform teams, product teams, implementation teams, Service Desk, customers, and third-party partners.
  • Lead governance for major incidents and service disruptions, ensuring disciplined process execution, timely stakeholder engagement, effective bridge management, clear escalation, and high-quality internal and customer communications.
  • Define and enforce RCA standards, including ownership, timelines, evidence quality, corrective/preventive actions, cross-functional follow-through, and closure governance.
  • Lead Change and Release governance, including CAB effectiveness, production-readiness controls, risk assessment, rollback/testing expectations, release calendars, and post-change validation.
  • Create consistent executive and customer communication standards for incidents, service health, operational risk, planned changes, and material service issues.
  • Develop service governance scorecards and management reporting covering SLA performance, incident trends, change quality, RCA completion, recurring failure patterns, operational risk, and continuous-improvement commitments.
  • Partner with technical leaders to identify systemic operational issues and convert recurring incidents, manual processes, and control gaps into prioritized improvement initiatives.
  • Drive standardization across customer environments while allowing documented exceptions where contractual, technical, or customer-specific requirements demand variation.
  • Partner with tooling and observability teams to improve ITSM workflows, Jira/JSM utilization, telemetry, alerting, automation, and the quality of operational data used for governance and decision-making.
  • Establish and maintain service-management documentation, playbooks, templates, knowledge standards, and audit-ready evidence.
  • Build an effective onshore/offshore operating model that uses follow-the-sun capabilities while maintaining appropriate leadership, customer engagement, and executive communication coverage.
  • Develop SMO talent, establish measurable objectives, coach leaders and practitioners, and create a culture of ownership, transparency, urgency, and continuous improvement.

ROLE BOUNDARIES AND OPERATING PRINCIPLES

  • The SMO owns the process, governance, communication standards, escalation discipline, and enforcement mechanisms; technical teams retain accountability for technical diagnosis, remediation, recovery, and permanent corrective action.
  • Incident Management facilitates coordinated response and communication; the responsible Technical Operations Manager, Technical Lead, Technical Director, platform, product, or engineering owner remains accountable for technical resolution.
  • The SMO is expected to challenge weak process execution, unclear ownership, inadequate evidence, missed commitments, and recurring operational failure regardless of organizational boundary.
  • Governance must improve speed and quality of delivery; controls should be risk-based, measurable, and increasingly automated.

LEADERSHIP & STAKEHOLDER RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Serve as a senior operational partner to the VP, Client IT Operations and other technology and business leaders.
  • Influence across organizational boundaries without relying solely on direct reporting relationships.
  • Provide concise, fact-based executive updates during high-severity events and periods of elevated operational risk.
  • Build trusted working relationships with customer-facing leaders, Technical Operations Managers, Technical Directors, infrastructure/platform teams, product and implementation organizations, vendors, and offshore delivery leaders.
  • Escalate systemic risks and accountability gaps early, with clear recommendations and decisions required.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in IT operations, service management, production support, technology delivery, or related disciplines, including significant leadership responsibility.
  • Demonstrated leadership of enterprise Incident, Problem, Change, Release, or broader IT Service Management functions in complex, high-availability environments.
  • Strong working knowledge of ITIL practices and the ability to translate frameworks into pragmatic operating processes rather than compliance-only administration.
  • Experience leading major-incident response, executive/customer communications, RCA governance, and cross-functional remediation.
  • Proven ability to design or materially improve service-management operating models, governance structures, workflows, metrics, and tooling.
  • Experience operating across global onshore/offshore teams and 24x7 service environments.
  • Strong analytical capability with experience using operational data, trends, and service metrics to identify risk and drive improvement.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex operational issues clearly to executives and customers.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive accountability and change across teams where authority is distributed.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience in healthcare technology, healthcare payer operations, BPaaS, SaaS, EPaaS, or other highly regulated/transaction-intensive environments.
  • Experience with Jira Service Management (JSM), enterprise ITSM platforms, observability/monitoring platforms, PagerDuty or comparable on-call tooling, and workflow automation.
  • Experience supporting environments with significant customer-specific integrations, data operations, third-party dependencies, and complex production release requirements.

MEASURES OF SUCCESS

  • Consistent adoption of defined service-management standards across Client IT Operations.
  • Improved major-incident execution, communication quality, escalation speed, and stakeholder confidence.
  • Reduced repeat incidents through stronger RCA quality, corrective-action governance, and problem management.
  • Improved change success rate and reduced change-related incidents through stronger readiness and risk controls.
  • Clear, timely, and reliable operational reporting with fewer manual reconciliations and conflicting sources of truth.
  • Reduced ambiguity in ownership and faster resolution of cross-functional operational issues.
  • Measurable reduction in operational risk, process variance, and avoidable manual effort.
  • A scalable SMO organization viewed by delivery teams as an enabler of better operations and by leadership as a reliable source of operational truth.

LEADERSHIP PROFILE

The successful candidate will be a pragmatic operator who combines service-management discipline with strong judgment, executive presence, and the willingness to hold teams accountable. This role requires someone who can move comfortably between a Sev1 bridge, an executive review, a customer discussion, a process-design session, and a data-driven operating review—and who understands that the objective of governance is better service outcomes.

Geographic Responsibility: Remote, US

Type of Employment: Full-time, permanent

FLSA Classification (USA Only): Exempt

Work Environment: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job: 

  • The employee is occasionally required to move around the office. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
  • Work across multiple time zones in a hybrid or remote work environment.
  • Long periods of time sitting and/or standing in front of a computer using video technology.
  • May require travel dependent on company needs.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of the job being performed by the individual(s) assigned to this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required. HealthEdge reserves the right to modify, add, or remove duties and to assign other duties as necessary. In addition, reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Candidates may be required to go through a pre-employment criminal background check.

HealthEdge is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to workforce diversity and actively encourage all qualified persons to seek employment with us, including, but not limited to, racial and ethnic minorities, women, veterans and persons with disabilities.
