Job Description

As a Customer Success Manager focused on direct tax, you will translate complex tax rules and changing regulations into practical guidance, helping clients stay ahead of change and make confident decisions in every filing season.

Customer Success is not just a function or team at Thomson Reuters, but also our reason for doing business. We measure our success based on the prioritization of our customers' needs and goals. The relationship we create with our customers determines the future benefits for them and our company. The Customer Success Manager (CSM) is assigned a book of business specific to Concierge and/or Advisory customers, responsible for the development of customers' knowledge on their suite of offerings. The CSM will manage these customers to drive performance towards Thomson Reuters' strategic objectives and retention goals. This will require the management of multiple projects with strong business acumen to remove obstacles interfering with the growth and retention of customers.

Key Responsibilities
In this opportunity as a Customer Success Manager, you will:

  • Partner with customers to define success, deliver educational activities throughout their lifecycle, and track progress toward business outcomes
  • Develop and share best practices and Customer Success Plans, collaborating with internal teams like Sales and Professional Services
  • Monitor customer health by tracking usage data and escalating critical concerns, using insights to drive strategic adjustments
  • Identify and activate commercial growth opportunities, recommending improvements based on customer maturity and working closely with the commercial team
  • Ensure customers receive maximum value from their investment, driving retention and growth through tailored engagement and collaboration
  • Leverage technology tools (e.g., Gainsight, Salesforce) to manage client information, pipeline, and financial forecasts accurately
  • Build and present business plans, report on market and competitor activities, and represent Customer Success in cross-functional meetings to support business objectives

Required Qualifications
You are a fit for the role of Customer Success Manager if you have:

  • 8+ years of professional experience, with a minimum of 3 years’ experience in customer success
  • Direct Tax experience
  • 4-year college degree required
  • Experience working in and around cloud software solutions and cloud delivery models
  • Strong business acumen and communication skills; can manage a customer journey, conflict resolution, and problem-solving.
  • Ability to travel, 25%

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree or equivalent
  • Salesforce user experience
  • Functional/technical skills in SaaS implementations and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) applications

What’s in it For You?

  • Flexibility & Work-Life Balance:Flex My Way is a set of supportive workplace policies designed to help manage personal and professional responsibilities, whether caring for family, giving back to the community, or finding time to refresh and reset. This builds upon our flexible work arrangements, including work from anywhere for up to 8 weeks per year, empowering employees to achieve a better work-life balance.

  • Career Development and Growth:By fostering a culture of continuous learning and skill development, we prepare our talent to tackle tomorrow’s challenges and deliver real-world solutions. Our Grow My Way programming and skills-first approach ensures you have the tools and knowledge to grow, lead, and thrive in an AI-enabled future.

  • Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer comprehensive benefit plans to include flexible vacation, two company-wide Mental Health Days off, access to the Headspace app, retirement savings, tuition reimbursement, employee incentive programs, and resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.

  • Culture:Globally recognized, award-winning reputation for inclusion and belonging, flexibility, work-life balance, and more. We live by our values: Obsess over our Customers, Compete to Win, Challenge (Y)our Thinking, Act Fast / Learn Fast, and Stronger Together.

  • Social Impact: Make an impact in your community with our Social Impact Institute. We offer employees two paid volunteer days off annually and opportunities to get involved with pro-bono consulting projects and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives.

  • Making a Real-World Impact: We are one of the few companies globally that helps its customers pursue justice, truth, and transparency. Together, with the professionals and institutions we serve, we help uphold the rule of law, turn the wheels of commerce, catch bad actors, report the facts, and provide trusted, unbiased information to people all over the world.

In the United States, Thomson Reuters offers a comprehensive benefits package to our employees. Our benefit package includes market competitive health, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance programs, as well as a competitive 401k plan with company match. In addition, Thomson Reuters offers market leading work life benefits with competitive vacation, sick and safe paid time off, paid holidays (including two company mental health days off), parental leave, sabbatical leave. These benefits meet or exceeds the requirements of paid time off in accordance with any applicable state or municipal laws. Finally, Thomson Reuters offers the following additional benefits: optional hospital, accident and sickness insurance paid 100% by the employee; optional life and AD&D insurance paid 100% by the employee; Flexible Spending and Health Savings Accounts; fitness reimbursement; access to Employee Assistance Program; Group Legal Identity Theft Protection benefit paid 100% by employee; access to 529 Plan; commuter benefits; Adoption & Surrogacy Assistance; Tuition Reimbursement; and access to Employee Stock Purchase Plan.Thomson Reuters complies with local laws that require upfront disclosure of the expected pay range for a position. The target total cash compensation range varies across locations.For any eligible US locations, unless otherwise noted, the target total cash compensation range for this role is $93,100 USD - $172,900 USD.Pay is positioned within the range based on several factors including an individual’s knowledge, skills and experience with consideration given to internal equity. Base pay and any target sales incentive are part of a comprehensive Total Reward program which also includes flexible and supportive benefits and other wellbeing programs.Target total cash compensation ranges are inclusive of both base pay and any target sales incentive.This job posting will close 12/31/2026.

About Us

Thomson Reuters informs the way forward by bringing together the trusted content and technology that people and organizations need to make the right decisions. We serve professionals across legal, tax, accounting, compliance, government, and media. Our products combine highly specialized software and insights to empower professionals with the data, intelligence, and solutions needed to make informed decisions, and to help institutions in their pursuit of justice, truth, and transparency. Reuters, part of Thomson Reuters, is a world leading provider of trusted journalism and news.

We are powered by the talents of 26,000 employees across more than 70 countries, where everyone has a chance to contribute and grow professionally in flexible work environments. At a time when objectivity, accuracy, fairness, and transparency are under attack, we consider it our duty to pursue them. Sound exciting? Join us and help shape the industries that move society forward.

As a global business, we rely on the unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences of all employees to deliver on our business goals. To ensure we can do that, we seek talented, qualified employees in all our operations around the world regardless of race, color, sex/gender, including pregnancy, gender identity and expression, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, disability, age, marital status, citizen status, veteran status, or any other protected classification under applicable law. What We Can Achieve Together:


As the Reporting & Private Awards Specialist for the Great Plains Division, you will provide centralized reporting, award administration, and financial reporting support as part of the Great Plains Division Finance Operations & Enablement Team. Reporting to the Finance Operations & Enablement Director, you will be responsible for preparing, coordinating, and maintaining accurate financial reports for internal stakeholders, donors, private awards, and partner organizations while supporting consistent reporting practices across multiple Pods/BUs.


You will serve as a subject matter resource for financial reporting requirements and help ensure financial data is complete, accurate, timely, and compliant with donor, organizational, and regulatory requirements. You will collaborate closely with Finance Directors, Finance Managers, Budget & Forecast Specialists, Development staff, and Accounting Specialists to support financial transparency, stewardship, and decision-making.


Other areas of responsibilities include, but are not limited to:


Private Award Financial Management & Reporting

  • Coordinate financial reporting requirements for private awards, donor-funded projects, and other restricted funding sources.
  • Prepare and submit accurate financial reports in accordance with award agreements, donor requirements, and organizational standards.
  • Monitor financial activity against approved award budgets and funding restrictions.
  • Identify, investigate, and resolve reporting discrepancies or compliance concerns.
  • Partner with Development and program staff to support financial stewardship and donor accountability, including notifying staff of needed end-date extensions and monitoring award payments.
  • Maintain documentation and audit support files for awarded funds and reporting activities.
  • Responsible for closing Private Awards.

Financial Reporting

  • Ensure reporting consistency through standardized templates, methodologies, and data definitions.
  • Support preparation of internal management reporting, conservation reporting, and external reporting requirements.
  • Assist with board, donor, and partner reporting deliverables as assigned.

Process Standardization & Documentation

  • Maintain standardized reporting procedures and reporting calendars.
  • Develop and update reporting guides, job aids, and process documentation.
  • Collaborate across Divisions in the implementation of new reporting tools, dashboards, and process improvements.
  • Recommend enhancements that improve report accuracy, efficiency, and user experience.
  • Participate in finance process improvement and automation initiatives.

Stakeholder Support & Training

  • Respond to reporting and award-related inquiries from Finance Managers, Directors, and program staff.
  • Provide guidance regarding reporting requirements, financial data interpretation, and reporting schedules.
  • Support training efforts related to reporting tools, templates, and financial stewardship requirements.
  • Serve as a resource for questions regarding private award financial reporting processes.

Compliance & Internal Controls

  • Ensure financial reports comply with organizational policies, donor requirements, and applicable accounting standards.
  • Support audit requests and compliance reviews related to reporting and private awards.
  • Maintain appropriate documentation supporting reported financial results.
  • Adhere to established internal control and financial governance practices.

This is a remote position located within in the Great Plains Division (Arkansas, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri, Kansas, Nebraska, North Dakota, South Dakota, Oklahoma, and Texas) and strong preference for individuals who are able to support partners in the Central Time zone.


We’re Looking for You:


Are you looking for work you can believe in? At TNC we strive to embody a philosophy of Work that You Can Believe in where you can feel like you are making a difference every day. We’re looking for someone with strong organizational skills to support reporting and private award administration across multiple Pods/BUs, and who can exercise judgment in interpreting reporting requirements and resolve data discrepancies. If you're attentive to detail, able to multitask, and comfortable working independently and as a collaborative team player who contributes to organizational consistency through standardized reporting practices, then this is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the ongoing mission of conservation by directing and shaping the work of our team!

What You’ll Bring:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration or related field and 3 years' related experience or equivalent combination.
  • Minimum of 2 years of experience using Workday including data entry, reporting, recruiting, and/or other functions.
  • Experience with accounting/financial issues and analysis.
  • Experience using accounting and financial reporting systems.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and financial reporting applications.
  • Ability to manipulate, analyze, and interpret data.
  • Technical experience with spreadsheet programs, general ledger reports and financial management tools.
  • Experience with GAAP and fund accounting principles, practices and regulations.
  • Experience, coursework or other training with U.S. Federal Uniform Guidance, state and local regulations, multilateral and international regulations, and standard contract clauses, as applicable.

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Multi-lingual skills and/or multi-cultural experience appreciated.
  • Experience with donor-funded, grant-funded, or restricted-funding environments.
  • Experience supporting external financial reporting requirements.
  • Knowledge of non-profit accounting and stewardship practices.
  • Experience with financial dashboards, business intelligence tools, or report automation.
  • Familiarity with award compliance, budget monitoring, and project accounting.

This position requires a valid driver's license and compliance with TNC’s Auto Safety Program. Who We Are:

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring:

Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits. The Nature Conservancy is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Our commitment to equal employment opportunity includes the recognition that our conservation mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people of all backgrounds, beliefs, and culture. Recruiting and mentoring staff to create an inclusive organization is a priority, and we encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, sexes, national or regional origins, ages, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military, protected veteran status or other status protected by law.

CoverMyMeds is seeking a Senior Manager, Data Governance to lead the implementation and ongoing operation of its data governance and data enablement capabilities. This leader will build and manage a team of domain data analysts and data stewards who support business domains by addressing data quality, lineage, metadata, catalog, and data product control needs.


This is a hands-on leadership opportunity within a developing data governance function. You will translate governance strategies, policies, and standards into practical services that help teams understand, manage, and improve their data. Success requires data governance expertise, service-oriented leadership, strong change-management skills, and the ability to influence partners without relying on formal authority.


What You’ll Do:

  • Lead and develop a team of domain data analysts and data stewards responsible for the day-to-day implementation of data governance and data quality controls
  • Implement and maintain the CoverMyMeds data enablement framework, including policies, standards, and procedures for data management, data quality, lineage, metadata, and responsible data use
  • Operationalize data governance capabilities across data quality, business and technical metadata, data lineage, data cataloging, and data product controls.
  • Partner with domain data officers, data owners, enterprise architecture, IT security, legal, compliance, and technology teams to establish accountability and embed governance practices into business operations
  • Align data analysts and stewards with business domains, enabling them to develop subject-matter expertise and serve as a first point of contact for data-related issues
  • Guide the identification, assessment, prioritization, and remediation of data quality issues in partnership with data owners and technology teams.
  • Define and monitor data enablement metrics and key performance indicators to evaluate program effectiveness and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Drive adoption and change by communicating the value of new data governance services, building cross-functional support, and helping teams succeed in a developing operating model.
  • Promote compliance with applicable data privacy requirements and internal data security policies, including considerations related to GDPR, CCPA, and HIPAA.
  • Coach and support team members through clear goals, ongoing feedback, collaborative problem-solving, and a service-oriented leadership approach

Basic Requirements:

  • Degree or equivalent experience, and typically requires 9+ years of relative professional experience and 1+ years of supervisory and/or management experience
  • Experience implementing or operating data governance, data management, or data enablement programs in a complex organization
  • Knowledge of data governance principles and practices, including data quality, metadata management, data lineage, data cataloging, and data stewardship
  • Experience leading people, teams, or cross-functional initiatives, including situations requiring influence without direct authority
  • Experience partnering with business and technology stakeholders to translate data governance policies and standards into operational processes
  • Demonstrated communication and change-management skills, including the ability to build understanding and adoption of new capabilities
  • Experience identifying, assessing, and coordinating the resolution of data quality or data management issues
  • Ability to analyze complex issues, establish priorities, and coordinate team activities to deliver practical solutions

Preferred Skills / Experience:

  • Familiarity with data governance frameworks and industry practices, such as DAMA-DMBOK
  • Experience using enterprise data catalogs such as Alation, Collibra, or IBM InfoSphere. CoverMyMeds currently uses Alation as its data catalog, while experience with comparable platforms is relevant
  • Familiarity with master data management concepts, frameworks, or technologies, including platforms from IBM or Informatica

You want your work to support the people who keep the food supply safe. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you. Apply today!

WHO WE ARE:

• Leader in food safety solutions for both contract sanitation and chemistry in the food processing industry.

• Over 10,000 dedicated team members across North America.

• Corporate headquarters in Atlanta, GA with team members working in over 250 plants throughout North America.

OUR MISSION:

We protect the food supply by eliminating risks so families everywhere can eat without fear.

  • Protect What Matters:We are in service of safety at every step, ensuring the health of everyone is central to all we do – from plant team members to consumers.
  • Deliver On Our Promises: We speak honestly and are dedicated to doing the right thing by upholding ethical standards and following through on our commitments to our teams, our customers, and our business.

  • Advance a Safer Future: We are committed to innovating more effective, sustainable, and cost-efficient food safety solutions to develop a safer world for all.
JOB DESCRIPTION

This role goes beyond traditional HR reporting. You will build the data infrastructure and AI-assisted workflows that empower HR, Safety, and Compliance leaders ask better questions and get faster, more trustworthy answers. Job duties include but are not limited to:

  • AI-Augmented Analysis:Use Claude and other AI tools to accelerate exploratory, draft and refine SQL/queries, identify trends across HRIS and workforce datasets, and validate findings before they reach leadership. Treat AI as a thinking partner that extends your perspective and capabilities, not a shortcut that replaces sound judgment.
  • Workflow & Automation Design: Identify repetitive, manual reporting processes and redesign them as automated, sustainable workflows — reducing turnaround time and freeing capacity for higher-value analysis. Build with reusability in mind so workflows outlast any single request.
  • Insight Engines, Not Just Reports:Move past static reporting toward systems that surface trends, anomalies, and "why" behind the numbers — proactively flagging issues in employee engagement, turnover, safety compliance, and workforce planning before they're asked about.
  • Data Integrity and Management:Ensure accuracy, consistency, and completeness of HR data across HRIS, people management systems, and adjacent platforms. Conduct regular audits and build automated checks to catch discrepancies early.
  • Dashboards Built to Last:Design clear, visually compelling, and low-maintenance dashboards and reports (Power BI, Tableau, Excel, and AI-assisted tooling) that non-technical stakeholders can actually use — and that don't break the moment a data source shifts.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration:Partner with HR, Compliance, Safety, Operations, Finance, and IT to understand reporting needs, align metrics to organizational goals, and translate ambiguous questions into concrete, buildable deliverables.
  • Continuous Improvement:Identify smarter ways to collect, model, and communicate data, and take ownership of implementing those improvements rather than just flagging them.
  • Special Projects: Contribute to experimental or exploratory initiatives — new metrics, predictive models, or AI tools — as assigned by leadership.


YOUR MUST HAVES:

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Analytics, Statistics, Data Science, or a related field.
  • Proficiency in HRIS platforms and reporting/BI tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau, Excel, SQL).
  • Demonstrated comfort using AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) to support analysis, automate workflows, or accelerate reporting — and the judgment to know when to trust, verify, or override them.
  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret complex, sometimes messy data sets and translate findings into actionable insights.
  • A builder's mindset: you'd rather design a repeatable workflow than repeat manual work.
  • Genuine curiosity — you dig into anomalies instead of smoothing them over — paired with the creativity to present insights in ways that land with non-technical audiences.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills to convey insights effectively to HR, Safety, and Compliance leadership.
  • Knowledge of HR metrics, workforce analytics, and compliance reporting.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and work collaboratively across cross-functional teams.
  • High attention to detail and an unwavering commitment to data accuracy.

WHAT WE PREFER YOU HAVE:

  • Hands-on experience designing AI-assisted or automated reporting workflows (e.g., using Claude, Python, or low-code automation tools) in an HR or People Analytics context.
  • 3 or more years of related experience.
  • Experience with predictive analytics and HR data modeling.

jobs.excerpt: Collectors is the leading creator of innovative technology that provides value-added services for collectors worldwide.
jobs.description:
Collectors is the leading creator of innovative technology that provides value-added services for collectors worldwide. We grade, authenticate, vault, and sell millions of record-setting collectibles, all while modernizing and digitalizing the process to further our mission of helping collectors pursue their passions. We’re always on the lookout for talented people to join our growing team.


Our services span collectible trading cards, autographs, comic books, coins, video games, event tickets, and memorabilia. Our subsidiaries include PSA, PCGS, Beckett, SGC, and Card Ladder.


Since our founding in 1986, we have graded and authenticated millions of items. We employ more than 3000 people across our headquarters in Santa Ana, California and offices in New Jersey, Texas, Florida, Japan, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Canada, Mexico, Germany, the UK, and France.


As part of our interview process, we request that candidates have their cameras on during video interviews. This helps foster meaningful conversation and allows us to create an experience that closely resembles our standard working environment. Certain interview steps may take place by phone. For remote roles, and at our discretion, candidates may be asked to participate in an on-site interview as part of the final stages of the process.


We understand there may be occasional circumstances requiring accommodation and are happy to discuss them as needed. Your recruiter will be able to clarify expectations and answer any questions you have.


We’re transforming the collecting experience with technology that brings authentication, grading, and trading into the modern era. Our products are equalizing the playing field by providing tools that make complex research analytics — including pricing, scarcity reports, and historic sales data — accessible to every collector, old or new. Our engineering mission is to democratize technology while promoting innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning throughout the organization. We're seeking engineers to utilize advanced technology in agile settings, with a focus on improving the customer experience for every collector.


Collectors Cybersecurity team is committed to utilize cybersecurity, risk and privacy best practices on our platforms, leveraging signal intelligence and observability at scale to protect our customers, employees and our brand.


We’re looking for a Security Operations Engineer to join our Cybersecurity team to partner with the broader Product and Tech org and drive secure by default architectures and ensure the security and integrity of our infrastructure.

You’ll join our Cybersecurity Team and work from our Santa Ana, CA office. Remote or hybrid candidates will also be considered. We believe that there is significant value in in-person collaboration. If you live within a 1 hour commuting distance to one of our offices, you will be required to be onsite most of the time. This will be discussed further as part of the recruiting process.



What You’ll Do:



  • Drive Detection Engineering: Build, tune and manage high-confidence detections across cloud platforms (AWS/GCP), enterprise tooling (Okta, GWS, M365) and vendor products. Treat detections as code: version controlled, peer reviewed, tested in CI, and measured for precision and coverage against MITRE ATT&CK.
  • Incident Command and Containment: Serve as a senior responder for security incidents, driving triage, containment, forensics, and remediation, and authoring post-incident reviews that turn lessons into durable improvements.
  • Threat Hunting: Conduct proactive threat hunts across cloud, SaaS, identity and on-prem infrastructure, converting hypotheses and findings into new detections and hardened controls.
  • Tooling and Response Automation: Design and build automation and SOAR playbooks that reduce manual toil, accelerate response times, and improve alert enrichment and case management.
  • Security Telemetry: Own and improve the health of the security data pipeline: log source onboarding, parser and schema quality, coverage gap analysis, and data quality for data sources across our cloud, SaaS and on-prem environment.
  • Automated Analysis and Secure Frameworks: Scale security efforts by integrating automation for the identification, prioritization, and remediation of vulnerabilities
  • Partner cross-functionally with infrastructure, platform, and engineering teams to embed security operations requirements into new services and cloud architecture decisions.
  • Lead by example and be a champion of all company policies, including safety, attendance & security
  • Participate in a shared on-call rotation, and continuously improve runbooks, escalation paths, and alert quality to make on-call sustainable for the whole team.



Who You Are:



  • 5+ years in security operations, incident response, or detection engineering, with at least 2 years operating in a cloud-native environment at a senior level.
  • Deep hands-on experience securing AWS at scale (IAM, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Security Hub, EC2/EKS/Lambda) in a multi-account organization; familiarity with GCP or Azure is a plus.
  • Strong SIEM proficiency - you've built and tuned detections, written complex queries, and managed log pipelines, not just consumed alerts.
  • Proficiency in one or more general purpose programming/script languages, preferably Python, and comfortable building automation, integrations, and SOAR playbooks from scratch.
  • A seasoned incident responder who stays calm under pressure, communicates clearly with technical and executive audiences, and leads without needing formal authority.
  • Grounded in attacker tradecraft - you think in terms of MITRE ATT&CK, understand cloud-specific attack paths, and use that lens to prioritize work.
  • Experienced working across team boundaries: influencing engineering roadmaps, negotiating with vendors, and representing security operations in cross-functional forums.
  • Pragmatic and outcome-driven - you balance ideal security posture against operational reality and know when good enough today beats perfect next quarter.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and handle multiple tasks
  • Familiarity with major compliance frameworks, such as PCI, NIST, ISO, SOX, and experience assisting in audits

Salary Range:The salary range for this position is $140,971- $228,870. Actual compensation on this range varies based on a variety of non-discriminatory factors, including location, job level, experience, and skill set. jobs.description:
About the Role

We are hiring a Manager, Cloud Platform Engineers to lead our India-based platform and automation engineering staff. This is a people-management role with real technical ownership -- you will be evaluated as much on your ability to review and stand behind your team's Kubernetes and Terraform work as on how you manage the people producing it. You will oversee day-to-day execution of AKS operations and Terraform-based automation, working in close coordination with the US-based Principal and Expert Platform Engineers who set the platform's architectural direction.

This role exists to provide direct, hands-on management and accurate technical oversight of the India-based team -- including work planning, prioritization, quality review, and status reporting to the Senior Manager, Cloud Platform. Reporting must reflect verified, actual system state; this is a core expectation of the role, not a formality.


What You'll Do

  • Directly manage India-based Cloud Platform engineers, including workload assignment, prioritization, and day-to-day people management.
  • Review and stand behind your team's Terraform module submissions and AKS configuration changes for correctness, adherence to documented standards, and production-readiness before they are considered complete.
  • Enforce engineering process standards across the team: issue-based work tracking, triage and prioritization before work begins, work-in-progress limits, and daily status updates.
  • Provide the Senior Manager, Cloud Platform with accurate, verified status reporting on the India-based team's work -- cross-checked against actual system and repository state, not summarized from memory or secondhand updates.
  • Coordinate with the Principal and Expert Platform Engineers on platform architecture and standards, ensuring the India-based team's work aligns with the broader platform's GitOps, Terraform, and AKS conventions.
  • Escalate technical or delivery risks early and directly, rather than allowing status to be discovered after the fact.
  • Support hiring, onboarding, and skill development for the India-based team, including closing gaps in Kubernetes, Terraform, and CI/CD fundamentals where needed.
  • Apply policy-as-code and security standards already established on the platform (Kyverno or equivalent) when reviewing team output.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years in platform, infrastructure, or site reliability engineering roles, including some prior people-management or formal technical-lead experience.
  • Hands-on production experience with Kubernetes, ideally AKS specifically -- sufficient to personally review a team member's cluster or workload change and identify problems.
  • Working Terraform experience, including the ability to review a submitted module for correctness, reusability, and adherence to documented standards.
  • GitOps experience (ArgoCD, Flux, or equivalent) -- all infrastructure and cluster changes should trace to a git commit as a matter of practice, not preference.
  • Demonstrated ability to produce accurate, verifiable status reporting to senior leadership.
  • Experience managing engineers directly, including performance management, prioritization, and workload planning.
  • Working fluency in policy-as-code tooling (Kyverno, OPA/Gatekeeper, or equivalent).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience managing a distributed or offshore engineering team reporting to a manager in a different region.
  • Practical, current experience using AI-assisted development tools in daily engineering work.
  • Experience with observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, Thanos, or equivalent).
  • Background modernizing legacy automation (PowerShell or similar) toward Terraform or platform-native replacements.

Job Description:

We are Omnissa! 

Omnissa is the first AI-driven digital work platform, built to support flexible, secure, work-from anywhere experiences. We integrate industry-leading solutions —including Unified Endpoint Management, Windows Modern Management, Virtual Apps and Desktops, Digital Employee Experience, and Security & Compliance— into a seamless, autonomous workspace that adapts to how people work. Our platform boosts employee engagement while optimizing IT operations, security, and cost.

Guided by our Core Values—Act in Alignment, Build Trust, Foster Inclusiveness, Drive Efficiency, and Maximize Customer Value—we’re growing rapidly and committed to delivering meaningful impact. If you're passionate about shaping the future of work, we’d love to hear from you.

What is the opportunity?


At Omnissa, we are committed to maintaining a fair, consistent, and secure hiring process for all candidates. As part of this approach, we use standard interview and verification practices designed to ensure alignment and protect both candidates and the organization. These practices are applied thoughtfully and with respect for candidate privacy.

As a Professional Services Senior Architect, you will be responsible for leading the implementation and championing the adoption of solutions purchased by our most important and largest customers daily. You will gather and analyze customer requirements to create an architectural design consisting of compute infrastructure planning (private and public cloud), recommending and planning configurations, validating deployment, enhancing operations strategy, and increasing user adoption. You will serve as a trusted advisor to our customers, developing an intimate knowledge of their business and strategic goals and use your in-depth knowledge of the Omnissa Workspace ONE Platform to work with customers on building successful implementation and adoption roadmaps and driving the vision to completion.

You will have opportunities to solve customers’ challenges and deliver secure digital workspaces with Omnissa Workspace ONE while being a part of a team of overachievers, highly successful individuals. Here is a breakdown:

  • During your first month, you will work with a mentor and your peers to gain familiarity with our internal processes. In the context of customer engagements, they will help you gain insight and experience to ensure the solution being delivered is fit for purpose through referencing the initial business goals and objectives, demonstrating commercial and scope awareness, and understanding the wider technical landscape and how it relates to/integrates with customer environments.
  • Your manager, mentor, and peers will help you gain access to other important internal stakeholders to help you establish your network of contacts across different Omnissa business units to make you successful.
  • Within your first three months, you will be expected to take full ownership of business outcomes, lead technical project teams, and take accountability for all project deliverables—further developing your leadership, technical, and business process skills.
  • Following onboarding, you will transition into one or many customer engagements, depending on business need. As an Omnissa Professional Services Senior Architect, you will lead the implementation and adoption activities of Omnissa Workspace ONE solutions for our customers. By combining your unique leadership skills with your technical acumen, you will lead our customers to achieving their business goals. You won’t do it alone: You will always have the help of your team as you progress and develop your skills.
  • You will use your in-depth knowledge of Omnissa and adjacent products to become a trusted advisor to your customers and colleagues. Your passion for technology makes you uniquely capable of earning and maintaining subject-matter expertise in the innovative field of end-user computing.

What will you bring to Omnissa?

  • This is a consulting position where you will be using technical, consulting, business, and leadership skills. You will work directly with our customers and other Omnissa employees on the day-to-day activities involved with the post-sales implementation of Omnissa Workspace ONE. You will articulate solution designs, integrating both technical and business concepts, and present a transformational journey to project stakeholders. Was uns ausmacht

3A ist eine führende Unternehmensberatung für die Versicherungsbranche. Als partnergeführtes Team verbinden wir Stabilität mit der Flexibilität und Kreativität moderner Beratung.

Unsere Kultur lebt von Offenheit, Vertrauen und dem Mut, neue Wege zu gehen. Mit Strategie, Ideenreichtum und Teamgeist treiben wir interdisziplinäre Projekte voran und erzielen partnerschaftlich messbare Erfolge. Wir arbeiten nach den Standards des „Erfolgsfaktor Familie“ und unterstützen Dich dabei, Beruf und persönliche Lebensphasen zu vereinen. Bei uns profitierst Du von hoher Selbstorganisation, individueller Weiterentwicklung und flexiblem Homeoffice.

Warum eine Initiativbewerbung bei 3A?

Du möchtest die Versicherungsbranche aktiv mitgestalten, Verantwortung übernehmen und Deine Expertise in anspruchsvolle Projekte einbringen? Auch wenn aktuell keine Stelle exakt zu Deinem Profil ausgeschrieben ist, sind wir immer offen für engagierte Persönlichkeiten, die fachlich wie menschlich zu uns passen.

Ob Prozessberatung, Digitalisierung, strategische Konzepte oder Projektleitung: Wir freuen uns über Initiativbewerbungen von Beratern, die gemeinsam mit uns wachsen möchten.

Aufgaben

– je nach Profil:

In Beratungsprojekten:

  • Prozess- und Organisationsberatung:
    Du analysierst, optimierst und implementierst Geschäftsprozesse in der Versicherungswirtschaft. Dabei liegt Dein Fokus auf Digitalisierung, Automatisierung, Customer Experience, Workflow-Optimierung und der Einführung agiler Organisationsstrukturen.
  • Eigenverantwortliche Projektleitung:
    Du übernimmst die Leitung von Projekten oder Teilprojekten, steuerst Zeitpläne, Qualität und Budget und sorgst dafür, dass Ergebnisse zuverlässig umgesetzt werden.
  • Strategische Beratung:
    Du begleitest unsere Kunden bei der Entwicklung zukunftsweisender Konzepte, die ihre Geschäftsmodelle stärken und langfristigen Erfolg sichern.

Intern bei 3A:

  • Innovations- und Geschäftsentwicklung:
    Du entwickelst innovative Lösungen, identifizierst neue Chancen und gestaltest aktiv unser Beratungsportfolio mit, um unsere Kunden zukunftsorientiert zu unterstützen.
  • Netzwerkpflege:
    Du baust nachhaltige Beziehungen zu Kunden, Partnern und internen Stakeholdern auf und pflegst Dein berufliches Netzwerk langfristig.
  • Interne Mitwirkung:
    Du bringst Dich aktiv in interne Entscheidungsprozesse ein und unterstützt das Team bei strategischen, organisatorischen und operativen Themen.

Qualifikation

  • Ausbildung & Studium:
    Du hast eine Ausbildung als Versicherungskaufmann/-frau abgeschlossen und/oder ein Studium mit Bezug zur Versicherungswirtschaft, z. B. in Versicherungswesen, BWL, Wirtschaftsinformatik, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen oder vergleichbar.
  • Berufserfahrung:
    Du verfügst über mehrjährige Erfahrung im Versicherungsumfeld, idealerweise in Unternehmensberatung, Projektleitung oder Transformationsprojekten.
  • Fachliche Kompetenz:
    Du verstehst Versicherungsprozesse, hast ein Gespür für Effizienzsteigerung und Digitalisierung und bringst Kenntnisse in Geschäftsprozessmanagement oder verwandten Methoden mit.
  • Selbstständigkeit & Eigeninitiative:
    Du arbeitest strukturiert und eigenverantwortlich, übernimmst Verantwortung und bringst eigene Ideen aktiv ein.
  • Empathie & Beratungskompetenz:
    Du berätst partnerschaftlich auf Augenhöhe, erkennst Kundenbedürfnisse und baust vertrauensvolle Beziehungen auf.
  • Teamfähigkeit & Verantwortung:
    Du arbeitest gerne im Team, genießt Gestaltungsspielraum und übernimmst Verantwortung für Deine Projekte und Ergebnisse.
  • Digitale Kompetenz:
    Du bist sicher im Umgang mit MS Office sowie digitalen Tools für Projektmanagement und Präsentationen.
  • Flexibilität & Mobilität:
    Du bist bereit, bei Bedarf zu Kunden zu reisen und schätzt die Möglichkeit bis zu 100% remote zu arbeiten.

Benefits

  • Flexibles Arbeiten: Arbeite genau dort, wo Du am produktivsten bist. Ob im Homeoffice, unterwegs oder zeitweise im europäischen Ausland. Teilzeitmodelle sind ebenfalls möglich.
  • Freizeit & Erholung: Genieße 30 Tage Urlaub plus zusätzliche freie Tage und Sonderurlaub für besondere Anlässe. Und wenn Du länger auftanken möchtest, stehen Dir Sabbatical- und Workation-Möglichkeiten offen.
  • Teamkultur: Dich erwartet eine offene, herzliche Atmosphäre mit regelmäßigen Teamevents, After-Work-Angeboten und gemeinsamen Aktivitäten mit Kollegen und Familie.
  • Individuelle Weiterentwicklung: Wir fördern Deinen persönlichen und fachlichen Wachstumspfad mit maßgeschneiderten Trainings, Mentoring und klaren Entwicklungsperspektiven.
  • Work-Life-Balance: Beruf und Familie lassen sich bei uns gut vereinbaren. Wir bieten ein Umfeld, in dem persönliche Belange ernst genommen werden.
  • Gesundheit & Wohlbefinden: Bleib fit und ausgeglichen mit unserem vielfältigen Angebot für körperliches und mentales Wohlbefinden. Wir unterstützen Dich mit Programmen wie EGYM Wellpass.
  • Mobilität & Extras: Profitiere von flexibler Mobilität mit JobRad-Leasing und attraktiven Zusatzleistungen von Corporate Benefits.
  • Vorsorge: Mit betrieblicher Altersvorsorge, Gruppenunfallversicherung und weiteren Schutzleistungen bist Du langfristig bestens abgesichert.

Dein nächster Schritt

Du hast Lust, Deine Erfahrung einzubringen und gemeinsam mit uns die Zukunft der Versicherungsbranche zu gestalten?

Dann freuen wir uns auf Deine Initiativbewerbung und darauf, Dich kennenzulernen.

At Omnissa, you will have the opportunity to make a significant impact while working alongside a global community of passionate professionals shaping the future of digital work. Every day is different as you build strategic relationships, advocate for customers, and collaborate across Sales, Support, Product, Engineering, Professional Services, and Renewals teams.

    • Build strategic relationships with business decision makers and executive stakeholders.

Retention & Growth

What is the leadership like for this role? What is the structure and culture of the team like?


The EUC Customer Success team is focused on outcomes, not activity. We help customers realize tangible business value from their Omnissa investments while building long-term strategic partnerships. We are customer-obsessed, collaborative, innovative, and committed to continuous improvement. We share best practices openly, support one another’s development, and believe that when our customers succeed, we succeed. Our Workday Extend team is small, agile, and growing at light speed. We don’t just "configure" Workday—we treat it as a development platform. Key Technical Focus Areas:

  • App Development: Build custom apps using the Workday Extend framework, managing the full lifecycle from App Hub configuration to production deployment.

  • Orchestration: Design and build complex, event-driven Workday Orchestrations to sync data across Workday and third-party systems (using the Orchestration Builder drag-and-drop tool).

  • UI/UX Design: Craft intuitive user experiences using Page Builder, ensuring a "Workday-native" look and feel for every custom task.

  • Advanced Logic: Utilize Workday Query Language (WQL) and REST/SOAP APIs to pull, push, and transform data with precision.

  • Design & Prototype: Translate complex business requirements into technical blueprints including UI flows, security domains, and data models.

  • Full-Stack Extend Delivery: Independently build, test, and deploy applications, ensuring they are "update-safe" and maintainable.

Qualifications

We have trained our engineering team to be able to cope with interesting, complex and diverse technical issues from small companies though to large enterprise corporations.

Everything’s on the menu at Wonder. Except compromise.

About The Opportunity
We are seeking a Market People Leader ("aka" Regional HR Business Partner), to work strategically with our Regional Vice Presidents, Market Operations Directors, and multi-unit field leadership teams across a multi-state footprint. As a senior individual contributor, you will translate the field’s people strategy into actionable, data-informed programs and initiatives—designing and deploying solutions that elevate leadership capability, address root causes, and scale effectively across regions.

The Market People Leader will operate across a large and complex hourly and salaried workforce environment. They will be deeply embedded with field leadership—supporting strategic planning, diagnosing organizational opportunities, creating scalable interventions, and executing project-based and tactical people initiatives. The ideal candidate brings significant multi-unit HRBP experience within QSR, food & beverage, hospitality, or retail and excels at balancing strategic influence with hands-on execution.

The Impact You Will Make

Strategic Leadership & Business Partnership

  • Serve as the primary strategic HR partner to Regional Vice Presidents and Market Operations Directors across multiple markets.

  • Recommend, translate, and execute people initiatives aligned with operational goals, including workforce planning, leadership capability, retention, and culture.

  • Anticipate emerging needs and challenges, proactively offering solutions—not just surfacing issues.

  • Use data, trends, and insights to inform decisions and create interventions that scale across regions and store formats.

  • Lead with a high level of independence, navigating ambiguity while influencing leadership toward optimal people decisions.

  • Influence leaders toward effective, long-term people decisions through strong judgment, business acumen, and operational understanding.

Strategic + Tactical Execution & Field Enablement

  • Operate with end-to-end ownership, shifting fluidly between strategic planning, project execution, and tactical tasks that support daily operations.

  • Drive and support enterprise initiatives (performance cycles, compensation reviews, org design changes, HR system launches) while ensuring field execution and adoption.

  • Build repeatable, scalable processes that reduce manual lift for stores and improve consistency across regions.

  • Establish rhythms, standards, and operating mechanisms that ensure consistency of HR support across regions.

Organizational Effectiveness & Workforce Strategy

  • Diagnose root causes of operational and people challenges such as turnover, staffing models, leadership gaps, and team effectiveness, and develop targeted, scalable solutions to address them.

  • Partner with field leaders to design and execute workforce plans that support current and future business needs, including staffing strategies, labor optimization, performance management, and leadership bench development.

  • Implement interventions that improve operational readiness, strengthen leadership performance, and reinforce long-term organizational health across markets.

  • Use analytical and dashboards to generate insights and make data-backed recommendations that enhance workflows, shift behaviors, and influence long-term strategy.

Employee Relations & Culture Stewardship

  • Serve as the escalation point for complex employee relations matters across multiple districts.

  • Guide leaders in consistent application of policies, values, and leadership behaviors.

  • Shape and reinforce programs that enhance engagement, build teamwork, and reduce avoidable employee friction.

Talent Development & Leadership Capability

  • Partner with Talent Acquisition on hiring strategies, forecasting, and capability planning for leaders and hourly teams.

  • Support and influence leadership development, succession planning, career pathing, and bench readiness for multi-unit operations.

  • Coach leaders to elevate their decision-making, communication, and team leadership effectiveness.

HR Operations, Compliance, & Risk Management

  • Ensure all practices comply with federal, state, and local requirements across a growing multi-state footprint.

  • Partner cross-functionally to ensure strong execution of core HR programs including benefits, compensation, accommodations, investigations, and performance cycles.

  • Apply strong risk judgment to protect the business while maintaining trust and fairness across teams.

Change Management & Continuous Improvement

  • Lead people-related components of change tied to new market expansion, org design shifts, process improvements, or structural realignments.

  • Diagnose operational inefficiencies and create scalable HR processes that support growth and reduce complexity for leaders.

  • Influence field adoption of new tools, systems, and workflows through clear communication and partnership.

​

What You Bring to the Table

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or related field.

  • 8+ years of progressive HRBP experience, with significant time supporting multi-unit operations in QSR, food & beverage, hospitality, or retail.

  • Demonstrated ability to translate people strategy into scalable, effective initiatives that drive meaningful business outcomes.

  • Proven experience operating as a senior-level individual contributor with strong cross-functional influence.

  • Exceptional ability to anticipate needs, diagnose problems, and drive solutions that scale.

  • Strong analytical mindset with the ability to interpret trends and turn insights into action.

  • Knowledge of employment laws and compliance considerations across multiple states.

  • Excellent communication, relationship-building, and influencing skills with leaders at all levels.

  • Comfort working in a fast-paced, high-growth environment with competing priorities and continuously evolving structures, processes, and practices.

As a matter of company policy, Wonder does not sponsor applicants for employment visa status for this role.

United States: $115,00 - $143,00 per year.

Wonder uses geographic-specific salary structures, which means the salary offered may vary depending on where the job is located. The final salary offer will take into account various factors, such as the candidate's skills, education, training, credentials, and experience.

We also offer a choice of medical, dental, and vision plans, company paid short and long term disability coverage, paid time off including flexible time off for exempt employees, paid vacation for non-exempt employees, and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable law in addition to paid parental leave, discounted meals and exclusive perks across the Wonder family of brands.

jobs.description:
Marathon Health is a leading advanced primary care provider, partnering with employer and union plan sponsors to improve health for millions of Americans. With nationwide onsite, nearsite, and network health centers, and virtual primary care, Marathon delivers a value-based model that enhances the healthcare experience for members and providers, while driving meaningful cost savings for plan sponsors. Marathon is proud to be certified as a Great Place to Work®, reflecting the company's commitment to building an inclusive, high-trust culture where all employees can thrive. Learn more at

ABOUT THE JOB

The Data Product Owner leads several cross-functional scrum teams responsible for delivering outcome-based data solutions to the business. This role is defined by the problems it solves, not the technology it uses. Whether the right answer is a Tableau dashboard, a Snowflake Cortex agent, a Python-based insight package delivered as a Streamlit portal, or a reusable component of our semantic model, the Data Product Owner is accountable for choosing the approach that best achieves the desired outcome and for guiding their teams to build it.


Our stakeholders are primarily internal, though some solutions serve external audiences, and their needs evolve quickly. This person must be comfortable operating in an environment where both Technology and Product direction change, treating that change as a normal condition rather than a disruption. A major part of the mandate is enablement: building the foundational pieces — starting with a well-structured semantic model — that let stakeholders and teams across the organization build their own solutions, inside and outside of Technology. The ideal candidate is fluent in leveraging AI to accelerate how these solutions get designed, built, and maintained.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own the product vision, roadmap, and prioritized backlog for a portfolio of outcome-based data solutions serving internal and external stakeholders.
  • Lead multiple scrum teams day to day — including backlog grooming, sprint planning, prioritization, and removing blockers — while keeping teams focused on measurable outcomes over outputs.
  • Take direction from the Director of Business Intelligence on analytics and reporting outcomes, and from the Technical Product Manager on technical and product execution, reconciling their input into a single prioritized backlog.
  • Proactively surface conflicts in priority or direction early, and drive them to resolution rather than letting teams stall.
  • Translate stakeholder goals into clearly defined problems, success metrics, and acceptance criteria, and validate that delivered solutions actually move those metrics.
  • Select the right delivery approach for each problem (e.g., Tableau, Snowflake / Cortex agents, Python / Streamlit portals) based on the outcome and the audience, rather than defaulting to a preferred technology or pattern.
  • Leverage AI and modern tooling to accelerate discovery, prototyping, development, and iteration across the teams.
  • Build and steward foundational, reusable components — especially the semantic model — so that stakeholders and other teams can reliably build their own solutions against a trusted, governed layer.
  • Establish and support self-service enablement, including documentation, patterns, and guardrails, so users can create their own solutions with confidence.
  • Partner closely with Product leaders and internal stakeholders who depend on these solutions, keeping all parties aligned on priorities, tradeoffs, and delivery status.
  • Anticipate and absorb change from both Technology and Product, adjusting priorities and communicating impacts without losing delivery momentum.
  • Ensure solutions meet quality, security, and compliance expectations appropriate to internal and external use.
  • Track adoption, usage, and business impact, and use those insights to continuously refine the portfolio.
  • Define success metrics and business outcomes for all major initiatives and hold teams accountable for measuring realized value after delivery.
  • Ensure solutions follow established release, change management, and production readiness processes.

QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's degree in a relevant field plus a minimum of 7 years proven experience as a Product Owner, Product Manager, or similar role delivering data, analytics, or BI products, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Demonstrated success leading Agile / Scrum teams, ideally more than one team concurrently. Strong background in data and analytics, with the ability to reason about data products end to end (source to consumption). Experience in healthcare, population health, benefits administration, or related regulated industries preferred. Experience working with data governance, data quality, and master data initiatives preferred.


DESIRED ATTRIBUTES

  • Hands-on familiarity with Snowflake, including Cortex agents, Cortex Analyst / search services, and semantic views.
  • Experience with modern analytics and delivery tools such as Tableau, Python, and Streamlit (or comparable frameworks for building lightweight portals and insight packages).
  • Practical fluency in leveraging AI / LLMs to build, accelerate, or augment data solutions.
  • Strong grasp of semantic modeling and the value of a reusable, governed foundation that enables self-service.
  • An outcome-first, technology-agnostic mindset: chooses the right tool for the job and lets go of tools that no longer fit.
  • Highly adaptable and calm amid shifting Technology and Product priorities.
  • Diplomatic and decisive: builds trust with multiple stakeholders and makes clear prioritization calls when direction conflicts.
  • A builder-and-enabler orientation: as motivated by helping others create solutions as by delivering their own.
  • Curiosity and a habit of continuous learning as the tooling landscape evolves.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, comfortable working with both Product leadership and non-technical business users.
  • Experience managing product backlogs in Azure DevOps or similar tools.
  • Awareness of data governance, security, and privacy considerations (experience handling sensitive or regulated data such as PHI is a plus).
  • Comfort selecting and working across a range of delivery technologies rather than specializing in a single one.
  • Experience operating in an environment of frequent change and ambiguity.
  • Track record of translating business needs into prioritized, outcome-driven work and measuring results.
  • Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in a matrixed structure, taking direction from multiple leaders while managing competing priorities.

Pay Range: $110,000 - $140,000/yr

The actual offer may vary dependent upon geographic location and the candidate’s years of experience and/or skill level.

Computational biology intern

The intern will assess and integrate methods in a workflow for peptide substrate that includes de novo generation, evaluation of biophysical characteristics (charge, hydrophobicity, epitope prediction) as well as ranking and final selection for wet lab generation.

jobs.description:
About Blackbird Health

Blackbird Health is clinician-founded, owned, and operated by dedicated professionals. We believe that providing the best care for children starts with building the best possible team. We deliver virtual and in-person mental health services across Pennsylvania, Virginia, New Jersey & Maryland—and we’re growing into new markets in 2027.

At Blackbird, we take a whole-child approach, looking at how the brain, body, and behavior interact to address the root causes of challenges, not just the symptoms. Every role matters here, and you’ll join a collaborative, supportive, and innovative team that’s shaping the future of pediatric mental health care. If you’re passionate about helping children and families while growing your career, Blackbird is the place to make an impact.

Join us and help change mental health care for children for the better!

Position Summary

As a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP) at Blackbird Health, you’ll play an essential role in delivering high-quality, comprehensive psychiatric evaluations, treatment planning, and medication management for children, adolescents, and young adults. You’ll build meaningful relationships with patients and families, taking the time to understand their needs, support engagement in treatment, and educate them on care options that foster long-term progress.

Working alongside an interdisciplinary team of psychotherapists, specialists, and clinical leaders, you’ll be empowered to make a tangible difference in the lives of young patients and their families through compassionate, evidence-based care.

We’re seeking dedicated prescribers to join our team and serve children, adolescents, and young adults ages 2–26. Multiple remote employment tracks are available: you’ll select your preferred arrangement in the application.

Employment Options

W2 Full-Time (FTE) | PMHNP

  • Compensation:
    • Base Salary: $135,000 – $145,000 base salary.
  • Hours & Schedule:
    • Workload: Fully remote position with a commitment supporting completed clinical direct care hours.
    • Commitment: 34 clinical direct-care hours per week.
    • Core Hours: Minimum commitment during peak "after school" core windows (after 4:00 PM ET weekdays and/or weekends).
  • Full Benefits Package: Medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match, employer-paid life insurance, generous paid time off + 11 paid holidays, and professional liability insurance coverage.

W2 Part-Time (20 hrs/week) | PMHNP

  • Compensation:
    • Base Salary: $72,500 base salary for part-time schedule.
    • Incentive Pay: Earn $100 per completed clinical hour for additional sessions beyond your base caseload.
  • Hours & Onsite Expectations:
    • Commitment: 20 contracted hours per week (17 clinical direct-care hours).
    • Core Schedule: Minimum 15 hours anchored in peak core windows (after 3:00 PM ET weekdays and/or weekends).
  • Benefits: Full benefits package including medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with match, generous PTO + 11 paid holidays, paid weekly clinical consultation, and covered liability insurance.

1099 Contractor | PMHNP

  • Compensation (Flat-Rate VA):
    • Hourly Pay: $120.00 flat rate per completed clinical hour.
  • Hours & Flexibility:
    • Minimum Commitment: 15 open patient-care hours/week to support a target baseline of 12 completed clinical hours/week.
    • Core Requirement: Hours anchored during peak core windows (after 3:00 PM ET weekdays and/or weekends).
  • Perks: Full credentialing support, paid weekly clinical consultation, liability insurance covered, and reimbursement for client no-shows.

Why Blackbird & Your Impact

  • Focus on Patient Care: Full administrative support—we handle credentialing, billing, insurance, and EHR administration so you can focus entirely on your clinical work.
  • Guaranteed Patient Referrals: Start seeing patients right away with a predictable caseload.
  • Grow as a Clinician: Paid weekly clinical consultation and peer support are built into your schedule for ongoing skill development.
  • Integrated Care Model: Work closely alongside psychotherapists, speech therapists, OTs, and neuropsychology specialists to treat the whole child.
  • Mission-Driven Culture: Join a collaborative, intelligent, and compassionate network of professionals shaping the future of pediatric behavioral health.

Who You Are

  • Licensure: Active Virginia PMHNP/CRNP/APN license, active DEA registration, and State Prescriptive Authority.
  • Certification: Board Certified by ANCC or AANP (PMHNP-BC).
  • Education: Master’s Degree from an accredited nursing program.
  • Experience: 1+ years of independent psychiatric experience working under licensure (with direct experience serving children, adolescents, or young adults).
  • Availability: Available during Blackbird's peak core hours (after 3:00 PM ET weekdays and/or weekends).
  • Technical Skills: Tech-savvy and equipped with a computer, phone, high-speed internet, and proficiency in EHR systems and Google Suite.
Salary Range
$72,500—$160,000 USD

Join us!

To raise the standard of pediatric mental health care through accurate understanding and precise treatment that reflect how each child’s brain, body, and behavior work together.

“It's so rare to find comprehensive care like this---from testing to therapy to med management (and more)--all in one place. In addition, the school advocacy support we receive is unprecedented. We no longer feel like we are managing things alone.”

Fostering an inclusive environment:

Blackbird is committed to cultivating and preserving a culture of inclusion and belonging. We are able to grow and learn better together with a diverse team of employees. Imagine yourself…

  • Owning your ambition and fueling your career growth.
  • Joining a company with a proven track record of success and an exciting future.
  • Collaborating with a vibrant, inclusive, global team.

It's all possible with a role at ​Esko​. Esko, a ​Veralto​ company, is a global provider of integrated software and hardware solutions that accelerate the go-to-market process of packaged goods. Our integrated platform and comprehensive tools empower retailers, pre-media and trade shops, manufacturers, and converters to manage best-in-class packaging design and print processes.

Innovation is built into the DNA of our business: every day, we challenge ourselves to be better by seeking out new ways to elevate our products, our processes, and our people.

We also know that innovation and ingenuity starts with prioritizing a diverse workforce and a deeply inclusive workplace. We encourage people from all backgrounds to apply to our positions.

Learn about our leading portfolio of innovative products:


About the Role


Reporting to the Director of Sales, the Account Executive, Mid-Market Pharma & Life Sciences is responsible for winning new mid-sized pharmaceutical and life-sciences customers for Esko's validated brand software, starting with WebCenter Go. This is a newly created role in a growing segment, with real ownership in shaping how we win in this market. You'll own the full sales cycle, from prospecting and discovery through solution design and close, focusing primarily on net-new revenue while identifying selective expansion opportunities within a small set of assigned accounts. You'll help pharmaceutical companies improve how they manage packaging artwork, labeling, review, approval, compliance and go-to-market workflows, delivering greater control, speed to market and measurable business impact. Working closely with Solutions Consulting, Product, Validation, Marketing and Customer Success, you'll translate regulated business requirements into practical outcomes and position validated software as a scalable solution for mid-sized life-sciences organizations, while growing your career within a global technology company where innovation is embedded in everything we do.


This is a fully remote role and will be located in the United States, within the Eastern or Central time zone (East Coast preferred).

What You'll Do

In this role, you will:

  • Own mid market pharma and life sciences segment, managing a healthy pipeline and achieving quarterly and annual revenue targets.
  • Drive the full sales cycle from outbound prospecting and qualification through discovery, demonstration, proposal, negotiation, and close. This is a hands-on hunter role with primary responsibility for winning new customers.
  • Build trusted advisor relationships with key stakeholders—including marketing, regulatory ,procurement, packaging and IT decision-makers—within the region
  • Position the value of Validated Software in terms of process control, traceability, data integrity, inspection readiness, speed to market, quality and risk reduction.
  • Develop account plans that identify upsell, cross-sell, and expansion opportunities across Esko's portfolio of software solutions.
  • Partner with Solutions Consultants and Customer Success Managers to deliver compelling, outcome-driven product demonstrations and value assessments.
  • Collaborate with Marketing to execute regional demand generation campaigns and convert inbound leads into qualified opportunities. Represent Esko at relevant events.
  • Analyze win/loss trends, competitive dynamics, and market signals to continuously sharpen your go-to-market approach and territory strategy.
  • Deliver accurate and timely pipeline reporting, forecasting, and CRM hygiene within Salesforce to support business planning and leadership visibility.
  • Champion Esko's value proposition ensuring prospects and customers understand the ROI of our integrated platform.
  • Travel may be required based on business needs, customer engagement requirements, and the complexity of opportunities.

What We're Looking For

These are the must-have requirements for the role:

  • Experience selling into life sciences (pharma, biotech, medical device, CDMO or consumer health), ideally software that touches GxP, quality, regulatory or labeling processes.
  • Demonstrated ability to navigate multi-stakeholder SaaS sales while maintaining the pace, prioritization and commercial discipline required in a mid-market environment.
  • Experience with CRM tools (Salesforce or equivalent) for pipeline management, forecasting, and reporting.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present to both technical and business audiences.

These are nice-to-have skills that will set candidates apart:

  • Experience selling validated SaaS, quality-management, regulatory, labeling, artwork-management, document-management or compliance solution
  • Experience with value-based or consultative selling methodologies e.g., MEDDIC.

Education

  • Flexible working hours
  • Professional onboarding and training options
  • Powerful team looking forward to working with you
  • Career coaching and development opportunities
  • Health benefits
  • 401(k)

About Veralto

Esko is proud to be part of the Product Quality & Innovation segment of Veralto (NYSE: VLTO), a $5B global leader dedicated to ensuring access to clean water, safe food and medicine, and trusted essential goods. When you join Veralto's vibrant global network of 17,000 associates, you join a unique culture and work environment where purpose meets possibility: where the work you do has an everyday impact on the resources and essentials we all rely on, and where you'll have valuable opportunities to deepen your skillset, pursue your ambitions, and grow your career.
