jobs.excerpt: About ISACAISACA® (www. isaca. org) champions the global workforce advancing trust in technology.
jobs.description:
About ISACA

ISACA® (www.isaca.org) champions the global workforce advancing trust in technology. For more than 55 years, ISACA has empowered its community of 195,000+ members with the knowledge, credentials, training and network they need to thrive in fields like information security, governance, assurance, risk management, data privacy and emerging tech. With a presence in more than 195 countries and with more than 230 chapters worldwide, ISACA offers resources tailored to every stage of members’ careers—helping them to thrive in a rapidly changing digital landscape, drive trusted innovation and ensure a more secure digital world. Through the ISACA Foundation, ISACA also expands IT and education career pathways, fostering opportunities to grow the next generation of technology professionals.

Overview

The AI/ML Lead is a senior, hands-on engineer and the first member of ISACA's AI implementation team, a new internal capability that will take on AI engineering work currently delivered by external vendors. Reporting to the VP, Application Engineering, and working within the platform architecture, standards, and governance set by the Senior Director, AI Architecture, Platforms & Agentic Systems, this role builds and hardens the AI solutions that serve ISACA's members and business, both those in delivery today and those that emerge as ISACA's AI portfolio grows. The initial focus is ISACA's personalized member experience, a production RAG and knowledge graph-based recommendation system that integrates ISACA's Body of Knowledge, certification details, workforce skills data, and member profile information. The majority of the role is spent implementing: writing production code, building data and retrieval pipelines, and operationalizing the engineering practices that keep AI systems reliable. Success is measured by production stability, the share of AI engineering work brought in-house, and the implementation team's growing ability to deliver ISACA's current and future AI needs without vendor dependency.

Responsibilities

AI Platform Technical Contribution

  • Provide hands-on engineering for the development, integration, and production delivery of ISACA's AI solutions, beginning with the AI-driven member experience, working within the platform architecture and standards set by the Senior Director, AI Architecture. Build and maintain core AI components, including knowledge graph ontology and configuration (Graphwise or a comparable enterprise knowledge graph platform), embedding and retrieval pipelines, recommendation logic, and LLM-powered and agentic application components. Implement the APIs and service contracts that connect AI capabilities to ISACA's digital experiences and business systems. Ensure all components are built for reuse, long-term internal ownership, and maintainability.

AI Vendor Oversight & Insourcing

  • Serve as the key internal technical counterpart to external AI development vendors and contractors. Participate in vendor architecture reviews and review vendor code and pull requests, evaluating AI solution designs, including RAG pipelines, knowledge graph implementation, and LLM integration, against ISACA's technical requirements and the engineering standards set by the Senior Director, AI Architecture. Define and maintain acceptance criteria for vendor deliverables, support production readiness validation, and surface technical risk or delivery misalignment to the Senior Director, AI Architecture, and IT leadership. Lead knowledge transfer so that vendor-built components move to internal ownership on a planned timeline, progressively reducing vendor dependency.

AI Engineering Practices & Operations

  • Implement and operate MLOps and LLMOps practices in line with the platform standards set by the Senior Director, AI Architecture, including CI/CD for ML and LLM pipelines, model and prompt versioning, evaluation, monitoring, drift detection, and token cost tracking. Establish team-level engineering practices, including code review, documentation, runbooks, and reusable components, that promote quality and consistency across the implementation team and sustain ISACA's AI solutions beyond any single initiative. Foster knowledge sharing so that expertise is built into the organization rather than held by individuals. Implement the security, responsible AI, and auditability controls defined by the Senior Director and Security within the AI solutions the team builds.

Data Infrastructure & AI Data Enablement

  • Build and maintain the data foundations that supply ISACA's AI solutions with reliable, well-structured inputs. Implement ingestion and transformation pipelines from source systems such as CRM, third-party content and learning platforms, and external workforce and market trend data. Implement data contracts with source-system owners, plus data quality checks and monitoring aligned to the standards set by the Senior Director, AI Architecture. Identify and document gaps in ISACA's current data architecture that limit AI performance or extensibility, and work with data, engineering, and product teams to close them.

AI Implementation Team Building

  • Serve as the first engineer on ISACA's AI implementation team. Recommend roles and hiring sequence to bring outsourced AI engineering in-house, participate in hiring and onboarding, and mentor engineers and contractors.

Stakeholder Communication

  • Translate AI system decisions, technical risks, and engineering tradeoffs into clear, actionable communication for product, engineering and IT stakeholders. Collaborate across product, architecture, security, and data teams to ensure AI initiatives integrate coherently into ISACA’s broader enterprise.

Other Duties

  • Evaluate emerging AI tools, platforms, and architectures through hands-on experimentation and proofs of concept, providing practical recommendations that support the Senior Director's build-versus-buy and platform decisions.

Qualifications

Required Field of Study:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

Minimum Years of Experience Required:

  • 8+ years of professional software, data, or application development experience, including 2+ years of hands-on experience developing, implementing, or integrating AI, generative AI, LLM-powered, or agentic AI solutions in production environments, beyond proof-of-concept work.

Description of Minimum Relevant Experience Required:

  • Production delivery of LLM-powered or AI solutions in cloud environments (Azure strongly preferred or equivalent), including experience with LLM integration, RAG pipeline architecture, and model evaluation beyond proof-of-concept work.
  • Proficiency in Python and LLM application frameworks and SDKs; working knowledge of LLM evaluation, RAG pipeline performance tracking, and prompt versioning practices using tools such as Microsoft Foundry, Azure Promptflow, or equivalent evaluation frameworks.
  • Hands-on experience with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, prompt engineering, embedding-based semantic retrieval, vector databases (e.g., Azure AI Search, Pinecone, or Weaviate), and LLM orchestration. Familiarity with multi-agent frameworks (e.g., LangChain, Microsoft AutoGen, or comparable) is a plus.
  • Hands-on experience with knowledge graph architectures and ontology design; direct Graphwise experience is a strong plus. Working knowledge of Neo4j, Amazon Neptune, or Azure Cosmos DB provides transferable graph reasoning skills and is helpful.
  • Foundational MLOps and LLMOps capability: CI/CD for ML and LLM pipelines (Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions), containerized deployment (Docker/Kubernetes), model and prompt versioning, monitoring, token cost tracking, and drift detection. Familiarity with data and workflow pipeline orchestration tools such as Azure Data Factory or Apache Airflow is a plus.
  • Demonstrated ability to oversee AI vendor work through technical architecture review, acceptance criteria definition, and delivery validation.
  • Strong stakeholder communication skills: proven ability to translate AI architecture decisions, risks, and tradeoffs for non-technical audiences including product and engineering stakeholders.
  • Experience working in agile delivery environments with cross-functional product, engineering, data, and security teams.

Preferred Field of Study:

  • Masters Degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Data Science, or Artificial Intelligence

Preferred Years of Experience:

  • 10+ years of professional software or data engineering experience, including 3+ years of hands-on experience developing, implementing, or integrating AI, generative AI, LLM-powered, or agentic AI solutions, ideally including early-stage or greenfield AI systems delivered at enterprise scale.

Description of Preferred Relevant Experience:

  • Experience contributing to or helping shape an AI or data practice — establishing engineering practices and delivery patterns. Experience helping build or scale an engineering team is beneficial.
  • Domain literacy in IT governance, cybersecurity risk management, or professional certification ecosystems — sufficient to collaborate effectively with ISACA's internal subject-matter experts and align AI outputs to organizational standards.
  • Experience with knowledge graph reasoning, or GraphRAG patterns relevant to professional knowledge and competency ontology use cases.
  • Familiarity with bias and fairness evaluation for AI-driven recommendation systems, including output-level testing for demographic or professional skew
  • Prior experience working in a non-profit, professional association, standards body, or other mission-driven organization is a plus.
  • Experience collaborating across hybrid delivery models including in-house staff, contractors, and external development vendors.
  • Proficiency with Azure AI platforms, or equivalent services on AWS or GCP. Azure is the primary cloud platform for this role.
  • Familiarity with enterprise platforms commonly used in ISACA's ecosystem, such as Salesforce, Sitecore, and Microsoft Azure environments, is a plus.
  • Working familiarity with responsible AI principles and general awareness of relevant AI regulatory trends.

Certification and Licensing Preferred:

  • Microsoft Certified: Azure AI App and Agent Developer Associate (AI-103) or MLOps Engineer Associate (AI-300); prior Azure AI Engineer Associate (AI-102) or Azure Data Scientist Associate (DP-100) also recognized
  • AWS Certified Generative AI Developer – Professional or Machine Learning Engineer – Associate, or Google Cloud Professional Machine Learning Engineer

Competencies/Skills Required:

  • Strong customer and member focus, with the ability to design and deliver AI systems that reflect ISACA’s commitment to professional excellence and digital trust
  • A senior hands-on engineer who writes production code, reviews vendor work, and helps grow an internal implementation team.
  • Intellectual adaptability and continuous learning orientation; ability to rapidly develop fluency in new architectures and tools as they emerge.
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical thinking; ability to evaluate tradeoffs between innovation, delivery constraints, cost, and risk in early-stage AI programs
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills, with the ability to explain AI architecture decisions, technical risks, and engineering tradeoffs to technical and product stakeholders
  • Collaborative working style, with the ability to build alignment across engineering, product, data, and security teams without direct authority.
  • Self-starter capable of operating autonomously in environments with evolving requirements and incomplete information
  • Commitment to ISACA’s mission, purpose, and values; cultural sensitivity and awareness appropriate for a global professional membership organization.

This position may require periodic onsite attendance, either currently or in the future, based on business needs. Occasional travel may also be required to attend company-sponsored events, meetings, all-hands gatherings, training sessions, or other activities necessary to support the essential functions of the role.

jobs.description:
Imagineeer is a fast-growing SBA 8(a) Small Disadvantaged Business headquartered in Arlington, VA, delivering federal AI modernization across health, defense, homeland security, and transportation. We design, test, and deploy secure, AI-ready systems that move agencies from pilots to production without breaking governance, compliance, or mission continuity. Our Mission Studio model creates shared environments where policy, data, security, and operations come together. We are capability-driven and competitive by design, not program-dependent. Our leadership has operated inside the federal systems we now transform, bringing institutional knowledge that accelerates delivery and reduces risk. If real delivery motivates you more than slides, and you want your work to compound across programs and agencies, Imagineeer is growing and we are building the team to match.

About the role

Imagineeer is seeking an experienced Oracle DBA/Developer to join our team supporting the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Human Resources Information Technology (HRIT) contract. In this role, you will help modernize how HHS receives, processes, and uses critical HR and payroll data by consolidating and standardizing key federal data file exchanges, building reliable Oracle-based intake and processing workflows, and analyzing a large enterprise HR data environment to document how its tables, reports, and downstream data exchanges are used across the Department. This is a hands-on technical role for someone who enjoys bringing structure and clarity to complex data systems and who can work effectively with both technical teams and government stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Support consolidation of CIDB files, including obtaining the CIDB Full file from Office of Personnel Management (OPM) and generating the CIDB Abbreviated file internally to eliminate reliance on externally supplied abbreviated extracts.
  • Standardize the intake, format, and processing of the Admin (SAC Codes) file received from OPM.
  • Standardize the intake, format, and processing of the Paytran file, including developing a file format specification to share with OPM and establishing receipt of the file from OPM
  • Analyze the technical usage of the Enterprise Human Capital Management (EHCM) data dump, including reviewing 100+ data tables to determine purpose and usage, identifying derived files, associated reports, and data exchanges with HHS Operating Divisions (OPDIVs) that rely on the data dump.
  • Design, develop, and maintain PL/SQL packages, procedures, and ETL processes to ingest, validate, and transform incoming data files.
  • Perform Oracle database administration tasks, including performance tuning, schema management, backup and recovery, and security configuration.
  • Produce technical documentation, including data dictionaries, data lineage, file format specifications, and standard operating procedures.

Qualifications and Skills:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Information Systems, Information Technology, or a related field.
  • 6+ years of experience as an Oracle DBA and/or Oracle Developer
  • Advanced proficiency in SQL and PL/SQL, including stored procedures, complex queries, and performance tuning
  • Experience building ETL processes for flat-file ingestion (fixed-width and delimited) using SQL*Loader, external tables, or equivalent tools
  • Experience developing file format specifications or interface control documents for external data exchanges
  • Experience standardizing and consolidating data file processes
  • Experience working with OPM file exchanges
  • Ability to analyze large, complex data sets to determine purpose, usage, and downstream dependencies
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

Desired Skills and Competencies:

  • Familiarity with Oracle HCM / EHCM data structures
  • Experience with federal HR and payroll data, such as EHRI, personnel and payroll transaction data, or the OPM Guide to Data Standards
  • Prior experience supporting HHS or other federal civilian agencies
  • Oracle Certified Professional (OCP) certification
  • Scripting experience (Python, Shell) to automate file processing

Additional Information:

Employment for this position is contingent upon the candidate being a United States citizen and having the ability to successfully obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance, in accordance with applicable federal regulations. We use AI to review resumes. All hiring decisions will be made in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations

Senior Director, AP Test Publishing

College Board – Advanced Placement & Instruction

Location: This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type: This is a full-time position

About the Team

The College Board’s Advanced Placement and Instruction division (300+ staff) develops and administers coursework taken by more than 3 million students worldwide each school year, and the related subject-matter exams utilized by more than 4,000 colleges and universities for course placement and awarding of college credit. These include credit and placement examination programs like CLEP and ACCUplacer; Advanced Placement (AP) and Pre-AP courses in 40+ disciplines; and associated teacher professional learning programs.

The AP Test Publishing team manages the production of print materials for AP exams worldwide. In collaboration with College Board Operations and vendors, the team produces accommodated print, large print, Braille, and hybrid free response booklets — ensuring equitable, high-quality access for students requiring alternate formats.

About the Opportunity

The Senior Director, AP Test Publishing will collaborate with key organizational workstreams on the build and execution of requirements and processes for the evolving print exam needs of the AP program. This will require defining the development needs and requirements to build print exams in alignment with the current AP course and exam change roadmap. This role oversees content change alignment, planning, and execution for exam publishing and print needs with external vendors, maintaining and communicating detailed documentation and reporting across various interdependent workstreams led by a number of internal and external teams.

In this role, you will:

LEAD & MANAGE THE AP TEST PUBLISHING TEAM (10%)

  • Lead a team of two team members that is responsible for the annual production of print exam materials.
  • Set vision and priorities for the team, track and mange progress to goals, and provide coaching and support to ensure team members meet and exceed goals, remain engaged, and contribute meaningfully to our mission
  • Cultivate an inclusive and high achieving culture that enables all team members to live out College Board’s Operating Principles.
  • Bring proven leadership experience and consistently embody College Board’s Manager Expectations in your work.

TEST PUBLISHING GOVERNANCE & ARCHITECTURE (25%)

  • Own the enterprise Test Publishing operating model, including governance architecture, decision rights, and escalation structure, that enables consistent, scalable execution as the AP program insources assessment production and expands its internally owned exam portfolio.
  • Serve as system integrator and Tier 2 decision authority, adjudicating cross-portfolio tradeoffs across scope, timeline, quality, and cost. Steward material cross-subject and governance risks and resolve escalations that cannot be settled at the Director level.
  • Define, publish, and evolve enterprise Test Publishing standards and frameworks, QC architecture, workflow guardrails, and escalation models, grounded in retrospective data, to drive process integrity and reduce recurring cross-portfolio failure points.

PORTFOLIO DELIVERY & VENDOR OVERSIGHT (25%)

  • Direct sustained delivery of all internally owned AP print, accommodated, and Braille publishing commitments at full scale. Hold milestone integrity and portfolio readiness through delegated project-management and vendor-systems leads while retaining accountability for outcomes.
  • Own senior-level external alignment and vendor governance with print and production vendors, including SLA and performance oversight, contract-level escalation, and quality-control accountability, as the sustained operating relationship supporting insourced production.
  • Maintain and communicate detailed documentation and reporting across interdependent internal and external workstreams, ensuring transparency into progress, dependencies, and risk.

CHANGE MANAGEMENT & INSOURCING ADOPTION (25%)

  • Lead change management for AP Test Publishing as the program insources assessment production from external test developers, building the communication, coordination, and adoption plans that move new publishing workflows, roles, and requirements into steady-state practice.
  • Establish and reinforce clear roles, decision rights, and handoffs across internal teams and vendors, sponsoring training and stakeholder alignment to sustain adoption across all subject types.

CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT, INNOVATION, & TEAM ENABLEMENT (15%)

  • Expand responsible use of generative AI to improve Test Publishing quality and efficiency, such as AI-assisted quality control and analysis of prior-cycle feedback to strengthen first-pass vendor output.
  • Lead structured, data-informed process improvement, drawing on project tracking, stakeholder feedback, and issue logs, to refine publishing workflows across administrations.

About You

You have:

  • Expertise in operational excellence with 7+ years program and/or project management work, preferably in the education industry.
  • A strategic, process-oriented approach: you drive strategic planning, program development, and change management, while identifying risks early and solving problems with creativity.
  • A high degree of ownership and accountability: you consistently deliver results in fast-paced, high-profile environments, backed by strong organizational and time management skills.
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills: you build positive, collaborative working relationships at every level of the organization.
  • A strategic and inclusive leadership style: you set clear priorities, build effective team structures, plan for future needs, and foster a culture of belonging.
  • A proven ability to drive performance and growth: you set high expectations, deliver real-time, evidence-based feedback, and coach team members to take smart risks, stretch their skills, and achieve meaningful impact.
  • A Bachelor’s degree in business or related field is required; advanced degree preferred.
  • The ability to travel 4-6 times a year to College Board offices or on behalf of College Board business.

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise such as live coding, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck: we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.

A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $104,000–$155,000.
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

About the role

    Our Finance & Analytics team owns the authoritative view of Metabase's business performance, and the opinionated read on what's driving it. Internally, this is used to drive decisions; externally, this is used to meet our obligations to investors, auditors, and tax authorities.

    We’re looking for a quantitative-minded generalist to lead a portfolio of analytical projects across the business and own an area of finance operations. Your analytical projects will focus on how we measure and understand the broader business: establishing authoritative definitions for key metrics and investigating what’s driving changes in the data. In your operational area, you’ll run the work and build systems that make it reliable and increasingly automated, drawing on external specialists for technical expertise.

    This isn’t a traditional finance role: we’re a small team of generalists who think in systems, learn unfamiliar domains quickly, and reason through problems from first principles.

Responsibilities

  • Leading analytical projects that change how we understand the business. Examples include:
  • Adapting our ARR definition as our business model evolves
  • Evaluating the health of our sales and marketing funnel
  • Finding relationships between product initiatives and expansion or churn
  • Owning a traditional finance domain (such as Accounting or Tax). This will involve a combination of operational work, managing external experts, and evaluating the overall health of the operation
  • Automating the workflows in your domain so our operational and compliance requirements take as little manual effort as possible. Our aspiration is that areas of traditional finance are treated similarly to analytical systems: a set of inputs that are transformed via defined logic to produce a targeted outcome or insight
  • Leading cross-functional projects to tackle operational problems as they arise

About you

  • You think in systems: you understand how pieces fit together, build reliable processes, and automate repetitive work
  • You think in terms of numbers and are comfortable in a wide range of analytical domains, whether that’s financial modeling, doing intermediate statistical analysis, reviewing the methodology of external vendors, or transforming raw data. We work hard, care deeply and reach further to help people uncover their own power to be healthy. We inspire hope. We learn, grow, and achieve more – in our careers and in our communities.

Job Description Summary:

The Systems Analyst Epic supports the design, build, testing, training, deployment, and ongoing support of Epic applications to optimize clinical and operational workflows. This position develops knowledge of healthcare workflows, system integration, and project delivery practices while partnering with operational leaders and end users to translate business requirements into reliable Epic configuration, integrations, and reporting—supporting safe patient care, efficient revenue cycle operations, and regulatory compliance while meeting Service Level Agreements (SLAs) for supported applications. Works under guidance of senior analysts, architects, and technical leads to follow standards that safeguard the integrity and security of the application environment and contribute to continuous improvement activities related to application management for Epic and related third-party applications. The System Analyst Epic encompasses two closely related role focus areas: Application Build and Application Training. While responsibilities are similar, emphasis may vary based on team assignments.

Responsibilities And Duties:

Both Roles

System Analysis and Design:

Engage stakeholders to gather and refine requirements, map current-state workflows, and design Epic build that aligns with operational goals and policy.
Create and maintain specifications, decision logs, and design documents for clear traceability and change control.
Conduct gap analyses to identify configuration or workflow changes needed for upgrades, regulatory changes, or new initiatives.

Project Management:
Support small projects and enhancements related to system implementations and upgrades under the guidance of senior team members.
Working knowledge of common project approaches (e.g., waterfall, agile) and ability to follow the established methodology.
Participate on project teams and apply agreed project methodology to deliver assigned tasks on time.

Training and Documentation:
Create and maintain documentation for system configurations, workflows, and support procedures, following team standards.

Application Build Role
Application Build, Configuration, and Deployment:
Configure records, master files, and tools (e.g., profiles, rules, security classes, workflows) aligned to approved design.
Maintain environment parity and adhere to change management and build naming conventions.
Develop and execute unit, integrated, and UAT test plans; log and resolve defects; document test evidence.
Validate interfaces, printing, reporting, and downstream workflows; confirm regression coverage in upgrades.
Coordinate release management, environment moves, and downtime procedures for upgrades and patches.
Provide go-live and post-live hypercare, including rounding, office hours, tip sheets, and at-the-elbow support.
Manage service requests and incidents in a timely manner; meet SLAs through effective triage, documentation, and root-cause analysis with guidance as needed.
Provide support for Epic and other enterprise applications as assigned. Collaborate with IT and operational teams to understand cross-application impacts and support integrated workflows (e.g., Epic and third-party applications).

Integration and Data Management:
Collaborate with interface teams on HL7, FHIR, PDFs, CCD/CCDA, and other exchange workflows.
Partner with analytics teams on Clarity/Caboodle extracts, registries, and operational reporting needs.
Ensure data integrity and metric definitions are consistent across modules and stakeholders. Compliance & Risk:
Support regulatory readiness (e.g., CMS, Joint Commission), audit needs, and policy alignment.
Embed privacy/security controls, including sensitive record handling and audit trails.
Contribute to ITIL-aligned incident, problem, change, and configuration management processes.

Application Training Role
Curriculum Management:
Support the design and delivery of role-based training aligned with operational workflows and organizational standards
Support maintenance and updates to the CareConnect curriculum in partnership with training leadership
Help ensure curriculum accuracy and consistency by following established build and validation processes
Incorporate learner and stakeholder feedback into curriculum updates and continuous improvement efforts
Support build, maintenance, and readiness activities for training environments under established standards
Communicate system releases and upgrade impacts to training stakeholders using approved channels and templates

Request/Incident Management
Manage end‑user training‑related requests and incidents with professionalism and efficiency
Support triage and resolution of requests within established service expectations, escalating as appropriate
Document incidents and resolutions to support a comprehensive knowledge base
Collaborate with IT and operational partners to identify trends and recommend preventative improvements
Contribute to support process improvements to enhance service quality and user experience

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's Degree

Additional Job Description:

  • degree in computer science, Information Technology, Healthcare Administration, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 1-3 years of experience in system/application analysis, support, or related IT experience (healthcare environment preferred).
  • In lieu of degree, 5+ years of experience in system/application analysis, support, or related IT experience (healthcare environment preferred).

SPECIALIZED KNOWLEDGE

Required for Both Roles:

• Experience with Epic application(s) and healthcare workflows (clinical, revenue cycle or IT experience).

• Strong requirements gathering, workflow design, and testing skills.

• Familiarity with ITIL, change control, SDLC practices, system governance, and waterfall/agile project methodologies.

  • Ability to communicate with clinical, operational stakeholders, and managed service providers and produce clear documentation.

• Demonstrated ability to support small to medium initiatives and collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.

Requirements for Application Training role:

  • Epic Training Environment Build certification/proficiency (or ability to obtain within required timeframe) and 1+ year of training environment build or application support experience.
  • Epic Principal Trainer certification(s) preferred (or ability to obtain within the required timeframe).

Preferred for Application Build role:

Current Epic Certification or Proficiency in one or more relevant module(s) (e.g., HB, PB, Cadence, Referrals, Orders, ClinDoc, Clarity).

• 1+ year of Epic build/configuration experience preferred (or demonstrated ability to learn and apply build standards quickly).

• Exposure to system integration concepts (e.g., HL7, FHIR) and interface testing is preferred.

• Exposure to reporting and data concepts (e.g., Clarity/Caboodle, SlicerDicer, Reporting Workbench, Radar) is preferred.

• Prior work in patient access, billing, coding, finance, or clinical operations (for respective modules).

DESIRED ATTRIBUTES

  • ITIL Foundation certification desired not required.
  • Certifications in one or more Epic applications
  • Experience in a large healthcare system or hospital setting.
  • Experience with other healthcare applications and systems.
  • Knowledge of healthcare regulations and compliance standards.
  • Familiarity with cloud computing platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure).
  • Experience with business intelligence and analytics tools.

jobs.title: Corporate Travel Coordinator
jobs.excerpt: It's fun to work in a company where people truly believe in what they are doing!
jobs.description:
It's fun to work in a company where people truly believe in what they are doing!

Neogen is seeking an experienced Corporate Travel Coordinator to support global business travel across the organization.

This role will coordinate domestic and international corporate travel, support employees with Concur Travel and Concur Expense, manage complex travel logistics, and partner with vendors to help ensure efficient, cost-effective, and consistent travel experiences.


The Corporate Travel Coordinator will work closely with employees, leaders, supervisors, travel vendors, hotels, airlines, and other external partners to support individual and group travel for conferences, trade shows, meetings, and other business needs. The successful candidate will be highly organized, collaborative, service-oriented, and comfortable managing confidential information and multiple travel priorities across a global organization.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

In this role, you will make an impact by:

  • Coordinating domestic and international corporate travel, including airfare, lodging, ground transportation, and related travel needs
  • Supporting employees with travel arrangements for trade shows, conferences, meetings, customer visits, and other business activities
  • Coordinating group travel and complex itineraries for multiple employees or teams
  • Serving as a support resource for employees experiencing issues with Concur Travel or Concur Expense
  • Troubleshooting Concur-related questions and helping employees navigate travel booking, expense reporting, and related processes
  • Developing and delivering training, guidance, and job aids for employees on the effective use of Concur Travel and Concur Expense
  • Providing individual and group training and support related to travel booking, expense reporting, travel policies, and system best practices
  • Identifying recurring employee questions or system issues and developing training materials or process documentation to improve employee knowledge and system adoption
  • Using Sabre to support corporate travel activities
  • Partnering with employees and supervisors to coordinate travel plans, schedules, and business requirements
  • Working with travel vendors, hotels, airlines, and transportation providers to resolve issues and support traveler needs
  • Negotiating rates, terms, contracts, and service agreements with hotels, airlines, travel vendors, and other suppliers
  • Supporting vendor selection and relationship management to improve service, cost, and traveler experience
  • Monitoring travel reservations and assisting with changes, cancellations, disruptions, and urgent travel needs
  • Maintaining accurate traveler information, itineraries, confirmations, and related documentation
  • Supporting international travel requirements, including coordination of passports, visas, and other travel documentation as appropriate
  • Ensuring travel arrangements align with Neogen travel policies, processes, and cost expectations
  • Supporting administration and continuous improvement of Neogen’s corporate travel and expense program
  • Identifying opportunities to improve travel processes, traveler experience, vendor performance, and cost management
  • Maintaining strict confidentiality when handling employee, leadership, travel, financial, and business information
  • Collaborating with Finance, Procurement, Human Resources, Administrative teams, supervisors, and business leaders across the organization
  • Supporting travel reporting, reconciliation, and other administrative activities as needed
  • Assisting with special projects and other corporate travel responsibilities as assigned

Basic Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • 5+ years of experience in corporate travel coordination, corporate travel management, or a closely related business travel function
  • Experience using Concur Travel
  • Experience using Concur Expense
  • Experience using Sabre
  • Experience providing employee support or help desk-style assistance for travel or expense systems
  • Experience coordinating domestic and international corporate travel
  • Experience coordinating group travel for conferences, trade shows, meetings, or other business events
  • Experience working directly with hotels, airlines, travel agencies, or other travel vendors
  • Experience negotiating vendor rates, contracts, terms, or service agreements
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to manage multiple travel requests, priorities, and deadlines simultaneously
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy
  • Ability to work effectively with employees, supervisors, vendors, and stakeholders across different functions and geographic regions
  • Ability to handle confidential and sensitive employee, travel, financial, and business information appropriately
  • Ability to collaborate closely with a supervisor and coordinate work across multiple stakeholders

Preferred Qualifications

  • Associate or bachelor’s degree in Business, Hospitality, Travel and Tourism, Communications, or a related field
  • Experience supporting travel within a global organization
  • Experience supporting executive or leadership travel
  • Experience working with a corporate travel management company
  • Experience negotiating hotel blocks, airline agreements, or group travel arrangements
  • Experience supporting international visa, passport, or entry documentation processes
  • Experience with corporate travel policy administration
  • Experience with travel reporting, expense reconciliation, or travel analytics
  • Experience supporting meetings, conferences, trade shows, or large-scale company events
  • Experience developing or delivering employee training on Concur Travel, Concur Expense, or other corporate travel and expense platforms

What Will Help You Succeed

  • Strong customer service mindset
  • Excellent organization and follow-through
  • Ability to work effectively with employees, supervisors, and external partners
  • Ability to remain calm and responsive when travel plans change unexpectedly
  • Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting skills
  • Ability to anticipate traveler needs and identify potential issues before they become problems
  • Professional and approachable communication style
  • Strong judgment and discretion when handling confidential information
  • Ability to coordinate multiple priorities across different time zones
  • Flexibility and adaptability in a fast-paced, global environment
  • Strong sense of ownership and accountability

At Neogen we believe that taking care of our employees allows them to do their best work. When you join our team, you'll enjoy competitive benefits and the opportunity to make a meaningful difference every day.

Benefits include:

  • Benefits starting on Day One – Medical, dental, and vision coverage begin on your first day of employment.
  • 401(k) with company match – Invest in your future with retirement savings and company contributions.
  • Paid Time Off (PTO) – Enjoy generous paid time off so you can rest, recharge, and spend time with those who matter most.
  • Career Growth Opportunities – We are committed to promoting from within and providing the tools, training, and support to help you grow your career.
  • Meaningful Work – Be part of a team whose work has a real impact on our customers, communities, and the world around us.
  • Collaborative Culture – Join a team that values innovation, respect, teamwork, and continuous improvement.

Come Be Part of a Mission That Matters

At Neogen, our mission is to protect the world’s food supply. Our products and solutions support customers across food safety, animal safety, diagnostics, and related industries around the world.

Joining Neogen means becoming part of a global organization where your work helps employees travel effectively, supports critical business activity, and contributes to a mission that matters.


Come build your future with us while making a difference every day.

#Applynow

Come Be Part Of A Mission that Matters!

From inside the farm gate to our dinner plates, Neogen protects the world’s food supply. Through a variety of animal healthcare products, to food safety solutions for dangerous bacteria, allergens, toxins, drug residues and much more, Neogen is there — and you can be too.

Company Overview

At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.


Department Overview

At Motorola Solutions, we empower people to be their best in the moments that matter.
We provide critical situational awareness by connecting first responders to seamless communication networks, real-time information, and intuitive, rugged devices. As a vital part of this mission, the Silent Sentinel group within our North America Fixed Video Team specializes in ruggedized, multi-sensor, long-range thermal and infrared camera systems. Silent Sentinel's core mission is to deliver precision target identification and all-in-one situational awareness across extreme environments, equipping defense, border, aviation, and maritime operations with the vision needed to detect threats from miles away and secure critical infrastructure.


Job Description

The Customer Support Manager (CSM) drives overall operational success by actively managing the relationships among the Customer, Motorola, and our subcontractors.


Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the single point of contact for customer management, ensuring seamless service delivery and Service Level Agreement (SLA) compliance for all Silent Sentinel video surveillance deployments.
  • Partner with Motorola Program Managers to ensure a smooth transition of Silent Sentinel systems from the project implementation phase to warranty support and ongoing service operations.
  • Manage service contract scope, ensuring customers fully understand their obligations and the specific service deliverables associated with their solutions.
  • Collaborate with customers and field engineering teams to develop, document, and maintain tailored Customer Support Plans (CSP).
  • Oversee third-party vendors and subcontractors to ensure field deliverables and maintenance work adhere to scope and performance outcomes required for Silent Sentinel hardware.
  • Lead the service contract renewal process for Silent Sentinel agreements, managing customer hardware inventory updates, Statements of Work (SOW) modifications, and third-party pricing changes.
  • Address customer concerns regarding Silent Sentinel network or product quality issues, driving corrective actions to closure and implementing best practices to improve overall service quality.
  • Drive services growth by understanding the customer's evolving needs and proposing appropriate up-sell or cross-sell opportunities.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of technical customer service or support experience, preferably managing video surveillance, defense, or physical security accounts.
  • Solid understanding of Motorola Solutions' Fixed Video portfolio.
  • Fundamental financial acumen required to manage contract renewals, third-party vendor pricing, and service revenue forecasting.
  • Working knowledge of Network Operations Center (NOC) and Customer Call Center procedures to effectively manage escalations for mission-critical surveillance platforms.
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills to articulate service deliverables and technical requirements to both customers and field engineering teams.
  • Proficiency in enterprise tools, including Oracle, Services Lifecycle management platforms, Microsoft Office Suite, Google Workspace, etc.
  • Must be able to travel between 25% to 50% as required for this position.

This position requires compliance with all Motorola policies, standards, and code of conduct, as well as passing necessary background checks required for customer site access.


This position is subject to working in high security areas governed by the US Department of Justice's "Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) Security Policy" and therefore requires successfully passing a more stringent fingerprint background check administered by Motorola Solutions Inc. customers.


Target Base Salary Range: $85,000 - $95,000 USD


Consistent with Motorola Solutions values and applicable law, we provide the following information to promote pay transparency and equity. Pay within this range varies and depends on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The actual offer will be based on the individual candidate.


Basic Requirements

Required Skills:

  • High School diploma, Associates, or Bachelor's degree in Business, Communication, Management, Technology, or 3+ years of Customer Service Management experience required.
  • Must be able to obtain a background clearance as required by our government customers.
  • Legal authorization to work in the U.S. indefinitely is required. Employer work permit sponsorship is not available for this position.

6–12 months

Bonus

Job Title:

Associate Director, Strategy

Job Description

We're Concentrix. The intelligent transformation partner. Solution-focused. Tech-powered. Intelligence-fueled.

The global technology and services leader that powers the world’s best brands, today and into the future. We’re solution-focused, tech-powered, intelligence-fueled. With unique data and insights, deep industry expertise, and advanced technology solutions, we’re the intelligent transformation partner that powers a world that works, helping companies become refreshingly simple to work, interact, and transact with. We shape new game-changing careers in over 70 countries, attracting the best talent.

The Concentrix Technical Products and Services team is the driving force behind Concentrix’s transformation, data, and technology services. We integrate world-class digital engineering, creativity, and a deep understanding of human behavior to find and unlock value through tech-powered and intelligence-fueled experiences. We combine human-centered design, powerful data, and strong tech to accelerate transformation at scale. You will be surrounded by the best in the world providing market leading technology and insights to modernize and simplify the customer experience. Within our professional services team, you will deliver strategic consulting, design, advisory services, market research, and contact center analytics that deliver insights to improve outcomes and value for our clients. Hence achieving our vision.

Our game-changers around the world have devoted their careers to ensuring every relationship is exceptional. And we’re proud to be recognized with awards such as "World's Best Workplaces," “Best Companies for Career Growth,” and “Best Company Culture,” year after year.

Join us and be part of this journey towards greater opportunities and brighter futures.

Position Summary


As an Associate Director, Strategy, you will help shape future marketing strategy for leading technology and SaaS clients by turning research, insights, and business challenges into clear, actionable go-to-market recommendations. In this leadership role, you will partner closely with clients and internal teams to develop strategic marketing plans, compelling narratives, and executive-ready points of view that drive measurable impact.


You’ll bring deep marketing expertise, strong consulting instincts, and the confidence to lead strategic conversations with senior stakeholders while guiding high-quality delivery from planning through execution.


Responsibilities

  • Lead strategic marketing and go-to-market engagements for technology and SaaS clients, aligning recommendations to client business objectives and growth priorities.
  • Conduct detailed research and analysis to understand clients’ business environments, market trends, audience behaviors, competitive landscapes, objectives, and challenges.
  • Develop strategic frameworks for GTM strategies, customer journey mapping, event strategy, messaging, content planning, and customer experience strategy.
  • Translate insights into clear, concise, and compelling narratives across multiple formats, including presentations, strategic plans, executive summaries, and thought leadership content.
  • Prepare and present detailed points of view, recommendations, and strategic plans to clients, stakeholders, and senior executive audiences.
  • Facilitate strategic planning workshops, engaging participants and guiding collaborative discussions toward actionable outcomes.
  • Oversee implementation of strategic marketing plans, monitor progress, identify opportunities for optimization, and recommend adjustments to improve results.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with clients and stakeholders, serving as a trusted advisor and strategic partner.
  • Collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams in fast-paced and high-pressure environments while managing productively through complexity or conflict.
  • Support new pursuits and marketing services opportunities through strategic thinking, compelling storytelling, and high-quality delivery.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in a similar lead marketing consulting, marketing strategy, or strategic advisory role.
  • Proven track record in digital marketing, marketing strategy, marketing technology, event marketing, customer experience strategy and design, customer insights, and analytics.
  • Demonstrated success delivering marketing services, supporting new business pursuits, and leading high-quality client work.
  • Strong expertise in research, messaging, GTM strategy, event strategy, content best practices, and customer journey development.
  • Superior communication and client-facing skills, with the ability to engage multiple stakeholders and senior executive teams.
  • Strong writing, storytelling, and presentation skills, with the ability to craft compelling content for different audiences and formats.
  • Confidence delivering presentations in a dynamic, polished, and engaging manner.
  • Advanced PowerPoint creation skills, with the ability to build executive-ready, visually clear, and persuasive presentations.
  • Deep marketing acumen, strong channel understanding, and project management skills to deliver work on time and on budget.
  • High motivation, initiative, and ownership, with the ability to identify opportunities and lead delivery with confidence.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively, navigate ambiguity, and bring structure to complex business challenges.

The base salary for this position is $101,419 -$150,000 plus incentives that align with individual and company performance. Actual salaries will vary based on work location, qualifications, skills, education, experience, and competencies. Benefits available to eligible employees in this role include medical, dental, and vision insurance, comprehensive employee assistance program, 401(k) retirement plan, paid time off and holidays and paid learning days.


The deadline to apply for this position is: 10/20/2026. This position is for an existing, immediate vacancy. We are currently seeking to fill this role with an individual who can start as soon as possible.


As part of the hiring process, candidates may be required to undergo background screening and identity verification, where permitted by applicable law and consistent with the requirements of the role. Certain verification processes used by the Company or its service providers may involve technologies that rely on biometric identifiers or biometric information, where permitted by law. If biometric identifiers or biometric information are collected, used, or stored, the Company will provide the legally required disclosures and obtain any required written consent prior to such collection, and will handle such information in accordance with applicable biometric privacy laws and Company policies.

jobs.description:
About Cambiar Education:

Founded in 2016 as the first K-12 nonprofit venture studio, Cambiar Education saw untapped potential in the marketplace that could change the world of education - an opportunity to foster and advance radical, innovative ideas that massively accelerate student success for all. Since then, Cambiar has propelled over 140 game-changing ventures that operate at the speed of innovation, cultivated a portfolio of bold and visionary leaders, and built a connected community anchored in a commitment to creating and scaling solutions that center all students. As a member of the Cambiar Education team, you will help change the marketplace for education innovation to prove undeniably that every student can succeed and thrive.

Role Overview

As Cambiar expands its national portfolio of education innovation initiatives, we are scaling our digital ecosystem—integrating systems, data, and tools that power our mission. Safeguarding the security, integrity, and trust of this ecosystem is critical to enabling our impact.

The Director, IT & Security, reporting to the SVP, Technology, will be both a strategic leader and a hands-on practitioner responsible for Cambiar’s technology platforms and cybersecurity posture. This role will guide the organization’s approach to IT systems management, vendor oversight, and security best practices—ensuring strong governance, resilient infrastructure, and a culture of data stewardship. You will lead Cambiar’s work to strengthen IT and security operations, implement modern processes and tools, and partner with both internal teams and external vendors to advance the technology maturity and security posture across Cambiar and its incubated ventures.

The ideal candidate combines technical acumen, strategic vision, and a human-centered mindset—balancing operational excellence with the flexibility and creativity that drive innovation. They bring deep expertise in IT and cybersecurity best practices, strong leadership and communication skills, and a proactive, solution-oriented approach.

What you’ll do:

You’ll serve as a trusted partner to Cambiar’s leadership, operations, and venture teams, leading the IT and Security strategy and roadmap, vendor partnerships, and compliance. Your work will include both strategic direction and tactical execution.

  • Establish a systems inventory and governance framework: Build and maintain a comprehensive registry of Cambiar’s applications, data flows, and integrations to identify risks, redundancies, and opportunities for optimization.
  • Rationalize and optimize the tech stack: Evaluate usage, cost, and security posture of tools to reduce duplication, improve interoperability, and deliver measurable efficiencies.
  • Lead cybersecurity strategy: Develop and implement policies and practices aligned to SOC 2 and other relevant frameworks; establish and oversee secure architectures across cloud, network and applications including data classification, backup and retention, and incident response.
  • Enhance access and identity management: Implement scalable joiner/mover/leaver workflows, least-privilege and role based access principles, and security aware optimization.
  • Oversee and partner with the IT vendor: Manage relationships, ensure SLAs and DPAs are met, and guide shared workstreams such as device management, identity and access management, and network security.
  • Consult for incubated ventures: Provide advisory support on IT infrastructure, security practices, and compliance as ventures establish and scale their systems.
  • Foster a security-minded culture: Foster organization-wide understanding of cybersecurity practices and shared accountability for data protection. Lead risk management and compliance, conducting regular assessments, audits, and training to strengthen organization-wide awareness and readiness.
  • Monitor and report: Track metrics, manage audits, and present IT/security performance and emerging risks to leadership and the board.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with operations, finance, data, and partner teams to embed privacy, security, and trust into every project.

This role is for you if:

  • You bring 10+ years of experience in IT operations, cybersecurity, or technology risk management, ideally in reputed mission-driven or innovative environments.
  • You have hands-on experience executing and managing IT systems, cybersecurity software and processes (IAM, MDM, RBAC, pentesting, etc.), and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO, or similar).
  • You’re adept at partnering with external vendors while also building internal capacity and scalable IT processes.
  • You thrive in dynamic, entrepreneurial settings, balancing structure with adaptability and creative problem-solving.
  • You are an excellent communicator who can translate and motivate technical topics into accessible, actionable insights for diverse audiences.
  • You demonstrate high integrity and discretion, with a strong sense of responsibility for protecting sensitive information.
    You are organized, detail-oriented, and proactive, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results independently.
  • You have a proven record of building secure, efficient, and people-centered systems that enable productivity and trust.
  • Experience in education, nonprofit, or social impact organizations is a plus.

What you'll get:

  • Salary range of $140,000-$170,000 per year depending on experience, location and aligned title
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, vision benefits
  • Paid vacation and sick time, plus organizationally-observed holidays throughout the year
  • Access to optional benefits such as 401(k) Retirement Plan, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), HSA/FSA, pet insurance, etc.
  • Stipends to partially cover phone and internet costs, home office set-up, and wellness
  • Team retreats and meetings during the year to meet your teammates or see our work in-person

Our Core Values:

We’re committed to living our organization's core values:

  • CREATE 🌎 We create to make a transformative difference in the world. We are eternally optimistic and develop game-changing solutions.
  • LOVE ❤️ We believe in the tremendous talent and human potential of all; we want to discover, engage, and celebrate everyone’s unique “superpowers.” We seek out and lean into eclectic ideas, joyful debates, and direct feedback.
  • GROW 🌱 We have an insatiable curiosity, love big challenges, and aren't afraid to fail. We accelerate growth and impact so change agents and change efforts reach their fullest potential.
  • LAUGH 😄 We laugh often and out loud; creativity is best fostered when we are having fun! We defer judgment so we can all laugh, dance, sing, and express "like no one is watching."
  • DARE 🚀 We dare to dream big, take bold action, and challenge the impossible. We embrace risk, push boundaries, and step into the unknown with strength and courage, knowing that growth lies beyond comfort.

Work environment:

Although our team works remotely, you are expected to engage in overnight travel at least 2x throughout the year to various US cities to meet up with other team members (in-person retreats, other program-related meetings and events), and be ready to play an active role in contributing to our collaborative, inclusive culture.

We’re looking for applicants who are comfortable working remotely and who have experience successfully collaborating with team members across different time zones. Your core working days and hours will be M-F from 8am-6pm, with the ability to flex according to workload, scheduled calls and in-person/virtual meetings.

Our Equal Opportunity Employer Commitment:

At Cambiar Education, we believe everyone can make a positive impact, and that a range of perspectives and experiences strengthens our team. We are committed to building an agile, engaging environment where every team member can do their best work, the foundation for creating life-changing impact for one million youth.

Cambiar Education is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants. This policy extends to all aspects of our employment practices including, but not limited to, recruiting, hiring, promotions, transfers, compensation, benefits, training, leaves of absence, and other terms and conditions of employment.

jobs.description:
About Us

Every moment of every day, people all over the world rely on the infrastructure work provided by Quanta Services and Quanta Government Solutions (QGS). With its highly skilled and innovative workforce, Quanta is the largest specialty contractor in North America that powers modern life. Find your future with us by being a part of something bigger – leading the energy transition in building a better world for generations to come.

Imagine what you could do here. We encourage and inspire our people to embrace opportunities within our corporate office and 200 operating companies providing solutions for the utility, renewable energy, electric power, industrial, communications and government industries worldwide.

Quanta’s culture is about creating an environment where all employees can be themselves, are valued, and have an equal opportunity to succeed. When you join our team, you join a dynamic culture in which career development is encouraged, excellence is rewarded, and diversity is valued.

About this Role

COMPANY: Quanta Government Solutions

JOB TITLE: Senior Costpoint System Administrator

DEPARTMENT: Information Technology

LOCATION: Remote

REPORTS TO: Director, IT

CLASSIFICATION: Exempt

POSITION OVERVIEW:

QGS is seeking a Senior Costpoint System Administrator to serve as the subject matter expert and functional owner of Deltek Costpoint across QGS and its affiliated Operating Companies. In addition, this role manages, configures, and maintains the Deltek Costpoint enterprise resource planning (ERP) environment, serving as the organization’s main point of expertise for system security, integrations, and module troubleshooting across accounting, projects, and other business modules.

This is a hands-on role that combines day-to-day functional system administration and end-user support with technical ownership of the Costpoint ERP environment, including user access management, system security, compliance standards, integrations, and platform maintenance and upgrades. The Senior Costpoint System Administrator partners with accounting, finance, project control, and program teams to configure the system, resolve issues, manage integrations, process batch jobs, and keep month-end close, billing, and reporting cycles running smoothly.

This role is ideal for a seasoned Costpoint professional with deep government contract accounting knowledge, strong troubleshooting skills, and the ability to work across teams to bring accuracy, consistency, and reliability to critical financial systems and reporting. This role reports to the Director, IT; direction on the accounting and finance aspects of the role is provided by the Director, Accounting and Finance.

What You'll Do

  • Serve as the subject matter expert and system administrator for Deltek Costpoint GCCM, supporting government contract accounting operations end to end across QGS and its affiliated Operating Companies.

jobs.description:
Job Summary

About Fuze Health
At Fuze Health, we put patients first and tirelessly address the most pressing needs in healthcare. We empower millions to digitally connect with care providers, essential health resources and needed treatments – and enable care providers, employers, health plans and life sciences companies to meaningfully enhance quality, outcomes and value. We are dedicated to helping our partners evolve and modernize to meet emerging patient and marketplace needs.

Fuze Health’s foundation is built upon the strategic combination of several proven, technology-powered innovators in the digital health, diagnostics, and pharmacy sectors. Our growing portfolio brings together the capabilities of industry leaders including LetsGetChecked, Truepill, and Alto Pharmacy, to create a distinctive, unified force in healthcare. Together, we have the shared vision, advanced capabilities and talented teams to deliver next-generation solutions that patients and healthcare partners need today and into the future.

Job Description
We are seeking a strategic, client-facing leader to manage our most complex enterprise relationships while also owning the strategy and execution of our quality improvement programs. This is a hybrid role for someone equally comfortable serving as a trusted executive partner to enterprise clients and driving measurable outcomes on HEDIS, STAR, and other clinical quality measures.



Job Description

Key Responsibilities


Enterprise Account Management

  • Lead and manage trusted enterprise relationships, acting as the primary point of contact for inquiries and escalations from key decision-makers, aligning product value with business goals to ensure long-term strategic alignment.
  • Oversee the complex customer lifecycle from strategic onboarding through retention, providing technical support, addressing inquiries, resolving issues, and ensuring product functionality meets specifications.
  • Serve as the voice of the customer, collaborating with Product and Engineering teams on product reliability and feedback for improvements based on enterprise client needs.
  • Provide consultative leadership, leveraging a proven track record managing the company's largest, most complex books of business to influence stakeholders across Operations, Legal, and Product/Engineering.
  • Pioneer and execute expansion strategies, independently identifying and securing upsell and cross-sell opportunities to maximize satisfaction and retention.
  • Drive cross-functional alignment so client success initiatives integrate with and support overall company growth and financial performance.
  • Advocate for client interests, representing client needs and feedback internally to ensure the product roadmap reflects market demands.
  • Track, analyze, and report on key metrics, including recurring revenue, margins, and satisfaction scores, to identify account risks early and lead complex escalation resolutions with data-backed updates.

Quality Improvement Programs

  • Lead and oversee cross-functional initiatives focused on identifying and closing care gaps, improving member engagement, and delivering measurable outcomes for health plan and employer clients.

Strategy

  • Develop, optimize, and execute gap closure plans.
  • Establish annual quality improvement objectives and performance targets.
  • Lead cross-functional teams to deliver measurable outcomes.

Program Operations

  • Design and implement member outreach campaigns.
  • Manage workflows supporting HEDIS and STAR initiatives.
  • Optimize operational processes to improve completion rates and efficiency.
  • Stand up a repeatable playbook for new quality measures as CMS/NCQA requirements shift.

Analytics & Reporting

  • Build KPI dashboards and executive reporting.
  • Monitor performance trends and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Turn outreach and completion data into specific, actionable recommendations each quarter.

Client Management

  • Serve as executive liaison for quality initiatives.
  • Present results and recommendations to senior client leadership.
  • Support business development efforts and solution design.

Process Improvement

  • Develop scalable and repeatable operational processes.
  • Identify technology enhancements and automation opportunities.
  • Implement best practices and continuous improvement methodologies.

Financial Management

  • Develop business cases and ROI models.
  • Manage program budgets and vendor relationships.

Required Experience & Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree required.
  • 5+ years of experience in Healthcare Operations or Customer Success, preferably within digital healthcare or pharmacy.
  • 3+ years leading HEDIS, STARS, population health, or quality improvement programs.
  • Proven success in complex healthcare client management, including confident management of relationships with C-suite executives.
  • Deep understanding of NCQA and CMS quality measures.
  • Strong technical expertise or aptitude for understanding and troubleshooting complex systems and applications.
  • Superb communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build, maintain, and influence strong relationships with high-stakes internal and external stakeholders, including senior client leadership.
  • Strategic thinker with a customer-centric approach and the ability to understand program and process impact across the entire organization.
  • Strong analytical mindset, with proficiency in data analysis and problem-solving to identify trends and inform executive decision-making.
  • Experience leading cross-functional teams in a matrixed environment.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, effectively managing multiple high-priority enterprise accounts and competing interests.

Required Experience

  • Direct experience closing HEDIS or STAR care gaps at scale (population health management)
  • Experience designing or running member outreach campaigns (call center, SMS, digital, or mail-based)
  • Experience managing contract renewals, SLAs, or escalations with enterprise health plan or employer clients
  • Familiarity with quality measure lifecycle management (measure retirement, specification updates, new measure rollout)
  • Experience navigating both the clinical/quality side and the commercial/account side of a healthcare business



Additional Information

Additional Physical Job Requirements


Physical requirements for this role include the ability to work at a computer terminal with monitor, keyboard and mouse for extended periods of time, stoop, bend, and reach for equipment and supplies, make frequent repetitive motions required to operate a computer that include the wrists, hands and fingers, and lift, carry, push, pull, and move light objects up to 20 pounds. The role also requires the ability to effectively communicate through verbal interactions, discern auditory information, and visually perceive details to perform essential job functions.
