jobs.description:
Risepoint is an education technology company that helps regional universities launch and grow online programs for modern learners. Risepoint supports more than 100 universities and colleges across five countries, with programs concentrated in high-demand fields including nursing, healthcare, teaching, business, technology, and public service. Our suite of products and services supports the full student journey and each university’s long-term goals. Together, we increase access to affordable education that delivers a strong return on investment for learners and meets employer and community needs. Learn more at risepoint.com.


The Impact You Will Make

Risepoint's Partner Data organization is the operational backbone connecting more than 100 university partners to accurate, timely student and program data. We are seeking a Senior Director, Partner Data Integrations & Operations to lead this organization through its next stage: Reshaping two dedicated teams - Partner Data Operations and Partner Data Enablement, so day-to-day case resolution and forward-looking partner enablement each run to a higher standard.

In this role, you will lead a team who resolve partner data issues, run the recurring processes that keep partner systems in sync, and deliver new partner launches and relaunches. You will transform the team into a Partner Data Integrations & Operations team that runs disciplined, well-governed case management and monitoring, and a Partner Enablement Data team that gets ahead of partner needs - owning onboarding, relaunches, and acting as the systems subject matter expert for partner data integrations. Across both teams, you will instill a product mindset - ensuring day-to-day issue resolution and partner enablement work continually surface and drive broader improvements to Risepoint's partner data products and integrations, not just close individual cases.

The ideal candidate pairs technical fluency in SIS systems and integrations with hands-on operations leadership, ideally built in ed-tech, higher education, or another partner-based, data-intensive environment. This person can read a data flow as comfortably as they can run a case-management queue, and can operate with real autonomy while keeping cross-functional partners - Enterprise Data, Partner Support, Student Success Center, and CRM - aligned.

How You Will Bring Our Mission to Life

What You Will Do

  • Build the operating model, leadership capability, and standards for the Partner Data Operations team - defining how partner data cases are triaged and resolved, and how monitoring and reconciliation work keeps partner systems accurate and reliable
  • Set clear service-level standards and escalation rules for the Partner Data Integrations & Operations team, collaborating with Enterprise Data, Partner Support, SSC, and CRM, replacing today's informal, case-by-case routing.
  • Drive automation and process redesign to cut repeat, low-judgment case volume and free the team for higher-value work.
  • Instill and enforce a product mindset across the organization, ensuring that case resolution and monitoring work routinely surfaces patterns and root causes that translate into broader improvements to partner data systems and integrations, not just one-off fixes.
  • Stand up Data Integration Engineering to work directly with partner SIS systems (Slate, Banner, Workday, and others), producing a repeatable integration playbook per system rather than one-off, person-dependent builds.
  • Serve as the strategic advisor partner-facing technical lead for new partner onboarding, engaging directly with partner IT and SIS teams from day one to scope integrations, unblock technical issues, and set the relationship up as a strong technical partnership rather than a handoff
  • Grow the Partner Enablement Data team into the go-to subject matter expert on partner systems, data, and workflows, bringing that expertise, and a product mindset, into every partner engagement so the team can advise Partner Management and partners directly on how Risepoint's products should integrate for a successful partnership.
  • Champion the architectural fixes that tooling can't replace to shape the cross-functional roadmap and priorities for partner data architecture, aligning Partner, Data, Product, and Technology leaders around enterprise-wide solutions, turning structural gaps into system enhancements and architectural improvements that go beyond what validation and tooling alone can fix.
  • Own the partner data strategy - setting priorities, investment choices, and trade-offs across the Partner Data Integrations & Operations and Partner Enablement Data teams, including owning validation and monitoring tooling (such as an Agentic AI validation tool) and standardizing file formats, data mapping, and integrations across a partner portfolio that today runs on multiple legacy systems with no single standard.
  • Lead, hire, and develop Partner Data Integrations & Operations organization across two teams; report on case trends, launch progress, and team performance to senior leadership, and own the KPI scorecard for partner data operations.
  • Operate autonomously with minimal oversight, proactively identifying issues and driving solutions, and influence decisions across the organization using data-driven reasoning, storytelling, and a strong executive presence.

What Success Looks Like

  • Partner data cases are resolved quickly and consistently against clear service-level targets, improving the partner and student experience.
  • New partner launches and relaunches run on a repeatable playbook and go live on time, without depending on any one person.
  • A capable Partner Enablement Data team is established and recognized as the systems expert for partner data integrations.
  • Partner data is treated as a strategic differentiator, not just a support function, opportunities such as richer application-form and retention data are identified and pursued to improve partner business outcomes, beyond fixing what's broken.
  • New partners experience includes integrations & operations team as a direct, hands-on partner during onboarding, not just a backend resource.

How Impact Will be Measured

  • Case volume, resolution time, and incident rate for partner data issues trend down, with clear SLAs defined and met.
  • New partner launches and relaunches hit target go-live dates at a high rate, using a documented, repeatable process.
  • Manual, repeat case volume drops through automation, and partner satisfaction with data support improves
  • Product and system improvement ideas surfaced from case and partner-enablement work are tracked, prioritized, and shipped, with a measurable reduction in partner-specific workarounds as upstream product gaps close.

What You’ll Bring to the Team

Experience That Matters Most

  • 8+ years leading data operations, technical support, or partner/customer success teams, including at least 3 years managing managers or multiple teams. (Must have)
  • Technical fluency with data systems (snowflake, databricks) and integrations (file feeds, SFTP, APIs) and CRM platforms such as Salesforce, comfortable going deep with engineering and data teams. (Must have)
  • Experience in ed-tech, higher education, or another partner-based, data-intensive industry. (Must have)
  • Experience with SIS systems such as Slate, Banner, Workday, and others (Must have)
  • Comfort as the client-facing point of contact on technical onboarding conversations, not just an internal operator.
  • A track record of building or restructuring an operations team, setting up intake, case management, and service-level standards. (Must have)

Experience That’s Great to Have

  • Background in partner onboarding, implementation, or customer launch and migration management.
  • Familiarity with Agile or Jira-based work management (epics, sprints, backlog prioritization).
  • Prior experience partnering with Enterprise Data or engineering teams on system enhancements and data-quality initiatives.
  • Experience partnering with Product teams to translate operational or partner pain points into product requirements, with comfort operating with a product mindset in an operations seat.

Risepoint is an equal-opportunity employer and supports a diverse and inclusive workforce.

jobs.description:
Visual Designer

College Board – AP & I

Location: This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type: This is a full-time position


About the Team

The Advanced Placement team supports College Board in serving more than seven million students a year as they prepare for a successful transition to college through programs and services in college readiness and college success — speciﬁcally through the Advanced Placement (AP) Program. With more than 40 courses in a variety of subject areas, we are committed to promoting innovation, equity, and excellence for generations of students.


The AP Design team is a small in-house team focused on delivering high-impact, brand-aligned creative solutions. Partnering closely with internal stakeholders, we translate business goals into functional user-centered design across print and digital channels. Our team combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution to ensure consistency, quality, and efficiency at every stage of the creative process.

About the Opportunity

As a Visual Designer, you have a love for design and an attention to detail in everything you touch. You’re interested in learning more about the craft of design, trying new things, and are open to working on any type of project. We’re looking for someone who can work independently, communicate regularly with autonomy over their projects, and support our design goals. You are comfortable creating and editing design files across many channels – print, digital, presentations, email, marketing, and video. You seek finesse in all projects, taking pride in your work ethic and delivery of excellent creative assets. If you are adaptable, service-oriented, and dedicated to being an advocate for our audiences through great design, then we want to work with you.



In this role, you will:

Conceptualize and Design (80%)

  • Develop and deliver consistent and high-quality design solutions for organizational campaigns and initiatives that are aligned to brand standards – this may include print, digital, email, products, and event graphics.
  • Work on an array of PowerPoint presentations for a variety of internal stakeholders.
  • Implement established best practices in marketing, including information design, social media, and other emerging strategies.
  • Manage all phases of an assignment from concept through completion, including design development and digital file preparation.
  • Maintain and organize design files, templates, and shared assets to support team efficiency.
  • Ensure accessibility standards are incorporated across all materials.
  • Support vendor coordination and production processes, including print specifications and quality control reviews.
  • Contribute to workflow improvements that help refine internal creative processes to increase output quality.

Communicate, Collaborate, and Adapt (20%)

  • Communicate with all team members to ensure timely delivery of design artifacts.
  • Work effectively with cross-functional teams, while navigating and adjusting to shifting priorities.
  • Build trust and strong working relationships with internal stakeholders.
  • Clearly articulate design ideas and rationale, present work confidently to stakeholders, and actively listen and incorporate feedback

About You

  • A portfolio of your work included in your application.
  • A BFA in graphic design, along with a minimum of 4–6 years of hands-on experience in design and production.
  • An understanding of visual design systems, hierarchy, typography, aesthetics, illustration, iconography, photography, data visualization, interaction, and composition.
  • An appetite for problem solving, while thriving in fast-paced environments.
  • Sharp design sensibilities and keen attention to detail, with experience crafting custom design specifications.
  • Openness to take on any project, no matter size or medium, with the ability to jump from one project to another, based on priorities and workload.
  • Affinity for problem solving and being a team player.
  • High understanding of industry standard design tools, such as Adobe Creative Suite and Figma.
  • Deep knowledge of Microsoft Office products, including advanced-level skills using PowerPoint, designing templates, master slides, and more. Experience working with Adobe After Effects, in animated media, or motion graphics a bonus, but not required.
  • The ability to travel 3–6 times a year to College Board offices or on behalf of College Board business.

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States


About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise such as live coding, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck- we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.


A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $64,000-$100,000
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

jobs.description:
The Identity & Trust Engineering team is seeking an experienced Manager, Identity & Trust Engineering to lead the strategy, engineering, and operational maturity of the enterprise platforms that protect identities, privileged access, certificates, secrets, and digital trust across BlueCross BlueShield of Tennessee.


In this highly visible leadership role, you'll guide the evolution of modern identity and security capabilities including authentication, access management, privileged access management (PAM), secrets management, public key infrastructure (PKI), certificate lifecycle management, and application protection.


You'll lead a team of engineers and security specialists, partner closely with Information Security, Architecture, Infrastructure, and Application Delivery teams, and drive automation, platform modernization, operational excellence, and technology lifecycle management. This role offers a unique opportunity to influence enterprise security strategy while enabling secure, scalable solutions that support business growth and digital transformation.


Ideal candidates will bring:

  • Expertise in enterprise identity, authentication, privileged access, PKI, secrets management, and digital trust capabilities.
  • Demonstrated experience leading engineering teams responsible for security platforms, operational excellence, modernization, and technology roadmaps.
  • Proven ability to partner with business and technology leaders to deliver secure, scalable solutions that reduce risk and enable business outcomes.
  • Experience driving automation, process improvement, and capability maturity within complex enterprise environments.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to translate complex security concepts into clear business value for executives and stakeholders.

Note:

  • While this is a fully remote role, final interviews onsite at our Chattanooga, TN headquarters will be required.
  • Sponsorship is not available for this role.


Job Duties & Responsibilities

  • Oversee design, implementation, configuration, maintenance, and troubleshooting of multiple security technologies
  • Develop, maintain and communicate policies, standards and procedures to manage security functions relative to information technology systems (including systems under development), networks, applications, and voice and data communications that are consistent with applicable regulatory and compliance requirements.
  • Develop and report business-relevant metrics to measure the efficiency and effectiveness of the Information Security Program, facilitate appropriate resource allocation and increase the maturity of the security program.
  • Provide subject matter expertise on a broad range of information security standards and best practices, such as NIST, PCI, ISO 27001, MAR and others as applicable.
  • Work with Information Security Directors, CISO and appropriate stakeholders to prepare and present relevant information on security status as required.

Job Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field or equivalent years of experience is required. Equivalent years of experience are determined as one year of technical experience for every year of college requested.

Experience

  • 5 years - Experience leading teams of technical resources in diverse disciplines is required.
  • 5 years - Experience in information security or related field is required.
  • 3 years- Experience in Security Engineering or in a related field required.

Skills/Certifications

  • Information Security certifications such as the Certified Information Systems Security Professional Certification (CISSP) or Certified Information Security Manager Certification (CISM) is required or must be obtained within 2 years of acceptance of position.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel and PowerPoint)
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills.
  • Strong interpersonal and organizational skills
  • Must be a team player, be organized and have the ability to handle multiple projects
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision or function in a team environment sharing responsibility, roles, and accountability

Oversee enterprise data engineering, data products, governance, analytics enablement, and AI capabilities to improve operational efficiency, decision-making, customer experience, and business growth.

Education

Experience

jobs.description:
Overview

Since our founding in 1924, we've cut cardiovascular disease deaths in half, but there is still so much more to do. To overcome today’s biggest health challenges and accelerate this progress, we need passionate individuals like you. Join our movement, be part of the progress, and help ensure a healthier future for all. You matter, and so does the impact you can make with us.The American Heart Association’s Internship Program provides college students an opportunity for hands-on experience in various facets for individuals interested in gaining work experience with a non-profit, voluntary health organization.

Under the supervision and mentorship of the American Heart Association’s Volunteerism team, the intern will support volunteer engagement and content management efforts across national initiatives. The intern will support three primary areas: volunteer communications and resource development; volunteer recognition initiatives, including National Volunteer Week; and youth engagement through Heart Clubs and the National Youth Leadership Council.

Working closely with the Volunteerism team, the intern will help translate volunteer engagement goals into practical resources, presentations, digital content and other materials for staff and volunteers. The intern will also support high school and college student volunteers by coordinating and facilitating virtual onboarding sessions, leading year-end feedback meetings and helping enhance the overall Heart Club volunteer experience.

The Association offers many resources to help you maintain work-life harmonization through your changing needs and life situations. To help you be successful, you will have access to Heart U, our award-winning corporate university, as well as training and support locally and through our National Center.#TheAHALife is more than a company culture; it is our way of life. It embodies our commitment to work-life harmonization and is guided by our core values where our employees can thrive both personally and professionally. Discover why you will Be Seen. Be Heard. Be Valued at the American Heart Association by following us on LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, and at heart.jobs.

Internship Overview:

  • Time Commitment: 20-25 hours per week
  • Internship Duration: 1/25/27-5/7/27​
  • Location: Remote
  • Salary: $23.00 per hour

Internship Outcomes:

Individuals participating in the internship program are provided with an opportunity to:

  • Gain important and practical job skills to be successful in a non-profit environment.
  • Opportunity to explore a career-path with a reputable voluntary health/service organization.
  • Complete an internship that enriches your academic and professional resume as well as enriching your personal life by making a difference in the lives of others.

Responsibilities

Tasks may include:

  • Drafting, editing and proofreading content for websites, social media, emails, newsletters, volunteer messaging and other communications.
  • Creating and updating visual content, templates and digital assets using tools such as Canva or Figma.
  • Communicating professionally with external volunteers by phone and email to share information, answer questions and support engagement.
  • Maintaining content calendars, contact lists, communication records and other internal tracking tools.
  • Supporting email and audience communications in Salesforce Marketing Cloud and maintaining volunteer information in Salesforce CRM, as needed.
  • Preparing slide decks, communication recaps, reports and materials for volunteer meetings, presentations and training webinars.
  • Assisting with special projects that strengthen volunteer engagement, content quality and communication processes.

Qualifications

  • College seniors and graduate students studying communications, marketing, public relations, nonprofit management, business or a related field are preferred.
  • Strong writing, website copywriting, copyediting and verbal communication skills, with the ability to adapt messaging for different audiences and channels.
  • Detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to manage multiple content assignments, deadlines and follow-up communications.
  • Demonstrated interest and involvement in volunteerism and student-run organizations.
  • Comfort communicating with volunteers by phone, email and on Teams/Zoom in a professional and timely manner.
  • Experience with content or design tools such as Canva or Figma is preferred; familiarity with Salesforce Marketing Cloud or Salesforce CRM is a plus.
  • A letter of recommendation from a professor, employer, or supervisor is preferred.
  • Ability to conduct independent research and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Demonstrated skills in effective one-on-one and group communications.
  • Ability to deal professionally in a corporate or non-profit environment and assume responsibility for guiding projects and programs.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment.
  • Required: Reliable WiFi Connection.
  • Minimum availability of 25 hrs/wk, M-F between the hours of 8:30am-5pm ET or CT.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States for any employer without sponsorship, now or in the future. For any roles working remotely, the work must also be performed inside the United States, not in a foreign country.

Compensation & Benefits

The job application window is expected to close: October 30, 2026.

The American Heart Association invests in its people. Visit Rewards & Benefits to see more details.

  • Compensation and Performance – Attracting talented, committed interns means offering competitive compensation, ongoing professional development and training, and an environment in which to work and grow. And we do.
  • Professional Development – You can join one of our many Employee Resource Groups (ERG) or be a mentor/mentee in our professional mentoring program. Heart U is the Association’s national online university, with more than 100,000 resources designed to meet your needs and busy schedule.
  • Healthcare Benefits – You will have the opportunity to participate in our Teladoc General Medical and Behavioral Health programs. We also provide access to our Employee Assistance Program (EAP) at no cost as a confidential program designed to assist employees and family members with personal issues that affect their relationships at home or at work.

Apply Today:So, are you ready to intern for the largest voluntary health organization dedicated to fighting heart disease, stroke, and other cardiovascular diseases?

jobs.description:
As a result of the combination of the BD Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions business with Waters Corporation (NYSE: WAT), by applying to this role, you will be applying for a position with Waters. Waters is a global leader in life sciences, dedicated to accelerating the benefits of pioneering science through analytical technologies, informatics, and service. With a focus on regulated, high-volume testing environments, Waters’ innovative portfolio harnesses deep scientific expertise across biology, chemistry, and physics. Waters collaborates with analytical laboratories around the world to advance the release of effective, high-quality medicines, assure the safety of food and water, and drive better patient outcomes by detecting diseases earlier, managing routine infections, and combatting growing antibiotic resistance. Through a shared culture of relentless innovation, Waters’ passionate team of approximately 16,000 colleagues partner with customers to turn scientific challenges into breakthroughs that improve lives worldwide.

We are the people who give possibilities purpose

BD is one of the largest global medical technology companies in the world. Advancing the world of health™ is our Purpose, and it’s no small feat. It takes the imagination and passion of all of us—from design and engineering to the manufacturing and marketing of our billions of MedTech products per year—to look at the impossible and find transformative solutions that turn dreams into possibilities.

Job Description

Summary


We are seeking a Senior Product Cyber Security Engineer to own the cybersecurity deliverables for assigned products end to end and to build the automation that lets a small team cover a large portfolio. You will plan the security activities for each release, lead threat modeling, run composition and static analysis, produce and monitor Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs), coordinate penetration tests, and write the documentation that goes into our design history files, regulatory submissions and customer assurance packages.


This is a product security engineering role, not an IT security, SOC or penetration testing role. You will read code, work in build pipelines, and defend your risk assessments in front of auditors, regulators and customers. You will work daily with R&D, Software Engineering, DevOps, Systems Engineering, Quality and Regulatory Affairs, and with our corporate product security and cyber risk teams.


This position is remote within the United States, with regular overlap with Pacific time working hours.


Key Responsibilities

Product Cybersecurity Planning and Deliverables

  • Own the cybersecurity plan and the Product Security Management Plan for assigned products, covering new development, major releases and sustaining changes, in line with our product cybersecurity procedures.
  • Produce the required deliverable set for each product: product security requirements gap analysis, threat model and data flow map, Product Security White Paper, Incident and Vulnerability Management Plan, Patch Management Plan, Cybersecurity Risk Summary Report, and third-party vendor assessments.
  • Decide with the team which deliverables apply to each product, scale them to the product's risk and regulatory status (research-use-only versus IVD), and document every exemption with its justification.
  • Keep the Product Security Management File complete, traceable and ready for FDA inspections and notified-body audits.

Threat Modeling and Risk Assessment

  • Lead STRIDE-based threat modeling sessions with product teams: assets, data flows, trust boundaries, threats, controls, and the risk register entries that result.
  • Assess products against our product security requirements, score findings with CVSS, and work with R&D on remediation or documented risk acceptance.
  • Document unresolved and accepted risks in the Cybersecurity Risk Summary Report that supports release decisions, and feed cybersecurity hazards into the product risk management file where patient safety is affected.

Security Testing, SBOM and Vulnerability Management

  • Run static code analysis and software composition analysis (e.g., Snyk) on product releases, triage findings with engineering, and archive the reports.
  • Generate and validate CycloneDX SBOMs from the actual release artifacts of every software-enabled product, integrate SBOM generation into build and release pipelines, and load SBOMs into our post-market vulnerability monitoring tool (e.g., CyBeats).
  • Monitor post-market vulnerability reports against product SBOMs, assess impact with R&D, and drive remediation within the timelines our procedures set.
  • Coordinate penetration tests with our corporate product security engineering team: define scope from the roadmap, schedule tests early in development and before submissions, evaluate results and assess mitigations.
  • Support investigation of externally reported vulnerabilities and potential cybersecurity complaints together with our corporate cyber risk team.

Patch Management and Secure Baselines

  • Maintain product Patch Management Plans and author or review Security Patch Verification Protocols and Reports.

· Regional Market and Opportunity Development: Build and execute a development plan for the assigned region. Identify priority markets, accounts, projects, partners, and new opportunities across cardiovascular and broader multi-modality CV ASC needs.

· Strategic Account Development: Develop executive relationships with CV ASC owners, operators, health systems, physician groups, private equity sponsors, management service organizations, developers, consultants, architects, and construction partners.

· Commercial Orchestration: Serve as the central development lead for complex CV ASC opportunities and align account executives, product specialists, solution architects, service, finance, applications, project management, and other stakeholders around one customer strategy.

· Ecosystem and Partnership Development: Cultivate relationships with partners that influence CV ASC planning, development, financing, construction, management, and clinical operations.

· Market Intelligence: Monitor outpatient migration, regulatory and reimbursement developments, competitive activity, ownership changes, and new facility development, converting insights into regional commercial actions.

· Business Management and Governance: Maintain account plans, pursuit strategies, pipeline data, forecasts, and activity metrics. Communicate progress, barriers, resource needs, and market insights through regular operating reviews.

· Growth and Commercial Outcomes: Contribute to assigned operating-plan objectives through qualified pipeline generation, opportunity progression, strategic positioning, and support of CV ASC orders and revenue growth.

About Us

At Medius, we believe managing finance should be about strategy, not stress. That same mindset shapes not only the solutions we build, but also the culture we create for our people. We remove complexity, embrace innovation, and give our teams the freedom to focus on what truly matters — whether that’s transforming the future of finance with AI or finding balance to go home on time.

Founded in Sweden in 2001, Medius has grown from a local startup into a global leader in cloud-based spend management solutions. Today, thousands of organizations worldwide trust us to simplify accounts payable and spend management processes. Our journey has been driven by continuous innovation, a passion for technology, and above all — the people who make it happen.

We’re more than a software company. We’re a team of problem-solvers, innovators and collaborators working together to reinvent the category of accounts payable. Our solutions use Artificial Intelligence to eliminate manual work, bring clarity, confidence, and control, and empower finance teams of the future.

At Medius,our values guide how we work and grow together:

  • Connect – We believe in the power of people—individually and collectively—and our success depends on understanding and respecting each other. We appreciate that ‘empowering finance teams of the future’ is an exciting endeavor, and we share it with everyone around us.

  • Question – We enjoy the challenge of our work and the thrill of collaboration. We are not afraid to question ourselves and each other because we believe diverse perspectives can lead to better outcomes and that there is great power in resolution.

  • Own – We are thorough, thoughtful, and decisive. We anticipate what’s next, what a customer might need, and then we deliver. That’s how we get things done. And that’s how we remain a leader. Customers trust us to do our job so that they can focus on what they do best.

At Medius, you’ll join a diverse, global community where curiosity is celebrated, ideas matter, and innovation never stops. If you’re passionate about technology, eager to make an impact, and ready to grow alongside a team that lives its values, Medius is where you can do your best work — your impact is global.

• Collaborate with Marketing, Customer Success, and Product teams to ensure alignment and customer satisfaction.

• Strong understanding of enterprise buying processes, procurement cycles, and contract negotiation. • Excellent executive presence, communication, and presentation skills.

jobs.title: Development Data & Systems Analyst
jobs.excerpt: At The Obama Foundation, our mission is to inspire, empower, and connect people to change their world.
jobs.description:
At The Obama Foundation, our mission is to inspire, empower, and connect people to change their world. We seek to build an active democratic culture where people are equipped and motivated to make change in the communities where they live, work, and play. Right here on the South Side of Chicago, we’re building a home for this vision, a global center for change with a range of opportunities - coordinated programming, community outreach events, educational moments, and more - that invite visitors from down the block or across the globe to turn hope into action.

Achieving our ambitious goals starts with an exceptional team built on our Hope to Action Values - Courage, Empathy, Integrity, Accountability, Community, Inclusivity, Pragmatism, Resilience, Imagination, and Hope. A Framework that anyone, anywhere, can use to build trust, activate participation, and expand opportunity in their community.

Purpose of the Role

Reporting directly to the Manager of Development Data, the Development Data & Systems Analyst is a critical technical role responsible for optimizing, maintaining, and innovating within the Foundation’s Salesforce CRM ecosystem. As the Foundation expands its Principal Gifts function, this role ensures our data architecture, donor recognition tracking, and reporting pipelines run with peak efficiency.

The Analyst serves as the primary technical lead for the Development division's internal data ticketing system, fulfilling custom report requests, troubleshooting user issues, and delivering technical support to frontline fundraisers. Additionally, this role co-designs and tests new Salesforce workflows - specifically for duplicate management, activity tracking, and complex grant reporting - while performing regular database quality control audits. While not a primary gift processor, the Analyst maintains cross-training in gift intake to serve as strategic backup during peak fiscal thresholds and PTO coverage.

Core Job Responsibilities

Division Ticketing Lead & Technical Support

  • Help Desk Management: Take direct ownership of the Development team’s Salesforce ticketing system. Receive, prioritize, triage, and resolve incoming data, reporting, and system access requests from frontline fundraisers and operations staff within established SLAs.
  • Frontline Technical Support & Training: Provide technical guidance and user support across the team. Assist in drafting technical documentation, SOPs, and user guides, co-leading quarterly database training sessions for development analysts and lead onboarding Salesforce training for new Development staff.

Salesforce Systems Optimization & Custom Tracking

  • Recognition & Benefit Tracking: Partner with the Manager to design, build, and enforce standardized Salesforce workflows to accurately track donor naming opportunities, physical/digital recognition, and bespoke benefit fulfillment for OPC and Principal Gift donors.
  • Grants & Gift Reporting Architecture: Build custom tracking frameworks, reports, and dashboards in Salesforce to capture the full lifecycle, financial milestones, and reporting triggers for complex institutional gifts and grants.
  • QA Testing & System Enhancements: Conduct rigorous quality assurance (QA) testing in the Salesforce sandbox environment for new features, bug fixes, third-party integrations, or automation flows that are deployed to production.

Data Hygiene, Auditing & Quality Assurance

  • Data Integrity & Auditing: Execute regular data cleanup initiatives, quality control queries, mass data uploads, and duplicate record merges to maintain a pristine CRM database.
  • Workflow Automation & Documentation: Identify manual, repetitive data entry pain points across the department and recommend automated solutions. Maintain comprehensive, up-to-date documentation of database configurations and data standards.

Cross-Functional & Revenue Backup

  • Gift Processing Backup: Cross-train on all gift processing, lockbox, wire transfer, and batching procedures under the guidance of the Gift Acceptance team, serving as vital cross-functional surge backup during fiscal year-end and peak fundraising cycles.

Key Deliverables / Outcomes

  • Rapid, high-touch resolution of all internal data ticketing requests, maintaining reliable and timely responses to internal stakeholders, in support of strong customer service to donors and prospects
  • Standardized, fully functional Salesforce tracking systems, reports, and dashboards for donor benefits, OPC recognition, and fundraising revenue .
  • Clean, accurate, and regularly audited Salesforce data, ensuring a trusted source of truth for the Development team.
  • Comprehensive, updated user documentation and technical knowledge-base resources for the Development team.

Required Qualifications

  • 1-2 years of hands-on experience in database management, data analytics, or systems administration, specifically within a non-profit development/advancement environment preferred.
  • Proficiency with Salesforce CRM in a non-profit context (Salesforce NPSP or Nonprofit Cloud experience strongly preferred); ability to build complex custom reports, dashboards, and fields.
  • Proven experience managing a data request queue or ticketing help desk system, with a track record of translating complex technical concepts for non-technical frontline staff.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and quality-assurance skills; meticulous attention to detail regarding data accuracy and hygiene.
  • Familiarity with non-profit fundraising mechanics, including major gifts, principal donor recognition, multi-year pledge schedules, and grant tracking.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities, work collaboratively across cross-functional teams, and adapt to a fast-paced, high-growth organizational environment.
  • Commitment to the values and mission of the Foundation.

The salary range for this role is between $51,965 and $64,980.


This is a remote role based in the Chicago area.

GoMedicus Praxen “Built for your purpose” - Wir unterstützen Dich und Dein Team, vor Ort und virtuell bei eurer Mission, Menschen gesünder zu machen – modern, digital, entlastend. Wir halten euch den Rücken frei, damit ihr euch auf die Patienten konzentrieren könnt – eigenständig, ohne Investitionsrisiko, in einem starken Team.

was dich erwartet

✅ Privatärztliche Psychotherapie
·Du übernimmst privatärztliche psychotherapeutische Behandlungen im Rahmen Deiner Facharztrichtung — diagnostische Gespräche, Einzeltherapie, ggf. Krisenintervention.
·Du arbeitest ausschließlich privatärztlich — kein KV-Sitz, keine Kontingente, kein Gutachterverfahren.
·Du entscheidest selbst über Sitzungslänge, Frequenz und Behandlungsplan.

✅ Remote von Beginn an
·Deine Sprechzeiten kannst Du von Beginn an vollständig remote gestalten — privatärztliche Psychotherapie eignet sich hervorragend für digitale Formate.
·Du arbeitest mit unserem eigenen digitalen Stack, entwickelt für rechtssichere und dokumentationsleichte Video-Sprechstunden.
·Vor-Ort-Tätigkeit am Kronprinzenbau in Reutlingen ist möglich, wenn Du das Setting schätzt — aber keine Voraussetzung.

✅ Setup & Ramp-up
·Du startest mit ~20 h/Woche und wächst mit dem Patientenaufkommen. Ausbau auf mehr Stunden ist jederzeit möglich, wenn Du es willst.
·Du bekommst ein Team, das Dir Terminierung, Abrechnung und administrative Aufgaben abnimmt — damit Du Dich auf Deine Patienten konzentrieren kannst.
·Unsere KI-Tools übernehmen einen Großteil der Dokumentationsarbeit, sodass Du deutlich mehr Zeit für Deine Patienten hast.

✅ Standard-Psychotherapie — Spezialisierung willkommen
·Du deckst das übliche Spektrum ambulanter Psychotherapie ab — kein Fokus auf einzelne Störungsbilder nötig.
·Falls Du einen Schwerpunkt mitbringst (z.B. Traumatherapie, Verhaltenstherapie, Paartherapie, DBT, Burnout) — sehr willkommen. Wir bauen das gerne mit Dir gemeinsam als Angebot aus.

was solltest du mitbringen?

✔Facharzt für Psychiatrie und Psychotherapie, Facharzt für Psychosomatische Medizin und Psychotherapie oder anderer Facharzt mit Zusatzbezeichnung Psychotherapie (deutsche Approbation, Fachkunde vollständig anerkannt)
✔Empathie, Reflexionsfähigkeit und ein echtes Interesse an Deinen Patienten
✔Offenheit für digitale Sprechstunden und moderne Praxis-IT
✔Selbstständige Arbeitsweise und Freude an einer neu aufgebauten Praxisstruktur
✔Deutsch fließend — Englisch von Vorteil (über MedKitDoc versorgen wir zunehmend auch internationale Patienten)
✔Berufserfahrung ist willkommen, aber nicht Voraussetzung — auch als Berufseinsteigerin nach der Facharztprüfung bist Du bei uns richtig

benefits

    • Finanzielle Unterstützung bei einem Umzug.

    • Benefits, die zu Deiner Lebenssituation passen – z. B. Zuschuss zum Fitnessstudio oder zum Kindergarten.

Description

The Senior Transformation Program Lead will lead the North America Billing transformation; a critical multi-year initiative focused on modernizing billing capabilities through the implementation of the Majesco platform.

This role serves as the Overall Program Lead (OPL), bringing together business, technology, operations, and delivery partners around a unified transformation roadmap and ensuring the program is positioned to deliver its intended business outcomes. The OPL will provide end-to-end leadership across the transformation, creating clarity across a complex portfolio of work, connecting interdependencies, enabling timely decisions, and ensuring leaders and teams remain aligned on priorities, outcomes, risks, and execution.

Success in this role requires a leader who can operate equally effectively at the executive and delivery levels. The OPL will partner closely with senior business and technology leaders, product and engineering teams, functional experts, and external partners to translate strategy into an executable roadmap and drive disciplined execution across a large, complex transformation.

Ultimately, the Senior Transformation Program Lead is accountable for connecting strategy to execution and creating a culture of execution excellence across the transformation. This leader will establish the operating discipline, accountability, transparency, and ways of working that enable a complex, multi-year program to perform at its best. They will set the tone for how teams work together, how decisions are made, how challenges are surfaced and resolved, and how the organization continuously learns and adapts to deliver meaningful and sustainable business value.

What You’ll Own

About Celldex

Celldex is pioneering new horizons in immunology to deliver life-changing therapies. We are relentless in our pursuit of novel antibody-based treatments that engage the human immune system and directly affect critical pathways to improve the lives of patients with allergic, inflammatory and autoimmune disorders. We have built a culture where innovative and talented people thrive—focusing a significant effort on attracting and retaining passionate and motivated employees who want to play a role in helping people with serious health conditions and who see this effort as personally rewarding. In our highly entrepreneurial environment, employees are empowered and the opportunity for professional development occurs every day.

Celldex is now entering an exciting new chapter – building a commercial team to launch barzolvolimab - the most advanced anti-KIT therapy in pivotal development that has the potential to redefine treatment for multiple allergy and dermatological diseases with Phase 3 studies in CSU, ColdU, SD and phase 2 studies in AD. We’re looking for curious, driven builders who can connect their day-to-day work to enterprise-level impact, endlessly prioritize what matters most, and deliver on their commitments with urgency and ownership. If you’re energized by building something meaningful, excited to grow personally and professionally, and motivated to create lasting impact in a fast-moving, entrepreneurial environment, we’d love to meet you.

Ready to make an impact? Learn more about joining the Celldex Team today!

Overview

Celldex is seeking an accomplished market access leader to serve as Executive Director, National and Key Accounts, reporting to the Vice President, Managed Markets. This individual will lead the national and regional payer account organization responsible for securing and optimizing access for barzolvolimab, Celldex's investigational therapy in development for chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU), subject to regulatory approval. The Executive Director will translate the market access strategy into disciplined account execution across national and regional health plans, pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs), integrated delivery networks, Group Purchasing Organizations (GPOs), government channels, and other priority customers.

The role requires exceptional leadership capabilities, deep market access expertise, and the ability to effectively represent account team insights, customer needs, reimbursement challenges, and market opportunities to Celldex Executive Leadership while ensuring alignment with the company's overall strategic direction. The successful candidate will build and lead a high-performing team of National Account Managers, Regional Account Managers, and Key Account Managers, establish clear performance expectations, guide complex access and contracting negotiations, and ensure launch readiness and post-launch execution. This role requires deep payer expertise, strong command of medical-benefit and buy-and-bill dynamics, sound judgment, and the ability to influence senior internal and external stakeholders.

Responsibilities

  • Lead, coach, and hold accountable the National Account Manager and Regional Account Manager teams responsible for payer access and account execution for barzolvolimab.
  • Develop and execute the national and regional account strategy plan in alignment with Celldex's overall market access, pricing, contracting, distribution, and commercial strategies.
  • Establish account segmentation, prioritization, call planning, objectives, milestones, performance standards, and operating rhythms across the payer account organization.
  • Ensure account strategies align with Celldex's overall commercial, market access, and corporate objectives.
  • Direct engagement with national and regional health plans, PBMs, specialty pharmacies, integrated delivery networks, government accounts, and other strategic customers, as appropriate.
  • Lead and support complex product access and contract negotiations, including medical-benefit and buy-and-bill arrangements, while protecting long-term product value and adhering to approved governance.
  • Ensure the team communicates a compelling, compliant clinical and economic value proposition to payer and population-health decision-makers.
  • Anticipate payer policy, utilization-management, reimbursement, and competitive barriers; develop account-specific strategies to improve timely and appropriate patient access.
  • Partner closely with Market Access Strategy, Pricing and Contracting, Trade and Distribution, HEOR, Medical Affairs, Marketing, Sales, Finance, Legal, Compliance, and Patient Services.
  • Provide high-quality account intelligence, access forecasts, policy updates, contracting insights, and risk assessments to senior leadership and cross-functional launch teams.
  • Build launch-readiness capabilities, tools, dashboards, and key performance indicators; monitor execution and take corrective action when performance is below expectations.
  • Recruit, onboard, develop, retain, and succession-plan a diverse team of market access professionals; foster a culture of ownership, transparency, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Manage the function's budget and external resources responsibly and ensure all activities comply with company policies and applicable laws and regulations.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree in business, healthcare, pharmacy, public health, or a related discipline preferred.
  • Minimum of 15 years of pharmaceutical, biotechnology, managed markets, healthcare account management, or related commercial experience.
  • Minimum of 8-10 years of progressive leadership experience, including responsibility for leading national account management, market access, or customer-facing organizations.
  • Demonstrated success leading Payer Account Directors, National Account Managers, Regional Account Managers, or comparable customer-facing market access teams.
  • Substantial experience negotiating product access and contracts involving medical-benefit, specialty, infused/injected, or buy-and-bill products.
  • Deep understanding of payer decision-making, formulary and medical-policy processes, utilization management, specialty pharmacy, reimbursement, distribution, and provider economics.
  • Proven ability to lead teams through pre-launch planning, launch execution, and evolving market conditions with clear goals and measurable accountability.
  • Strong executive presence, negotiation skills, business judgment, financial acumen, and ability to communicate complex issues clearly to senior leaders and customers.
  • Exceptional leadership, coaching, organizational development, and talent management capabilities.
  • Track record of effective cross-functional leadership in a matrixed, fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.
  • Ability to travel up to 60%, including overnight travel, based on business needs.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in immunology, allergy, dermatology, rare disease, or other specialty markets with complex payer and provider access dynamics.
  • Experience building or expanding a payer account organization for a first or early commercial launch.
  • Knowledge of government pricing, contracting governance, gross-to-net considerations, and the compliance requirements applicable to payer engagement.
  • Established credibility and relationships with senior payer, PBM, and organized-customer decision-makers.

Leadership Capabilities

  • Enterprise leadership: Connects account decisions to Celldex's broader clinical, commercial, financial, and patient-access objectives.
  • Performance leadership: Sets unambiguous expectations, uses data to assess performance, gives direct feedback, and follows through on commitments.
  • Strategic negotiation: Balances access, value, affordability, customer priorities, and long-term product economics.
  • Team development: Builds capability, empowers sound decision-making, and creates strong succession and talent pipelines.
  • Collaboration and influence: Aligns stakeholders without relying solely on authority and constructively challenges assumptions.
  • Strong executive presence with demonstrated ability to communicate complex business issues, customer insights, organizational needs, and strategic recommendations to executive leadership teams.

With BlinkRx, never again will a patient show up at the pharmacy only to discover that they can’t afford their medication, their doctor needs to fill out a form for them, or the pharmacy doesn’t have the medication in stock.

Patient Care

Prescriber Collaboration and Clinical Outreach

Cross-Functional Collaboration

jobs.description:
Purpose 

Delta Faucet Company is seeking a Salesforce Solution Architect to serve as the design authority for our Salesforce ecosystem within the Channel, Experience & Portfolio function of IT. This is a customer-side architecture role — you will partner closely with business leaders to shape the platform according to our roadmap, own how it evolves over multiple years, and guide its direction beyond how any single project is coded. 


Our environment spans B2B, B2C and B2B2C: wholesale distributors, trade professionals, retail partners, e-commerce and direct consumer service, supported by Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, Marketing Cloud, Data Cloud and CPQ/Revenue Cloud, integrated to ERP, PIM/DAM and analytics platforms. You will act as trusted advisor to business partners, set the architectural direction, and hold internal and third-party delivery teams accountable to that direction. 


You will succeed here if you enjoy owning the long-term integrity of a platform inside the company that runs it.


What Success Looks Like in Year One 

  • Within 90 days: You have documented the current-state Salesforce architecture, data model and integration landscape, and identified the top technical-debt risks with a remediation point of view. 
  • Within 6 months: You are the recognized design authority on all Channel & Experience initiatives — no significant design decision, internal or vendor-proposed, moves forward without your review. 
  • Within 12 months: A published multi-year platform architecture roadmap is in place and aligned to enterprise architecture standards; measurable reduction in custom code and rework on delivered releases; business partners come to you early, not after requirements are frozen. 

Key Responsibilities and Duties 

  • Design Authority: Own end-to-end solution design across multiple Salesforce Clouds — object and data model, security and sharing, automation strategy, and integration patterns — balancing near-term delivery against long-term maintainability. 
  • Roadmap Ownership: Translate business strategy into a multi-year platform architecture roadmap; recommend build vs. buy vs. configure, and sequence capability delivery accordingly. 
  • Stakeholder Engagement: Act as trusted advisor to Sales, Marketing, Customer Solutions and channel partners; challenge requirements constructively and translate them into technical specifications. 
  • Technical Leadership: Guide internal and partner development teams on best practices, data modeling, automation and API integration; lead design reviews rather than perform hands-on build. 
  • Vendor Governance: Provide architectural oversight of third-party delivery partners and systems integrators — validate that proposed solutions leverage out-of-the-box functionality wherever possible, and hold external partners accountable to industry best practices, security protocols and our standards. 
  • Documentation & Governance: Maintain architecture artifacts and decision records; establish and enforce standards that minimize technical debt. 
  • Emerging Capability: Evaluate new platform capability — including Data Cloud, generative and agentic AI such as Agentforce — and form a defensible point of view on where it creates value while protecting brand, privacy and governance standards. 
  • Validation: Use prototypes and proof-of-concepts, built personally or directed through the team, to de-risk significant design decisions. 

Required Experience and Skills 

  • Experience: 8+ years working with the Salesforce platform, including 2+ years as the accountable architect on at least two full-lifecycle, multi-cloud implementations. 
  • Multi-Cloud Design Depth: Demonstrated design ownership across at least three of: Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, Marketing Cloud, Data Cloud, CPQ/Revenue Cloud. 
  • Core Platform Knowledge: Deep command of data modeling, security and sharing architecture, declarative automation strategy, Lightning Experience and integration patterns (REST/SOAP, event-driven, middleware). 
  • Technical Fluency: Sufficient depth in Cross-cloud integration, Apex, LWC and API development to review, challenge and govern the work of developers — hands-on coding is not the primary function of this role. 
  • Governance Judgment: Track record of saying no to unnecessary customization and defending that position with business stakeholders and vendors. 
  • Strategic Thinking: Ability to design solutions that align to long-term business goals and enterprise architecture standards. 
  • Communication: Excellent written and verbal skills, with a proven ability to translate technical concepts for non-technical and executive audiences. 
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience. 
  • Autonomy: Executes responsibilities with limited oversight required. 

Preferred Experience 

  • Experience as an in-house Salesforce architect at a customer organization or consulting experience in a long-term client engagement.
  • B2B, B2C or B2B2C commerce with distributor, dealer or trade-professional channel models. 
  • Manufacturing or consumer products industry background. 
  • Experience governing a systems integrator or managed-service partner, including reviewing SOW-driven deliverables. 
  • Practical exposure to generative or agentic AI on the Salesforce platform, including Agentforce, Einstein or Data Cloud-driven use cases. This is valued and will be developed on the job — it is not a screening requirement. 
  • Experience integrating Salesforce with ERP, PIM/DAM or enterprise analytics platforms. 

Certifications 

Architect-track certification preferred, not required. Demonstrated design ownership will always outweigh credentials. 

  • Preferred: Salesforce Certified Application Architect, System Architect, or B2B/B2C Solution Architect. 
  • Commonly held: Salesforce Administrator, Advanced Administrator, Platform App Builder, Platform Developer I. 

Why Delta Faucet Company 

Delta Faucet Company is one of the largest and most recognized brands in kitchen and bath plumbing fixtures, and part of Masco Corporation. Our Salesforce footprint is expanding rapidly across sales, marketing and customer service, with a multi-year investment roadmap already funded. This role carries real design authority from day one and a direct line to IT and business leadership — the scope of an enterprise architect with the influence of a small team. 

Diversity & Inclusion 

At Delta Faucet Company, we view diversity as a mosaic of thoughts and perspectives that come from people’s varied cultural backgrounds, experiences, education, career paths and other influences that make each of us unique. For us, inclusion means welcoming differing opinions, collaborating, allowing people to come to work as who they are and recognizing everyone’s contributions. We know that in a diverse, inclusive company, ideas flow freely, all voices are heard and all perspectives are valued. Delta Faucet Company continuously strives to be this kind of organization. Diversity and Inclusion (D&I) supports our inherent values, makes us more relevant to customers and consumers and inspires innovation. It is not a goal or a program; it is a vital ingredient in our formula for success and a key to our future growth.

It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!

We're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business.

The PCB Layout & Design for Manufacturing (DFM) Engineer is a highly visible technical role within Creation Technologies, responsible for driving excellence in printed circuit board design, manufacturability, and production readiness across the organization. This position serves as a key subject matter expert for complex PCB layout, Valor DFM, Design for Assembly, and PCB fabrication and assembly processes.

Working from electrical schematics and engineering requirements, the engineer will develop and support complex, high density, multilayer PCB designs while ensuring electrical, mechanical, reliability, and manufacturing requirements are incorporated from the earliest stages of development. Beyond individual designs, this role will help shape how Creation approaches PCB design and manufacturing by developing DFM methodologies, integrating manufacturing design rules, establishing PCB design standards, and driving continuous improvement across engineering and manufacturing teams.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced PCB design professional who enjoys both hands on technical work and the opportunity to influence standards, processes, and best practices across a global electronics manufacturing organization.

The position offers flexibility to be remote, with a strong preference for candidates located in the Denver, Colorado area to support collaboration with key Creation Technologies teams and facilities.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include, but not limited to:

DFM Analysis on Circuit Card Assemblies (~75% of time)

  • Lead Design for Manufacturability (DFM), Design for Assembly (DFA) assessments for printed circuit board assemblies.
  • Utilize Siemens Valor NPI and / or related tools to perform automated manufacturability analysis on customer and internally developed PCB designs.
  • Develop, maintain, and continuously improve DFM rule sets aligned with IPC standards, fabrication capabilities, assembly processes, and customer requirements.
  • Review Gerber, ODB++, BOM, centroid, assembly drawing, and fabrication data packages for completeness and manufacturability.
  • Lead DFM review meetings with manufacturing, process engineering, quality, and customers to resolve design and process concerns.
  • Prepare DFM reports, technical presentations, and executive summaries to communicate findings and recommendations.
  • Stay informed on emerging technologies, tools, and standards to strengthen product performance and maintain industry leadership.
  • Other duties and responsibilities as assigned

PCB Layout & Design (~25% of time)

  • Develop complex multilayer PCB layouts from engineer-approved schematics using industry-standard PCB design tools such as Altium Designer, Cadence Allegro, or equivalent.
  • Create PCB stack-ups, placement strategies, routing topologies, and design constraints that satisfy signal integrity, power integrity, thermal, mechanical, and manufacturing requirements.
  • Collaborate with electrical and mechanical engineers to ensure successful implementation of design intent while optimizing manufacturability and cost.

jobs.excerpt: Company OverviewNCS is a leading industrial products, services and technology company whose primary end-market is car wash operators.
jobs.description:
Company Overview

NCS is a leading industrial products, services and technology company whose primary end-market is car wash operators. NCS provides a full suite of manufactured equipment, installation project services, aftermarket parts and services, chemicals (detergents, protectants, etc.), and software. More specifically with equipment, NCS provides tunnel equipment, IBA (In Bay Automatic), vacuums, dryers, water systems, doors, signage, arches, and related components. NCS also sells a range of brands – on both equipment, chemicals and software today – including Armor All, Rain-X, Blue Coral, TSS, VacuTech, NCS, AMP, etc. The company sells primarily in N. America, operates 6 manufacturing plants across N. America, and has ~1600+ employees. The Company operates numerous Distribution Centers and has sales/HQ offices across N. America, with its primary corporate offices in Des Moines, Iowa and Dallas, TX. NCS is currently owned by Berkshire Partners, a leading Boston-based PE firm

We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not currently able to sponsor work visas.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Cyber Security Cloud Engineer is the hands-on engineer responsible for implementing, operating, and maturing security controls across NCS's cloud environment, including Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services, and the enterprise SaaS platforms that run the business. NCS operates within an established set of NIST-based enterprise security requirements that define the controls, reporting cadences, and audit expectations for the business. This role implements the security controls that protect our cloud, SaaS, identity, workload, and data environments, and serves as the security lead for integrating newly acquired companies into the NCS security framework. As NCS invests in AI to transform how we serve customers and run the business, this engineer ensures those initiatives are deployed with the required safeguards in place. The engineer also partners with Product Engineering and DevOps teams to put required security controls into practice across the software development lifecycle for NCS products, connected equipment, and customer-facing platforms. The role works closely with Infrastructure, Networking, Data, Application Development, and business stakeholders, and provides security leadership with clear visibility into control status, gaps, and remediation progress. Success in this role means delivering required controls on schedule, demonstrating their effectiveness, and reducing enterprise risk without slowing the business.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Cloud Security Implementation & Operations

  • Implement and maintain security controls across Azure and AWS in accordance with NCS security requirements and the enterprise security framework, including identity and access management, network segmentation, encryption and key management, logging, and workload protection.
  • Deploy and operate cloud security posture management (CSPM/CNAPP), infrastructure-as-code guardrails, policy-as-code, and automated compliance checks that enforce required baselines and provide continuous evidence of control effectiveness.
  • Operate and tune cloud-native security services (e.g., Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Microsoft Sentinel, Entra ID Protection, AWS GuardDuty, Security Hub, CloudTrail, IAM Access Analyzer) and integrate cloud telemetry into enterprise SIEM detection and response workflows.
  • Execute detection engineering and incident response for cloud-hosted and identity-centric threats, including alert triage, investigation, root cause analysis, containment, and remediation coordination with managed security providers, following established playbooks and escalation paths; track emerging cloud attack techniques and recommend updates to detections, hardening, and response procedures.

Acquisition Integration & Migration

  • Support cybersecurity due diligence for acquisitions by executing technical assessments of target environments and documenting gaps against NCS security requirements to inform prioritized integration plans.
  • Execute the secure integration and migration of acquired companies onto NCS platforms, including identity consolidation into Microsoft Entra ID, tenant-to-tenant Microsoft 365 migrations, workload migrations to Azure and AWS, network and endpoint onboarding, and decommissioning of legacy infrastructure.
  • Maintain and follow repeatable, documented integration playbooks and security baselines that bring acquired entities to the required security standard within defined integration timelines, with status reporting throughout.

DevOps & Product Security

  • Implement and operate required security controls across the CI/CD pipeline in partnership with Product Engineering and DevOps teams, including static and dynamic application security testing (SAST/DAST), software composition analysis, secrets scanning, container image scanning, and software bill of materials (SBOM) generation, with risk-based gates that protect release velocity.
  • Support secure product development for NCS software, connected equipment, and customer-facing platforms through threat modeling, secure design reviews, application of secure coding standards, API security, and vulnerability management, with particular attention to payment-enabled and field-deployed systems.
  • Track product security metrics, maintain developer-facing documentation, and uphold remediation SLAs that give engineering teams clear, actionable ownership of security findings.

Compliance, Reporting & Leadership

  • Implement the data protection, DLP, identity governance, and access controls required to securely enable approved AI initiatives, including Microsoft 365 Copilot, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, and enterprise AI tooling, in partnership with Data, IT, and business teams.
  • Maintain security controls across Microsoft 365, identity, endpoint (Windows and Apple), and cloud platforms in line with NCS security requirements; produce the evidence, metrics, and documentation needed for PCI-DSS compliance, NIST CSF alignment, internal and external audits, executive security reviews, and customer security assessments.
  • Mentor engineers, serve as the escalation point for complex cloud and identity security issues, and report clearly on control status, gaps, risk, and remediation progress to technical and executive audiences.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5 or more years of progressive experience in IT, with broad exposure to infrastructure, networking, identity, and enterprise systems.
  • 3 or more years of hands-on experience in a dedicated cybersecurity role, including securing production workloads in Microsoft Azure and/or AWS.
  • Demonstrated experience implementing security controls within an established enterprise security framework, including translating defined control requirements, audit findings, and assessment results into deployed, documented, and measurable controls.
  • Hands-on implementation experience with cloud security services and patterns on at least one major platform (Azure or AWS) and solid familiarity with the other, including IAM, network security, encryption and key management, logging, and workload protection.
  • Experience with infrastructure as code (e.g., Terraform, Bicep, CloudFormation), CI/CD platforms (e.g., Azure DevOps, GitHub, GitLab), and application security tooling (SAST/DAST, SCA, secrets and container scanning), with a track record of partnering with development teams to embed security into the SDLC.
  • Working knowledge of the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and experience supporting PCI-DSS compliance and audit or assessment processes, including evidence collection and remediation tracking.
  • Clear, professional written and verbal communication, with the ability to report control status, gaps, and remediation progress to technical and non-technical audiences.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • One or more current, industry-recognized security certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, AWS Certified Security – Specialty, or Microsoft Certified: Azure Security Engineer Associate (AZ-500); equivalent demonstrated experience will be considered.
  • Direct experience executing security workstreams for mergers, acquisitions, or divestitures, including tenant-to-tenant migrations and identity consolidation.
  • Experience securing AI/ML platforms and services (Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Microsoft 365 Copilot, enterprise data platforms) and familiarity with the NIST AI RMF, OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, or similar frameworks.
  • Experience with CSPM/CNAPP platforms, container and Kubernetes security, and secrets management.
  • Experience implementing or maturing a product or application security program, including familiarity with OWASP ASVS and SAMM, NIST SSDF, or similar secure development frameworks, and tooling such as GitHub Advanced Security or equivalent integrated DevSecOps platforms.
  • Experience securing embedded, IoT, or payment-enabled products, including PCI-DSS considerations for software and device design.

A Sr. Principal Analyst uses research and analytical skills to create thought-leading insights that help Sourcing, Procurement and Vendor Management and other IT leaders navigate software and cloud pricing and contracting. As a Gartner analyst, you will meet daily with senior-level clients to help them achieve their most critical priorities, driving performance and business outcomes. Candidates must have current knowledge of Microsoft’s commercial programs, contracting models, pricing, and discounting approaches as well as a vision for how Microsoft licensing, and overall contracting and negotiations with large vendors, will evolve globally and regionally.

What you’ll do:

  • Provide clients and prospects with compelling, actionable advice regarding their Microsoft pricing and contracting needs, including negotiation strategies and ongoing vendor management, via virtual or face-to-face interactions.

Gartner analysts are viewed as the experts. This means you need to know your markets, vendors, trends, management practices, etc. and be able to see the forest and the trees. You should have:

  • Self-motivated, collaborative, quick-learning, and comfortable working in a multicultural, matrixed environment.
  • Able to conduct occasional travel (usually no more than 25%), regionally and globally.

At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world.

Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission-critical priorities.

Since our founding in 1979, we’ve grown to 20,000 associates globally who support over 13,000 client enterprises in ~90 countries and territories. We do important, interesting and substantive work that matters. That’s why we hire associates with the intellectual curiosity, energy and drive to want to make a difference. The bar is unapologetically high. So is the impact you can have here.

What makes Gartner a great place to work?

Our vast, virtually untapped market potential offers limitless opportunities – opportunities that may not even exist right now – for you to grow professionally and flourish personally. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance.

We hire remarkable people who collaborate and win as a team. Together, our singular, unifying goal is to deliver results for our clients.

Our teams are inclusive and composed of individuals from different geographies, cultures, religions, ethnicities, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities and generations.

We invest in great leaders who bring out the best in you and the company, enabling us to multiply our impact and results. This is why, year after year, we are recognized worldwide as a great place to work.

Gartner is the world authority on AI

At Gartner, you’ll join a company at the very center of the AI revolution. Gartner has proactive, objective guidance throughout clients’ AI journeys. We set the standard for how organizations leverage artificial intelligence to drive meaningful impact. You’ll have access to unmatched resources, expertise, and technology, and play a key role in helping Gartner and our clients innovate and grow as we leverage AI to transform business and technology landscapes.

It’s an exciting time to be at Gartner, with limitless opportunities to make a real impact, grow your skills, and build a lasting, meaningful career in a field that’s reshaping the way we operate. If you’re passionate about AI and want to be part of a team that’s guiding the leaders who shape the world, Gartner is the place for you.

What do we offer?

Gartner offers world-class benefits, highly competitive compensation and disproportionate rewards for top performers.

In our hybrid work environment, we provide the flexibility and support for you to thrive — working virtually when it's productive to do so and getting together with colleagues in a vibrant community that is purposeful, engaging and inspiring.

Ready to grow your career with Gartner? Join us.
